Regulations for Performance and Safety Standards of Motor Vehicle and Vehicle
- KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle Safety Standards)
MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

CHAPTER 1 GENERAL

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of the Regulations (hereinafter the "Regulation") is to establish the
safety standards and self-certification standards for vehicles applicable to the structures and systems
of motor vehicles and motorcycles, and the standards and methods applicable to the safety and the
Safety Compliance Test of vehicles, their parts or systems pursuant to Article 29 Paragraph 3 and
Paragraph 4, Article 29-3 Paragraph 1 and Paragraph 4, Article 30 Paragraph 1, Article 32 Paragraph
1 and Article 50 Paragraph 2 of the Motor Vehicle Management Act (MVMA) and Article 8 and
Article 8-2 of the Enforcement Ordinance of the same Act.

Article 2 (Definitions) The definitions of the terms used in this regulation are as follows:
1. "Unloaded state" means the state of a vehicle without any occupant seated, without cargo
(including spare parts, tools or other carrying material), with maximum capacity of engine fuel,
coolant and oil, with spare wheels (for vehicles equipped with spare wheel(s)), and operable.
2. "Loaded state" means the state of a vehicle loaded with occupants of the designated seating
capacity and the loads of maximum loading capacity in a vehicle of the unloaded state. In this
case, the weight of a person (1.5 children under the age of 13 to be calculated as one person)
shall be calculated as 65 kg, and the occupants shall be seated in the designated seating positions
(or standing passengers shall be positioned evenly) and the luggage shall be evenly loaded at the
luggage area.
3. "Axle load" means the sum of weights loaded on wheels comprising an axle of a vehicle in a
level state.
4. "Wheel load" means the weight applied to the ground by a wheel of a vehicle in a level state.
5. "Center line of a vehicle" means a straight longitudinal line connecting the center of a frontmost
axle (or a center of a tire-ground interface of a front wheel for a 3-wheeled vehicle for which a
front axle is not available) and the center of a rearmost axle of a vehicle on the three-dimensional
reference system [referring to a coordinate system which consists of the x-axis (front '-', rear '+'),
y-axis (right '-', left '+'), and z-axis (lower '-', upper '+') in a level state with wheels in the straight-
ahead position, as shown in Table 1; hereinafter the same shall apply], or a straight line
connecting the centers of tire-ground interfaces of a front wheel and a rear wheel for a
motorcycle (excluding a riding facility attached to its side if available).
5-2. "Vertical longitudinal plane" means the plane (x-z) including the x-axis and z-axis in the three-
dimensional reference system.
5-3. "Vertical transverse plane" means the plane (y-z) including the y-axis and z-axis in the three-
dimensional reference system.
5-4. "Horizontal plane" means the plane (x-y) including x-axis and y-axis in the three-dimensional
reference system.
6. "Curb weight" means the weight of a vehicle in the unloaded state. In the case of an incomplete
vehicle, it means the weight of a vehicle proposed by the incomplete vehicle manufacturer for
its application to the safety/performance of the vehicle.
7. "Gross vehicle weight" means the weight of a vehicle in the loaded state. In the case of
incomplete vehicle, it means the maximum permissible GVW that the manufacturer of phased-
manufactured vehicle can apply, as proposed by the incomplete vehicle manufacturer

8. "Full-trailer" means a trailer of which the weight of the trailer and most of the load are supported
by its axles.
8-2. "Low-bed trailer" means a towed vehicle of a semi-trailer structure, and the majority of the
deck is not higher than 1,100 mm and lower than the upper part of a coupler of a trailer.
8-3. "Semi-trailer" means a trailer so constructed that a part of it rests upon a towing vehicle, and
the substantial weight of it and its cargo are also distributed to the towing vehicle.
8-4. "Center axle trailer" means a trailer having 1 axle or more whose center of load with cargo
evenly loaded is near the front of the center of the axle, and the link device with the trailer is not
articulated vertically, and load less than 10% of the GVW or 1,000 kg is taken by the towing
vehicle.
8-5. "Module trailer" means a towed vehicle operating stand alone or in combination with two
trailers or more and having a system which enables even distribution of load.
9. "Tow vehicle-trailer" means a vehicle where a tow vehicle and a trailer are linked together.
10. "Tire-ground interface" means an area of a tire in contact with the ground inflated to its rated
pressure.
11. "Steering ratio" means a ratio of the turning angle of a steering wheel to the steered angle of a
steered wheel.12. (Deleted)
13. "Designated seating capacity" means the number of designated seating positions (including a
driver's seating position) provided.
14. "Maximum loading capacity" means the value of the maximum permissible load.
14-2. "Common space" means an area on which two or more telltales, identification symbols, or
other messages may be displayed but not simultaneously, among areas on which a hand-operated
control or a telltale of indicator is displayed.
15. "Effective luminous area" means an area of the lens excluding the area of the reflex reflector
and mounting hole bosses.
16. "Devices for indirect vision" means devices intended to give a clear view of the rear, side, or
front of the vehicle within the fields of vision, using conventional mirrors, camera-monitors, etc.
16-2. "Camera-monitor system (CMS)" means a device for indirect vision, where the field of vision
is obtained by means of a camera-monitor combination.
17. "Steering column" means a structural housing that surrounds a steering shaft.
18. "Steering shaft" means a component that transmits steering torque from the steering wheel to
the steering gear.
19. "Head impact area" means all nonglazed surfaces of the interior of a vehicle that are statically
contactable by a 165mm diameter spherical head form of a measuring device having a pivot
point to "top-of-head" dimension infinitely adjustable from 736 mm (or 600 mm for a seat back
test pursuant to Article 98) to 838 mm at the seating reference point and at a point 127 mm (or
frontmost position if adjustment range is less than 127 mm) horizontally forward of the seating
reference point and 19 mm vertically above the seating reference point for seats that are
adjustable fore and aft, or at the seating reference point for seats that are not adjustable fore and
aft.
20. "Seating reference point (SgRP)" means the unique design H-point which simulates the position
of the pivot center of the human torso and thigh or its equivalent normal design position
designated by the person who has registered pursuant to Article 30 Paragraph 2 of the MVMA
(hereinafter "manufacturer, etc."), with a dummy positioned in the seating position (with the seat
in its rearmost adjustment position for seats that are adjustable fore and aft, and in its lowermost
adjustment position for seats that are adjustable up and down, and with a seat back adjusted to

21. "Pelvic impact area" means the area of the door or body side panel which is bounded by
horizontal planes 178 mm above and 102 mm below the seating reference point and vertical
transverse planes 204 mm forward and 51 mm rearward of the seating reference point.
22. (Deleted)
23. "Forward control vehicle" means a motor vehicle in which the steering wheel hub is in the
forward quarter of the vehicle length.
23-2. "front-seating vehicle" refers to a vehicle falling under any one of the following Items.
A. In the following figure, in the case where the acute angle (α) between the horizontal plane
that includes the centerline of the front axle of the vehicle and the plane that includes the
centerline of the front axle and the seating reference point (R-point) of the driver's seat is 22

B. In the following figure, in the case where the ratio of the distance (L2) from the vertical plane

24. "Child seat anchorage" means the attachment hardware provided on the body or seat of a
vehicle to which a child seat is secured using anchorages.
25. "Anti-lock brake system" means a portion of a service brake system that senses and analyzes
the rate of angular rotation of the wheels and automatically controls the degree of rotational
wheel slip during braking.
25-2. "Service brake system" means a brake system mainly used while driving.
25-3. "Secondary brake system" means a brake system used by a driver to halt the vehicle in the
event of a failure of one of the subsystems of the service brake system.
25-4. "Automatically controlled braking" means braking created by an electronic brake control
system to decelerate a vehicle irrespective of the driver's control of the brake system.
25-5. "Selective braking" means braking that changes the posture of a motor vehicle by operating
the braking system on each wheel created by an electronic vehicle attitude control system,
irrespective of the driver's control of the brake system.
25-6. "Emergency stop lamp system" means a signal to indicate to other road users to the rear of
the vehicle that a high retardation force has been applied to the vehicle relative to the prevailing
road conditions.
25-7. "Electronic Stability Control System" or "ESC System" means a system that improves vehicle
directional stability by controlling brake pressure of each wheel and engine power, etc.,
automatically.
25-8. "Brake Assist System (BAS)" means a function of the braking system that detects an
emergency braking event from a characteristic of the driver's brake demand, and that assists the

26. "Compressed natural gas" (hereinafter "CNG") means a motor fuel as a mixture of hydrocarbon
gas and vapor in which methane is available mainly in the form of gas.
27. "CNG fuel container" means a container designed to store CNG as motor fuel onboard a motor
vehicle.
28. "CNG fuel system" means all components used to store or supply CNG to a vehicle's engine.
29. (Deleted)30. (Deleted)
31. "High pressure portion of a CNG fuel system" means all the components from and including
each CNG fuel container up to, but not including, the first pressure regulator.
32. "Bus for transportation of children" means a school bus for children pursuant to Article 2
Subparagraph 23 of the Road Traffic Act (excluding motor vehicles for transport service
operated for children as passengers under a restricted license for passenger transport service
issued in accordance with Article 4 Paragraph 3 of the Passenger Transport Service Act) and
means motor vehicles pursuant to Article 34 of the Enforcement Regulations of the Road Traffic
Act.
33. "Hybrid vehicle" means each hybrid vehicle pursuant to Article 2 Subparagraph 5 of the Act
on Promotion for Development and Supply of Environmentally Friendly Vehicles.
34. "Large-sized double-deck bus" means each large-sized bus which has an upper deck in the
occupant compartment partially or wholly which is provided not for standing.
35. "Articulated bus" means a vehicle linked by an independent towing vehicle and towed vehicle(s)
allowing free movement of passengers in between, and their connecting mechanism is designed
to be hard to separate.36. (Deleted)
37. "Auxiliary braking system" means a braking system to reduce the load of the main braking
system, having the capability to provide and to maintain a braking effect over a long period of
time, such as a retarder or exhaust braking system. However, in case of a micro PC (hereinafter
"micro PC"), a micro truck (hereinafter "micro truck"), a micro special purpose vehicle
(hereinafter "micro special purpose vehicle") and a motorcycle equipped with a progressive
braking system pursuant to Table 1 of the Enforcement Regulations of the MVMA, it means a
main braking system which is operating independent of a progressive braking system.
38. "Progressive braking system" means a main braking system where the brakes on all wheels of
micro PCs, micro trucks, and micro special purpose vehicles (hereinafter "micro vehicles"), and
motorcycles are controlled by a single control unit.
39. (Not translated)
40. "Pedestrian headform" means an adult headform and a child headform used for pedestrian
protection tests.
41. "Pedestrian legform" means an upper legform and a lower legform used for pedestrian
protection test.
42. "Pedestrian headform zone" means a zone on the outer surfaces of the front structure (except
windscreen), which is bounded by the 1,000mm and 1,700mm wrap around lines and side
reference lines ('child headform zone'), or which is bounded by the 1,700mm and 2,100mm wrap
around lines and side reference lines ('adult headform zone').
43. "Pedestrian legform zone" means a zone in the frontal surface where a legform is impacted.
44. "Wrap Around Distance (WAD)" means the geometric trace described on the frontal upper
surface by one end of a flexible tape, when it is held in a vertical fore and aft plane of the vehicle
and traversed across the front surfaces of the bonnet and bumper. One end of the tape is held at
ground reference level and the other end is held in contact with the front structure.

45. "Side reference line" means the geometric trace of highest point of contact between a straight
edge and the side of a front structure, when the straight edge, held parallel to the lateral vertical
plane of the car and inclined inward by 45 degrees, is traversed down the side of the front
structure, while remaining in contact with the surface of the body shell.
46. (Deleted)47. (Deleted)
48. "Lower bumper height" means the vertical distance between the ground reference plane and
the geometric trace of the lower most points of contact between a straight edge and the bumper,
when the straight edge, held parallel to the vertical longitudinal plane of the car and inclined
forwards by 25 degrees, is traversed across the front of the car whilst maintaining contact with
the ground and with the surface of the bumper line.
49. (Deleted)
50. "Electric vehicle" means a vehicle pursuant to Article 2 Subparagraph 3 of the Act on
Promotion for Development and Supply of Environmentally Friendly Vehicles.
50-2. "Low-speed electric vehicle" means an electric vehicle pursuant to Article 35-2 of the Act.
51. "Electric regenerative braking system" means a braking system which, during deceleration,
provides for the conversion of vehicle kinetic energy into electrical energy.
52. "High voltage electric device" means an electric device for the purpose of power train, such as
traction motor, power transformation device, traction battery, fuel cell, etc., whose working
voltage is > 60 V and ≤ 1500 V DC or and > 30 V and ≤ 1000 V AC rms.
53. "Traction battery" means an assembly of accumulators constituting the storage of energy used
for powering the traction motor(s) of the vehicle.
54. "Traction motor" means a device that can convert electrical energy into rotational mechanical
energy to propel the vehicle.
55. "Live parts" means any conductor or conductive part(s) intended to be electrically energized in
normal use.
56. "Tire pressure monitoring system" (TPMS) means a system fitted on a vehicle, able to perform
a function to evaluate the inflation pressure of the tires or the variation of this inflation pressure
over time and to transmit corresponding information to the user.
57. "Amphibious vehicle" means a vehicle, pursuant to Article 2 Subparagraph 1 of the MVMA,
equipped with the structure and system for which the vehicle can sail on the water.
58. "Fuel cell vehicle" means a vehicle powered by the electrical energy generated by using
hydrogen.
59. "Fuel cell" means a device which generates electrical energy by using hydrogen.
60. "Lane Departure Warning System (LDWS)" means a system to warn the driver of an
unintentional drift of the vehicle out of its travel lane.
61. "Advanced emergency braking system (AEBS)" means the system that braking is applied
automatically by the vehicle in response to the detection of a likely collision to reduce the vehicle
speed and potentially avoid the collision.
62. "Escape hatch" means an opening in the roof or the floor intended for use as escaping outside
the vehicle by passengers in an emergency only.
63. "Emergency exit" means an entrance, emergency door, emergency window, or escape hatch.
64. "Automated driving system" means an automated equipment, software, and related system that
can operate a vehicle upon recognizing and judging the surrounding situation and road
information, etc., without any operation of a driver or passenger.

Article 3 (Security of Safety of Structure and System) The structure and the systems of each motor
vehicle or motorcycle shall be so manufactured or serviced that ensures safe operation.

Article 3-2 (Scope of Device Necessary for the Safe Driving of Vehicle) The "device prescribed by
Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT)" specified in Article 8
Paragraph 2 Subparagraph 21 of the Enforcement Ordinance of the MVMA means the autonomous
steering system pursuant to Article 2 Subparagraph 64.

CHAPTER 2 SAFETY STANDARDS OF MOTOR VEHICLES AND MOTORCYCLES

Section 1 Motor Vehicle Safety Standards

Article 4 (Length, Width, and Height)
(1) The length, width, and height of a vehicle shall not exceed the following limits:
1. Length: 13 m (or 16.7 meters in the case of tow vehicle-trailers)
2. Width: 2.5 m [width of extruded parts such as devices for indirect vision, ventilation devices or
windows opening outward shall not exceed 25 cm for passenger cars pursuant to Article 3
Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 1 of the MVMA (hereinafter "passenger cars"), or 30 cm for other
vehicles. However, in the event that a trailer is wider than a tow vehicle, devices for indirect
vision of a tow vehicle shall not extrude more than 10 cm from the outermost part of a trailer.]
3. Height: 4 m
(2) The length, width, and height of a vehicle as specified in Paragraph 1 shall be measured in the
following states:1. Unloaded
2. On a horizontal plane with wheels in the straight-ahead position
3. With extruded parts removed or closed, such as devices for indirect vision mounted outside of
the body, antenna, windows opening outward, flash warning lamp, and ventilation device
installed in emergency vehicles
4. However, the items notified by the Minister of MOLIT, such as devices for fixing loading goods,
shall be excluded from the measurement.

Article 5 (Ground Clearance) The ground clearance of a vehicle in the unloaded state between the
ground and the parts other than the ground interface shall be greater than 10 cm, except for vehicles
such as special purpose vehicles or racing vehicles which are recognized by the Minister of MOLIT
as necessary.

Article 6 (Gross Vehicle Weight, Etc.)
(1) The gross vehicle weight of a vehicle shall not exceed 20 tons (or 30 tons for buses, or 40 tons for
trucks and special purpose vehicles), and the axle load shall not exceed 10 tons, and the wheel
load shall not exceed 5 tons.
(2) The tow vehicle-trailer shall also comply with Paragraph 1.
(3) The curb weight for a micro PC shall not exceed 600 kg while those of a micro truck and a micro
special purpose vehicle shall not exceed 750 kg and 1,100 kg, respectively.

Article 7 (Load Distribution)
(1) The sum of steered wheel loads shall be greater than 20% of each of the curb weight and gross
vehicle weight (or 18% for 3-wheeled light-weight or small-sized vehicles).
(2) Each tow vehicle shall meet the requirements of Paragraph 1 with a trailer (except full trailers)
linked.

KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)Article 8 (Maximum Stable Inclination Angle)
(1) Motor vehicles (including tow vehicle-trailers) shall not be overturned while tilted, either to the
right or the left, at degrees specified in each of the following Subparagraphs.
1. For passenger cars, trucks, special purpose vehicles (SPVs) and buses with a passenger capacity
of ten persons or less: 35 degrees at curb weight condition (if the gross vehicle weight of the
vehicle is 1.2 times or less of the vehicle weight, 30 degrees)
2. Buses with a passenger capacity of eleven persons or more: 28 degrees at laden condition
(2) The maximum stable inclination angle standards under Paragraph 1 shall not apply to the vehicles
specified in the following Subparagraphs:
1. Application-specific special purpose vehicles structured and equipped for vacuum cleaning
2. Application-specific special purpose vehicles structured and equipped for high-altitude works,
broadcasting, bridge inspections and transportation of household cargoes, and recovery-type
special purpose vehicles

Article 9 (Minimum Turning Radius)
(1) The minimum turning radius of a vehicle shall not exceed 12 m when a measurement is made
along the center line of the trace of a front outer wheel.
(2) Notwithstanding Paragraph 1, Each bus shall be able to maneuver on either side for a complete
circular trajectory of 360 degrees inside an area defined by two concentric circles, the outer circle
having a radius of 12.5 m and the inner circle having a radius of 5.3 m, without any of the vehicle's
outermost points projecting outside the circumferences of the circles.

Article 10 (Ground Interface and Pressure to Ground) The ground interface and pressure to
ground of a vehicle in the loaded state shall meet each of the following requirements.
1. The ground interface shall be of a structure which creates minimal noise and which will not
damage the road.2. (Deleted)
3. Pressure to ground of a caterpillar shall not exceed 3 kg per 1cm2.
4. (Deleted)

Article 11 (Engine and Power Train)
(1) The engine of a vehicle shall meet each of the following requirements.
1. Each part of the engine shall operate in the normal manner, and its starting system and shut-off
system shall be of a structure operable from the driver's seat.
2. (Deleted)3. (Deleted)4. (Deleted)
(2) The power train of a vehicle shall be free of damage or leakage of oil from the joints which may
affect safe driving.
(3) The governor (referring to the fuel injection regulator) of a diesel powered vehicle shall be sealed
so that the fuel injection cannot be adjusted arbitrarily, and the seal shall not be removed or
damaged arbitrarily.
(4) The engine and power train shall be designed and manufactured so that the maximum speed of
micro vehicle could not exceed 80 km/h.

Article 12 (Running Gear)
(1) The pneumatic tires of a vehicle shall meet the requirements specified in Table 1-2.
(2) The tires and each part of the running gear shall maintain solid connections, and shall be free of

(4) The wheels installed into PC, each bus(limited to trailer), truck or special purpose vehicle with a
gross vehicle weight of 4.5 tons or less shall meet the requirements specified in Article 112-11
and have the structure such that the abrasion of brake lining for service brake system can be
capable of being checked from outside without disassembling it. However, it shall not be applied
to the micro vehicle.

Article 12-2 (Tire Pressure Monitoring System (TPMS))
(1) The TPMS shall be equipped in PCs, and in buses, trucks and special purpose vehicles with a
GVW of 3.5 tons or less. However, the requirement is not applicable to those vehicles with dual
wheels on an axle, trailers, and micro vehicles.
(2) The TPMS equipped in vehicles shall meet each of the following requirements:
1. The system shall operate in the speed range of at least 40 km/h and maximum speed.
2. The malfunction telltale shall meet each of the following requirements:
A. It shall be activated when the ignition (start) switch is in the "on" (run) position, and
extinguished in normal operation. The requirement does not apply to telltales shown in a
common space.
B. It shall be in clear view of the driver even in daylight.

Article 13 (Controls, Etc.)
(1) The controls and displays for each of the following systems or devices installed in a vehicle shall
be positioned in a way to ensure the accessibility and field of view by a driver with a seatbelt
fastened.
1. Main starting system, shut-off system, accelerator control, and other engine controls
2. Controls for the brake system and power train
3. Controls for gearshift, windshield wiper, windshield washer, defrost, defog, headlamp, light
switch, hazard warning lamp, turn signal, and horn
4. Displays for speedometer, turn signal, high beam, fuel, engine coolant temperature, oil, brake
failure warning, electrical charge, and eco indicator
(2) The accelerator control system shall include at least two sources of energy capable of returning
the throttle to the idle position whenever the driver removes the opposing actuating force from
any accelerator position, and each position of gears shall be marked on the gearshift lever (or at a
place easily recognizable by a driver if it is difficult to mark on the lever).
(3) The automatic transmission shall meet each of the following requirements.
1. A neutral position shall be located between forward drive and reverse drive positions.
2. If a steering-column-mounted gear shift lever is used, movement from neutral position to
forward drive positions shall be clockwise.
3. If the gear shift lever sequence includes a park position, it shall be located at the end, adjacent
to the reverse drive position. However, the requirement is not applicable to a gear shift lever
which is not controlled in the sequence.
4. The engine starter shall be inoperative when the gearshift lever is in a forward or reverse drive
position, except for following vehicles.
A. Hybrid carB. Electric vehicle
C. Vehicle in which a neutral position is automatically engaged when the engine stops operation
D. Vehicle in which the engine may stop and restart automatically when the vehicle is stationary
5. In vehicles having more than one forward transmission gear ratio, any one of forward drive

(4) Any hand-operated control listed in Table 2, if installed, shall be identified by either the symbol,
the word, or the abbreviation designated in the same Table, and shall meet the requirement of
illumination. However, this requirement is not applicable to lever-type controls mounted on the
right or left of the steering column for the turn signal, hazard warning lamp, wiper, and washer.
(5) Any display located within the passenger compartment and listed in Table 2, if installed, shall be
identified according to Table 2, and shall meet the requirements of illumination and color.
However, the requirement is not applicable if displays indicating whether operational or
(mal)functioning (hereinafter "telltale") are used in conjunction with a gauge other than the
telltales.
(6) In vehicles with an auxiliary starting system (meaning remote keyless entry operated by radio
signals etc.), the engine starter shall not be operable if the gearshift lever is in any forward or
reverse drive position.
(7) If installing a lift axle that can move up and down to a truck or a special purpose vehicle, it shall
have the structure such that the lift axle is automatically lowered and impossible to be raised and
30 percent or more and 100 percent or less load of the adjacent axle load is distributed to the lift
axle which is lowered by the load of gross vehicle weight, when the load exceeding the smaller
one of the two loads specified in the following is applied to the axle adjacent to the lift axle.
1. Axle weight pursuant to Article 6
2. Permissible load per each axle specified in vehicle specification table pursuant to Form 25 of
the Enforcement Regulation of the MVMA (hereinafter "permissible load per each axle")
(8) Notwithstanding Paragraph 7, a manual operation device for each lift axle meeting the following
requirements may be installed if the lift axle is to be operated temporarily for the escape from off-
roads, etc.
1. The load distributed to each lift axle shall not be more than 130 percent of the permissible load
per each drive axle not exceeding 15 tons.
2. At least one axle installed in the front of the lift axle in the forward direction of a vehicle shall
not be lifted from the ground when the lift axle is raised using a manual operation device.
3. It shall be structured to be automatically lowered to distribute the load, before the vehicle speed
exceeds 30 km/h after the vehicle escapes from off-roads.

Article 14 (Steering Control System)
(1) The steering control system of a vehicle shall meet each of the following requirements:
1. Each part of the steering control system, when steered, shall not be in contact with other parts of
a vehicle, such as the frame or body, and shall be free of cracks or damage, and shall be operable
in the normal manner.
2. The steering control system shall be so constructed that no part of the system can catch the
driver's clothing or jewelry during normal driving maneuvers.
3. It shall be possible to leave a curve with a radius of 50 m at a tangent at the following speed.
The turning circle shall remain the same or become larger:
A. Passenger cars: 50 km/h
B. Vehicles other than passenger cars: 40 km/h or the maximum design speed if this is below
the speeds given above.
4. It shall be possible to travel along a straight section of road without unusual steering correction
by the driver and without unusual vibration in the steering system at the maximum design speed
of the vehicle, except the vibration caused by the steering control system according to
Subparagraph 10 Item A.

5. The steering equipment shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way that it is capable
of withstanding the stresses (strain) arising during normal operation of the vehicle.
6. The effectiveness of the steering equipment, including the electrical control lines, shall not be
adversely affected by magnetic or electric fields
7. Adjustment devices for steering geometry shall be such that after adjustment a positive
connection can be established between the adjustable components by appropriate locking
8. The steered wheels shall not be solely the rear wheels. This requirement does not apply to semi-
trailers.
9. For the purpose of this regulation the steered wheels, the steering control and all mechanical
parts of the steering transmission shall not be regarded as liable to breakage if they are amply
dimensioned, are readily accessible for maintenance, and exhibit safety features at least equal to
those prescribed for other essential components (such as the braking system) of the vehicle.
Where the failure of any such part would be likely to result in loss of control of the vehicle, that
part shall be made of metal or of a material with equivalent characteristics and shall not be
subject to significant distortion in normal operation of the steering system.
10. Any fault which impairs the steering function and is not mechanical in nature shall be signaled
clearly to the driver of the vehicle. However, one of the following cases shall be considered to
conform to the requirement:
A. The deliberate application of vibration in the steering system may be used as an additional
indication of a fault condition in this system.
B. In the case of a motor vehicle (except a trailer), an increase in steering force is considered to
be a warning indication.
C. In the case of a trailer, a mechanical indicator is permitted.
(2) (Deleted)
(3) The free play of the steering wheel (the distance the steering wheel moved until the steered wheel
starts to move) shall be less than 12.5% of the diameter of the steering wheel.
(4) The side-slip of the steered wheel shall be less than 5mm each to the right and to the left when a
vehicle travels 1 m, and the alignment of each wheel shall not hinder safe operation.

Article 14-2 (Lane Departure Warning System (LDWS)) The LDWS shall be installed in buses
(except light-weight buses) and in trucks and special purpose vehicles with a gross vehicle weight
more than 3.5 tons, except the vehicle applicable to any one of each following Subparagraphs.
1. (Deleted)2. Trailer
3. Dump trucks pursuant to Table 1 of the Enforcement Regulations of the MVMA
4. Vehicles for which the standing passenger capacity is specified in the vehicle specification
pursuant to Form 25 of the Enforcement Regulations of the MVMA
5. Other vehicles which are recognized by the Minister of MOLIT as incapable or unnecessary to
install the LDWS due to its structure or driving condition, etc.

Article 15 (Brake System)
(1) Each vehicle (except micro vehicle and trailers) shall be equipped with a service brake system
and a parking brake system mainly used when parking, and shall meet each of the following
requirements.
1. The service brake system and the parking brake system shall be operable independently, and the
service brake system shall act on all wheels simultaneously.

any other subsystem to stop the vehicle, and the brake system shall be of a structure to adjust
brake force progressively and to apply brake force continuously.
3. The recommended type of brake fluid shall be identified on a brake reservoir.
4. wear of the service brakes shall be compensated for by means of a system of automatic
adjustment, except for the service brakes of trucks and special purpose vehicles with a GVW
exceeding 3.5 tons which are driven by all wheels, and except for the service brakes on a rear
axle of trucks and special purpose vehicles with a GVW not greater than 3.5 tons.
5. The wear condition of all service brakes shall be indicated by a warning indicator (acoustic alarm
or yellow warning lamp) or it shall be able to be checked visually.
6. If the service braking force depend exclusively on the use of an energy reserve, there shall be at
least two completely independent energy reserves (one reserve if the service braking can be
activated by the drive's muscular energy not by the energy reserves), each of the aforesaid energy
reserves shall be equipped with a warning device as defined in Paragraph 4.
7. The parking brake system shall be of a structure to be held in the locked position by a purely
mechanical device.
8. The parking brake system shall be of a structure to apply brake force while in motion.
9. Vehicles equipped with a pneumatic service brake system (including an air boosted hydraulic
service brake system) shall meet each of the following requirements.
A. A pressure gauge indicating the air pressure of the energy reservoir of each line shall be
provided at a place readily visible by a driver.
B. In the case of a pneumatic service brake system comprising two or more independent sections,
any leakage between the brake control device and the braked wheels shall be vented to
atmosphere.
10. The spike-brake performance of the service brake system when a vehicle is spike-braked on a
dry, level and paved road surface shall meet the requirements specified in Table 3.
11. The brake performance and control force of the service brake system shall meet the
requirements specified in Table 4.
12. The brake performance and control force of the parking brake system shall meet the
requirements specified in Table 4-2.
(2) The micro vehicle shall be equipped with a service brake system and a parking brake system, and
shall meet each of the following requirements.
1. It shall be equipped with the foot-actuated split braking system, foot-actuated progressive
braking system, and auxiliary braking system as the service brake system. However, a parking
brake system meeting the performance requirements of the auxiliary braking system may be
used as the auxiliary braking system.
2. The service brake system and the parking brake system shall be operable independently, and the
service brake system shall act on all wheels simultaneously.
3. For vehicles that use hydraulic fluid for brake force transmission, the master cylinder shall:
A. Have a sealed, covered, separate reservoir for each brake system
B. Have a minimum reservoir capacity equivalent to 1.5 times the total fluid displacement
required to satisfy the new to fully worn lining condition with the worst case brake adjustment
condition
C. Have a reservoir where the fluid level is visible for checking without removal of the cover
4. Wear of the service brakes shall be compensated for by means of a system of automatic
sensing/adjustment
5. The wear condition of all service brakes shall be indicated by a warning indicator (acoustic alarm
or yellow warning lamp), or it shall be able to be checked with the naked eyes
6. The parking brake system shall be of a structure to be held in the locked position by a purely

7. The yellow warning lamp shall be installed in the micro vehicle equipped with the anti-lock
service brake system. It shall be switched on upon positioning the ignition key toward its
operation and in case of no breakdown, it shall be switched off and in case of breakdown it shall
be continuously switched on.
8. The spike-brake performance of the service brake system when a vehicle is spike-braked on a
dry, level and paved road surface shall meet the requirements specified in Table 3.
9. The brake performance and control force of the service brake system shall meet the requirements
specified in Table 4.
10. The brake performance and control force of the parking brake system shall meet the
requirements specified in Table 4-2.
(3) The service brake system of a trailer (except those with a GVW of 0.75 ton or less) shall meet
each of the following requirements:
1. It shall conform to the requirement of Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 1, Subparagraph 4 (except a
trailer with a GVW of 3.5 tons or less), Subparagraph 5, Subparagraph 7, and Subparagraph 10
through Subparagraph 12
2. It shall be of a structure which is linked with the service brake system of a tow vehicle and acting
simultaneously
3. The brake system shall be such that the trailer is stopped automatically if the coupling separates
the trailer which is in motion. However, this provision shall not apply to a trailer with a GVW
of 1.5 tons or less, on the condition that the trailer is fitted with a secondary coupling such as
chain, wire rope, etc. capable, in the event of separation of the main coupling, of preventing the
drawbar from touching the ground.
4. The parking brake system of a trailer, if separated from a tow vehicle, shall be actuated
independently
(4) Each vehicle (except micro vehicles and trailers) shall be fitted with a warning indicator mounted
in clear view of the driver to indicate malfunction of the brake performance of the service brake
system when the level of brake fluid drops below the reference level (or reference air pressure of
a pneumatic brake system), and the warning indicator shall meet the requirement of Subparagraph
1 and Subparagraph 2, or Subparagraph 1 and Subparagraph 3 below.
1. The acoustic signal or optical signal used for the warning indicator shall be able to be
differentiated from those for other warning indicators. However, this requirement shall not apply
if it is used in common for a parking brake system.
2. The optical signal shall be in red with sufficient brightness, and shall be mounted in clear view
of the driver.
3. The sound pressure of the acoustic signal shall be not less than 65dB for a passenger car when
measured at the driver's ear location, or 75dB for other vehicles, or 70dB for diesel engine
passenger cars.(5) (Not translated)
(6) The anti-lock brake system meeting the requirements of the following items shall be installed on
the vehicle, except micro vehicles and camping trailers/trailers with a GVW of 3.5 tons or less.
1. The yellow warning lamp shall be installed on the vehicle so that the driver, upon the failure of
the anti-lock brake system, could easily check the failure.
2. The tow vehicle towing the trailer with the anti-lock brake system shall be equipped with a
separate yellow warning lamp so that the driver of the tow vehicle, upon the failure of the anti-
lock brake system of the trailer, could easily check the failure.
3. The yellow warning lamp of Subparagraph 1 and Subparagraph 2 shall be illuminated by the
activation of the ignition switch and extinguished when the failure condition does not exist. The

warning lamp shall remain on while a failure condition exists.
4. The anti-lock brake system of the trailer shall be operated in conjunction with the anti-lock brake
system of the tow vehicle.(7) (Not translated)(8) (Not translated)
(9) The stop lamps shall be activated in each of the following cases, and shall remain activated until
the brake force is removed. However, the stop lamps shall not be activated upon selective braking,
and may be activated or not activated depending on deceleration in the case of braking by an
auxiliary braking system:1. Service brake is activated by the control of the driver,
2. Service brake is activated by automatically controlled braking. However, it may not be
illuminated if acceleration/deceleration is less than 0.7 m/s2
(10) Notwithstanding the requirement of Paragraph 9 above, all stop lamps (including auxiliary stop
lamp; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Paragraph) or turn signal lamps, for a vehicle
equipped with an emergency stop signal system or electrical regenerative brake system (limited
to PC), shall conform to the following requirements for operation.
1. Stop lamps or turn signal lamps for vehicles equipped with an emergency stop signal system,
upon quick braking, shall operate in accordance with the operational requirements for an
emergency brake signal in Table 5-2, Subparagraph 1.
2. Stop lamps for vehicles equipped with an electrical regenerative device that causes the vehicle
to decelerate upon releasing the acceleration pedal shall operate in accordance with the
operational requirements for stop lamps in Table 5-2, Subparagraph 2.
(11) A passenger car equipped with an electric regenerative braking system shall meet each of the
following requirements:
1. For vehicles equipped with an anti-lock device, the anti-lock device shall not be affected by the
electric regenerative braking system.
2. Vehicles equipped with the electric regenerative braking system which is part of the service
braking system, shall meet each of the following requirements:
A. In the case of vehicles equipped with electric regenerative braking systems which can be
controlled independently when the service braking system is in operation, the braking input
from other sources of braking shall be automatically compensated.
B. In the case of short disconnection transients, incomplete compensation is accepted, but within
1 second, this compensation shall have attained at least 75% of its final value.
C. The service braking system shall have only one control device, and it shall not be possible to
disconnect partially or totally one part of the service braking system other than by an
automatic device.
D. The service braking system shall not be adversely affected by the disengagement of the
motor(s) or by the gear ratio used.
(12) The brake hose and brake lining installed in motor vehicles (except micro vehicles) shall conform
to the standard of Article 112-2 and Article 112-10.
(13) Each vehicle shall be equipped with a Brake Assist System (BAS) to meet the requirements
specified in Table 4-3. However, micro vehicles, trailers, and buses exceeding, trucks exceeding
and special purpose vehicles exceeding 3.5 tons of GVW shall be exempt.
(14) Service braking system for PC, for which the control transmission system is electrical, shall meet
the structure and performance requirements for the service braking system in Table 4-5.

Article 15-2 (Electronic Stability Control System)
(1) The ESC system shall be equipped in vehicles. The requirement is not applicable to each vehicle

(2) The ESC system equipped in vehicles shall meet each of the following requirements:
1. It shall be capable of applying braking torques individually to all four wheels (an axle group
shall be treated as a single axle and dual wheels shall be treated as a single wheel.) and has a
control algorithm that utilizes this capability.
2. It shall be operational over the full speed range of the vehicle, during all phases of driving
including acceleration, coasting, and deceleration (including braking), except;
A. When the driver has disabled ESC,B. When the vehicle speed is below 20 km/h,
C. While the initial start-up self test and plausibility checks are completed, not to exceed 2
minutes when driven under the conditions of ESC malfunction,
D. When the vehicle is being driven in reverse;
3. It shall remain capable of activation even if the antilock brake system or traction control system
is also activated.
4. It shall be equipped with a telltale which is activated upon malfunctioning.

Article 15-3 (Advanced Emergency Braking System (AEBS)) The AEBS shall be installed in
motor vehicles (except light-weight buses and micro vehicles) except the vehicle applicable to any
one of the following Subparagraphs.1. (Deleted)2. Trailer
3. Dump trucks pursuant to Table 1 of the Enforcement Regulations of the MVMA
4. Vehicles for which standing passenger capacity is specified in the vehicle specification pursuant
to Form 25 of the Enforcement Regulations of the MVMA
5. Other vehicles which are recognized by the Minister of MOLIT as incapable or unnecessary to
install the AEBS due to its structure or driving condition, etc.

Article 16 (Suspension System)
(1) Each vehicle shall be equipped with a suspension system consisting of springs etc. which is
capable of absorbing the impact from the road surface.
(2) Each part of the suspension system pursuant to Article 1 shall be free of crack, separation or
damage.

Article 17 (Fuel System)
(1) The fuel tank, filler neck and vapor vent of a vehicle shall meet each of the following requirements:
1. The fuel system shall not cause fuel spillage by the movement of a vehicle.
2. The above parts (except fuel tank) shall be apart at least 30 cm from the end of the exhaust pipe.
3. The above parts (except fuel tank) shall be apart at least 20 cm from exposed electric terminals
or switches.
4. The above parts shall not be installed inside the occupant compartment, and shall be isolated

(2) The vehicles which use the hydrogen gas as the fuel shall meet each of the following requirements.
1. The hydrogen concentration, emitted from the vehicle exhaust system, shall not exceed 4 percent
average and 8% at any time.
2. At the fuel system in the downstream of shut-off valve, the hydrogen concentration shall not
exceed 1.0%.
3. At the fuel system in the downstream of shut-off valve, if the hydrogen concentration exceeds
2±1% in enclosed or semi-enclosed spaces such as passenger compartment, luggage
compartment and space under the hood, the red warning shall be illuminated and if the
concentration exceeds 3±1%, the shut-off valve shall be closed.

Article 18 (Electrical System) The electrical system of a vehicle shall meet each of the following
requirements.
1. The electrical wiring harness of a vehicle shall be covered by insulation material and fixed to
the body.
2. The electric terminals and switches inside the occupant compartment shall be covered by proper
insulation material.
3. The battery shall be securely fixed to avoid being loosened or damaged by vibration or impact
of a vehicle, and the battery, if installed inside the occupant compartment, shall be covered by
insulation material.

Article 18-2 (High Voltage Electric Device) The high voltage electric device of a vehicle shall meet
the requirements for insulation safety of high voltage electric device specified in Table 5.

Article 18-3 (Traction Battery) The traction battery of a vehicle shall meet each of the following
requirements.
1. The traction battery shall be of a structure which is isolated from the passenger compartment by
a wall or a protection plate.
2. The traction battery shall be protected by properly rated fuses or circuit breakers which may
prevent overcharging or over-current beyond the designed specifications.
3. The traction battery shall not catch fire or explode in a physical, chemical, electrical and thermal
conditions defined elsewhere by the Minister of MOLIT.

Article 18-4 (Cyber Security) The electrical/electronic systems of motor vehicles that are related to
motor vehicle cyber attacks/threats shall comply with the following standards in accordance with the
details of the automotive cyber security management system (CSMS) certification pursuant to Article
30-9 Paragraph 1 of the Act.
1. Key components of the motor vehicle that are related to motor vehicle cyber attacks/threats shall
be identified.
2. Risks associated with motor vehicle cyber attacks/threats shall be assessed for the relevant motor
vehicle type, considering the following.
A. Each component of the motor vehicle related to motor vehicle cyber attacks/threats, and
interactions between the components
B. Interaction between each component of the motor vehicle related to motor vehicle cyber
attacks/threats and external systems
C. Motor vehicle cyber attacks/threats including those prescribed and notified by the Minister
of MOLIT
3. Risks associated with motor vehicle cyber attacks/threats assessed in accordance with

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)Subparagraph 2 shall be appropriately managed.
4. Security measures prescribed and notified by the Minister of MOLIT to protect motor vehicles
from the risks associated with motor vehicle cyber attacks/threats assessed in accordance with
Subparagraph 2, shall be applied. However, if the security measures prescribed and notified by
the Minister of MOLIT are not relevant to, or not sufficient for, the risks associated with motor
vehicle cyber attacks/threats assessed in accordance with Subparagraph 2, separate and
appropriate security measures shall be applied.
5. When a dedicated environment, such as an interface (referring to software that mediates between
the vehicle occupant and manufacturer, etc.) is provided in a motor vehicle after its sale for such
purposes as storage or execution, etc. of software, services, application programs, and data,
security measures shall be applied to protect the dedicated environment provided against motor
vehicle cyber attacks/threats.
6. Appropriate and sufficient testing shall be conducted to verify the effectiveness of the security
measures pursuant to Subparagraphs 4 and 5. In such cases, testing of matters prescribed and
notified by the Minister of MOLIT shall be included.
7. The following functions shall be provided to protect the motor vehicle from motor vehicle cyber
attacks/threats.
A. A function to detect and prevent motor vehicle cyber attacks/threats and associated
vulnerabilities of the motor vehicle
B. A function to support manufacturers, etc. to monitor motor vehicle cyber attacks/threats that
have been detected and associated vulnerabilities of the motor vehicle
C. A data forensics function capable of analyzing attempts or success status, etc. of motor vehicle
cyber attacks/threats
8. Risks related to the suppliers of motor vehicle parts and services, etc., as risks associated with
motor vehicle cyber attacks/threats for the relevant motor vehicle type, shall be identified and
managed.


Article 18-5 (Software)
(1) The software of a motor vehicle shall allow motor vehicle users, etc. to identify its version
(referring to a unique identifier representing the software status; hereinafter the same shall apply).
(2) A motor vehicle that performs any software update (hereinafter “update”) using wireless
information and communications technology shall comply with the following standards.
1. In the case of a failed or interrupted update, the motor vehicle shall be returned to a safe state,
such as by reverting the software to the version prior to the update or disabling the function of
running gear, etc.
2. An update shall be executed only when there is power necessary for completing the update and
performing the function pursuant to Subparagraph 1.
3. If the execution of an update may affect the safety of the motor vehicle, the motor vehicle shall
be maintained in a safe state, such as by disabling the function of running gear, etc. during the
execution of the update through technical means, etc.
4. The following information shall be provided to the motor vehicle user before the update is
executed.
A. Purpose of the update (including information on the importance of the update if the update is
performed for the purposes of taking corrective measure pursuant to Article 31 of the MVMA
or ensuring the safety or security of the motor vehicle)
B. Changes in motor vehicle functions resulting from the update
C. The expected time to complete execution of the update

Article 18-6 (Safety Standards for Electrical Equipment and Camping Equipment of Camping
Vehicle)
(1) The electrical equipment of a camping vehicle pursuant to Article 29 Paragraph 3 of the MVMA
shall comply with the following standards.
1. The external power inlet shall be of a structure that prevents the entry of water.
2. The charger shall be equipped with an overload protection function.
3. A warning label pursuant to Table 5 Subparagraph 4 Item A shall be affixed to high-voltage
parts not less than 60 volts DC or 30 volts AC.
4. There shall be means to cut off the power, such as leakage circuit breakers, fuses, etc.
(2) The camping equipment of a camping vehicle pursuant to Article 29 Paragraph 3 of the MVMA
shall comply with the following standards.
1. It shall be equipped with sleeping facilities (including convertible sofas) that can accommodate
sleeping persons equivalent to at least one-third of the seating capacity. In such cases, when
calculating the number of sleeping persons, any decimals shall be rounded up. For each sleeping
person, the sleeping facility shall be at least 1,700 mm wide and 500 mm long, or its area shall
be at least 8,500 cm2.
2. The inside of the camping vehicle shall be equipped with an emergency evacuation space,
emergency exit, or window that fall under any one of the following.
A. An emergency evacuation space at least 450 mm wide and at least 550 mm long between the
camping space and the occupant compartment where the driver is present
B. An emergency exit or window at least 450 mm wide and at least 550 mm long, which is
located far away from the access door to the camping space
C. An emergency exit or window inside the camping space, through which an ellipsoid with a
horizontal axis of 610 mm and vertical axis of 432 mm can pass without interference
3. Any storage compartment installed in the camping space shall have a device or structure to
prevent it from opening while driving.

Article 19 (Frame and Body)
(1) The frame and body of a vehicle shall meet each of the following requirements.
1. The frame (or body if frame is not available) shall be of a solid structure which ensures safe
operation of a vehicle, and the body shall be securely fixed to the frame to avoid being loosened
by vibration or impact.
2. The flammable parts of the body shall not be in contact with the exhaust pipe.
3. The horizontal distance from the center of the rearmost axle to the rearmost end of the body
(meaning "the rear overhang") (excluding the bumper and devices for towing) shall not exceed
1/2 of the horizontal distance from the center of a frontmost axle to the center of a rearmost axle.

(2) The gross vehicle weight, etc. shall be displayed to the motor vehicles classified under each of the
following Subparagraphs in accordance with the display criteria and methods specified in the
relevant Subparagraph.
1. Trucks: The gross vehicle weight and the maximum loading capacity determined by the
manufacturer, etc. shall be displayed on the rear of a vehicle in accordance with the methods of
displaying the loading capacity of trucks in Table 32-3. However, in the case where the gross
vehicle weight is less than 15 tons, the gross vehicle weight may not be displayed.
2. A tow-type special purpose vehicle: The weight of the vehicle plus the weight of the number of
passengers shall be displayed on the rear or right side of the vehicle.
3. A recovery-type special purpose vehicle: The maximum loading capacity determined by the
manufacturer, etc. shall be displayed on the rear side of the motor vehicle.
(3) Lateral protective devices which meet each of the following requirements in the unloaded state
on a paved road surface shall be installed in each truck, special purpose vehicle, or tow vehicle-
trailer with a GVW not less than 8 tons or with a maximum loading capacity not less than 5 tons.
However, this requirement is not applicable to vehicles of such a structure that pedestrians etc.
are not likely to be run over by the rear wheels, vehicles incapable of being installed due to
interference from structures of vehicle itself and its body, or vehicles for which the distance from
the steering axis is within 2,100 mm.1.- 6. (Not translated)
(4) A rear underrun protection bar which meet each of the following requirements in the unloaded
state on a paved road surface shall be installed in each truck or special purpose vehicle with a
GVW not less than 3.5 tons. However, this requirement is not applicable to vehicles of such a
structure that other vehicle, if it hits the rear side of the vehicle, are not likely to go underneath
the vehicle, or vehicles manufactured for towing a semi-trailer, or special purpose trailers to carry
long and inseparable objects such as woods, steel product or poles, or vehicles for which a rear
underrun protection bar will not meet the purpose of the vehicles.
1. The width of the rear protective device shall at no point exceed the width of the rear axle
measured at the outermost points of the wheels, excluding the bulging of the tires close to the
ground, nor shall it be more than 100 mm shorter on either side.
2. The ground clearance of the lowest part shall be less than 550 mm.
3. The vertical minimum height of the bar shall be not less than 100 mm.
4. The curvature of the left and right lateral side shall be not less than 2.5 mm.
5. It shall be installed within 400 mm inward the end of the body located not more than 2 m high.
However, this requirement is not applicable to a vehicle of a structure where installation within
400 mm is not possible.
6. For vehicles fitted with a platform lift at the rear, the underrun device may be separated for the
purposes of the mechanism. In this case, the following special requirements shall be met.
A. The maximum lateral clearance measured between the elements of the underrun device and
the elements of the platform lift may amount to no more than 25 mm.
B. The individual elements of the underrun protection shall have an effective surface area of at
least 350 cm2, except the vehicles having a width of less than 2 m.

(6) The outside of the body shall be free of sharp edges or protrusions which may affect safe operation
of a vehicle. However, this requirement is not applicable to special purpose vehicles.
(7) (Deleted)
(8) The color of a bus for transportation of children shall be yellow.
(9) The front and rear sides of a bus for transportation of children shall be provided with a detachable
label for children protection specified in Table 5-3.
(10) The bus for transportation of children shall be equipped with the stop indication device
(hereinafter "stop indication device") conforming to Table 5-3 Subparagraph 2 on the front left
side. In this case, one more device may be installed on the rear left side.
(11) Double-decked large-sized buses entirely or partially without a roof (hereinafter "double-decked
large-sized buses without a roof") shall have a protection panel on the second deck to prevent the
possibility of passengers falling out of the vehicle.
1. A front panel with a height of not less than 140 cm shall be installed.
2. A panel with a height of not less than 110 cm at the sides and 120mm at the rear of the vehicle
shall be installed or the protection shall consist of continuous side and rear panels with a height
of not less than 70 cm combined with one or more continuous guard rail(s) that fulfills the
following characteristics:
A. The guard rails shall be firmly attached to the structure of the vehicle and no dimension of its
section shall be less than 2 cm, or more than 4.5 cm;
B. The size of any aperture between a guard rail and any adjacent guard rail or panel shall not
exceed 20 cm;

Article 20 (Coupling Device and Towing Device)
(1) Each vehicle (except trailers) shall be equipped with a towing device on the front side or on the
rear side which withstands a force not less than 1/2 of the curb weight of a vehicle applied to the
vehicle's longitudinal direction and whose structure will not cause separation of the engagement
due to the vibration and impact.
(2) In the case that a vehicle (except micro vehicles) shall be equipped with a coupling device in order
to tow the trailer, each of the following requirements shall be met.
1. The coupling device (when the trailer is not coupled to the towing vehicle) shall not obscure the
license plate, except that the coupling devices which obscure the rear license plate may be
removable or repositionable without the use of tools.
2. Each vehicle shall be equipped with the electrical connectors, etc. to reciprocally incorporate
with the lighting system of towing vehicles and trailers.
3. A trailer with a GVW of 0.75 ton or less (except a trailer equipped with a brake system which
stops the trailer automatically if the coupling separates the trailer in motion) shall be fitted with
an auxiliary coupling device, such as a chain or wire rope, which will not cause a connecting rod
etc. to touch the ground although the coupling device is separated.
4. The detailed installation and strength, etc. of coupling devices shall comply with the
requirements notified by the Minister of MOLIT.

Article 21 (Hood Latch System) Each hood of a vehicle shall be provided with a hood latch system,
and a front opening hood, which, if opened while in motion, may obstruct driver's field of view, shall
be provided with a second latch position on the hood latch system or with a second hood latch system.

(1) Each passenger car, and each bus or truck or special purpose vehicle with a gross vehicle weight
of 4.5 tons or less shall have the anti-theft system to function any one or more of the following
Subparagraphs.1. To prevent the normal operation of steering2. To prevent the gear shifting3. To prevent the control of gear position
4. To prevent the movement of a vehicle by applying a braking force to an axle or a wheel of the
5. To prevent the start of the power source electronically
(2) The detailed requirements and test procedures of the anti-theft system pursuant to each item of
Paragraph 1 are defined and notified by the Minister of MOLIT.

Article 23 (Riding System)
(1) The riding system of a vehicle shall be of a structure providing safe riding of the passengers and
the buses with a seating capacity of 16 persons or more shall have the structure meeting each of
the following Subparagraph.
1. The stairs in entrance shall be equipped with protective equipment defined and notified by the
Minister of MOLIT
2. The stairs connecting the lower and upper decks of the double-decked buses are equipped with
protective equipment defined and notified by the Minister of MOLIT
3. Each vertical surface of the stairs connecting the lower and upper decks of the double decked
buses shall be closed up.
4. The front part in the first-row seats installed in a direction of the front window on upper deck of
double decked buses shall be equipped with protective equipment defined and notified by the
Minister of MOLIT
5. If the handlebars and handles are installed on the riding system, they shall comply with the
requirements specified in Table 5-27
(2) Each vehicle designed for carrying a driver and passengers shall be provided with an occupant
compartment blocked from outside (hereinafter "occupant compartment"). However, the
requirement is not applicable to vehicles such as fire trucks which are recognized by the Minister
of MOLIT as unnecessary.
(3) The occupant compartment of a vehicle (except micro vehicles, convertibles, or open-body type
vehicles) shall be equipped with a lighting system and a ventilation system recirculating inside
and outside air, and those parts which may affect the safety of passengers, such as engine coolant
(except for heating), regulator, alternator, transformer, shall not be installed inside the occupant
compartment.

However, the occupant compartment of a bus shall be equipped with a lighting system complying
with the requirement determined separately by the Minister of MOLIT.
(4) (Deleted)
(5) Double decked buses without a roof shall be equipped with video and announcement device that
enable a driver to make sure whether passengers on the upper deck are seated and to control those
passengers in the driving seat.

Article 24 (Driver's Seat)
(1) The driver's seat shall meet the requirements specified in each of the following items.
1. It shall be capable of providing proper field of view necessary to drive, and which will not
obstruct driver's control by passengers or cargo.
2. It shall be provided with a space which enables proper operation by a driver of the control devices

3. The center of the driver's seat and that of the steering wheel shall not deviate enough to cause
inconvenient handing of the steering wheel.
(2) The dimension of driver's seat shall meet the requirements specified in each of the following items.
1. For PC, 50 percentile male dummy shall be capable to seat as specified in Table 5-32
Subparagraph 1.
2. The longitudinal and transverse dimension of the seat shall be at least 40cm each for buses,
trucks, and special purpose vehicle (the longitudinal dimension may be 35cm or more for buses
with a designated seating capacity of 23 persons or less, and buses exceeding the seating capacity
of 23 persons with more number of room for standing than seating capacity).
(3) The driver's seat for buses with a seating capacity of 16 persons or more shall be installed in
compliance with the requirements of Table 5-28.

Article 25 (Passenger Seats, Etc.)
(1) The dimension of each passenger seat of vehicles (except buses for transportation of children)
shall meet the requirements specified in each of the following items. However, this requirement
is not applicable to those seats installed in ambulances, fire trucks or special purpose vehicles
which are recognized by Minister of MOLIT as difficult to meet in design.
1. For PC, 5 percentile female dummy shall be capable to seat as specified in Table 5-32
Subparagraph 2.
2. The longitudinal and transverse dimension of the seat shall be at least 40cm each for buses,
trucks, and special purpose vehicles (the longitudinal dimension may be 35cm or more for buses
with a designated seating capacity of 23 persons or less, and buses exceeding the seating capacity
of 23 persons with more number of room for standing than seating capacity).
3. The clearance between the rear of a seatback of a front seat and the front of a seatback of a seat
immediately behind shall be at least 65cm each for buses, trucks, and special purpose vehicles
(the clearance between the front of a seatback of facing seats, installed in buses, shall be at least
130 cm).
(2) The dimension of each passenger seat and the clearance between rows of seats of the buses for
transportation of children shall meet the requirements specified in each of the following items.
1. Seat dimension: A 5 percentile female dummy pursuant to Table 5-32 Subparagraph 2 shall be
seated, with a seat back (including the head restraint) of 71 centimeters or more in height.
2. Clearance between rows of seats: The clearance between the rear side of a seatback of a front
seat and the front side of a seatback of a seat behind shall be at least the distance in which a 5
percentile female dummy pursuant to Table 5-32 Subparagraph 2 can be seated.
(3) The height of each seat in buses (except buses with a designated seating capacity of 15 persons or
less and buses for transportation of children) shall be not less than 40cm nor more than 50cm,
except for those seats installed above the engine or wheels.
(4) For each passenger car a seat which may be attached/detached without the use of a tool may be
installed in the seats other than the front seats (including the driver's seat). However, the
classification of a vehicle pursuant to Article 3 of the MVMA shall not be changed.
(5) The sideways-facing seats shall not be installed in the vehicle, except in the following vehicles.
1. Buses with a seating capacity of 16 persons or more
2. Emergency vehicles
3. Vehicles where the safety belts are not installed in accordance with the exceptional provision of

30 persons or less. However, a folding seat for a guide may be installed in buses with a designated
seating capacity of 31 persons or more.
(2) Folding seats pursuant to Paragraph 1 installed in buses for transportation of children shall be of

(3) (Deleted)

Article 26 (Head Restraints) A head restraint which mitigates head impact shall be provided at each
front seating position (except inboard seating positions) in any of the following vehicles:
1. Passenger car (except micro PCs)2. Bus with a GVW of 4.5 tons or less
3. Truck with a GVW of 4.5 tons or less (except micro trucks and towed vehicles)
4. Special purpose vehicle with a GVW of 4.5 tons or less (except micro special purpose vehicles)

Article 27 (Seat Belt Assembly)
(1) A seat belt assembly shall be provided for each seat of a vehicle. However, it is not necessary to
provide the seat belt assemblies for those seats in one of the following vehicles.
1. Each seat for patience in an ambulance or seat in a special purpose vehicle recognized by
Minister of MOLIT as not necessary
2. Each passenger seat in a city bus or rural bus used for passenger transportation business pursuant
to Article 3 Subparagraph 1 of the Enforcement Ordinance of the Passenger Transport Service
Act, which is not driven on a motorway or expressway.
3. (Deleted)
(2) A 3-point or more seat belt assembly shall be installed in each seat of a passenger car, and a
driver's seat and its adjacent seats in other vehicles. However, a 2-point seat belt assembly may
be installed in each inboard seat or seats of the other vehicles for which it is structurally difficult
to install a 3-point or more seat belt assembly.
(3) The seat belt assembly required by Paragraph 1 shall conform to the standard pursuant to Article
112-3.
(4) For each vehicle (except micro vehicles) provided with seat belt assemblies pursuant to Paragraph
1, a warning device pursuant to requirements of Table 5-24 shall be provided recognizable from
driver's seat, if the engine is started or the vehicle is driven without a driver's seat belt or
passenger's seat belt of the vehicle pursuant to each of the following items fastened.
1. PC and truck/special purpose vehicle with a GVW of 3.5 tons or less: all seats
2. Bus and truck/special purpose vehicle with a GVW exceeding 3.5 tons: driver's seat or the seat
adjacent to the driver's seat(5) (Deleted)
(6) The seat belt assemblies installed in the passenger seats of buses for transportation of children
shall be adjustable to fit the children.

Article 27-2 (Child Seat Anchorage System) Child seat anchorage system shall be installed in each
passenger car (except micro PCs), except those with one row of seats, meeting each of the following
requirements.
1. The child seat anchorage system shall be installed at two or more seating positions, at least one
of which shall be installed at a second row seating position.
2. The child seat anchorage system shall be accessible without the need for any tools.
3. Markings easily visible showing the availability of the anchorages and their locations shall be
provided. However, this requirement is not applicable if a tether anchorage is visible and if lower

to the vehicle's longitudinal direction.
4. The anchorages shall be sealed to prevent the entry of exhaust fumes into the passenger
compartment.
5. The lower anchorages shall be installed not less than 120 mm behind the seating reference point.
6. In the case the anchorages are provided in the first row seat and an airbag is installed in front of
the seat, a device which can stop activation of the airbag shall be provided.
7. A child seat anchorage system shall consist of one tether anchorage and two lower anchorages
meeting the installation requirements set forth in Table 5-4. Convertibles are excluded from the
requirements to be equipped with tether anchorages, but if installed, it shall meet the installation
requirements of it.

Article 28 (Room for Standing)
(1) The room for standing is designed so that the measuring devices specified in Table 5-29 may pass
freely.
(2) The area for each standing passenger shall meet the requirements specified in Table 5-27.
(3) Grips or handle grips meeting the requirements specified in Table 5-27 shall be installed in
vehicles which are designed to accommodate standing passengers.
(4) Double-decked large-sized buses including Double-decked large-sized buses without a roof shall
not accommodate the standing passenger in the upper deck.

Article 29 (Entrance)
(1) An entrance shall be provided for each vehicle which meets each of the following requirements:
1. The bus with a seating capacity of 16 persons or more shall be installed at the entrance (except
the entrance with a structure such that a passenger may be seated immediately after opening the
entrance) meeting the requirements specified in Table 5-30.
2. (Deleted)
3. The bus with a seating capacity of 16 persons or more shall be installed a grip meeting the
requirements specified in Table 5-27 for passengers aiding getting in or out
4. (not translated – applicable to a bus for children's transportation)
(2) (Deleted)(3) (Deleted)
(4) Each door of a vehicle, except mid-sized buses or large-sized buses, shall be equipped with a
locking device meeting each of the following requirements:
1. The locking device shall have an operating means and a lock release/engagement device located
within the interior of the vehicle.
2. The locking device, when engaged, shall prevent operation of the exterior door handle or other
exterior latch release control
3. Each rear side door shall meet each of the following requirements, except doors equipped with
a child safety system which can be engaged and released independently of other locking devices:
A. The locking device, when engaged, shall prevent operation of the interior door handle or other
interior latch release control.
B. Tt shall require separate actions to unlock the door and operate the interior door handle or
other interior latch release control.
4. Each back door equipped with the interior latch release control shall be equipped with at least
one locking device which requires separate actions to unlock the door and operate the interior
latch release control.

Article 30 (Emergency Exit) An emergency exit meeting requirement specified in Table 5-31 shall
be installed in each bus with a designated seating capacity of 16 persons or more.

Article 31(Aisle) An aisle, by which the aisle-measuring device can pass, shall be installed in buses
with a designated seating capacity of 16 persons or more, except a vehicle with a structure equipped
with a seat so that persons may board the vehicle by opening the entrance.

Article 32 (Cargo Compartment)
(1) The cargo compartment of a vehicle shall be of a structure which ensures safe accommodation
and transportation of goods, and shall meet each of the following requirements:
1. The cargo box and other cargo compartments of a truck shall have a closed structure. However,
this shall not apply to a general truck, a dump truck, and a truck equipped with a device to fix
cargo.
2. The van-type trucks shall meet each of the following requirements:
A. The loading entrance shall be located at the rear or sides, and the doors shall open to the right
or left, or up or down, or shall be of a sliding type.
B. The riding compartment and cargo compartment shall be completely separated by the same
sheet metal as the body or a wall of a material which is not deformed more than 300 mm when
a load 50% of the maximum payload is applied. However, this requirement is not applicable
to a vent, or an area which cannot be separated due to manufacturing process, or a window
where protective bars to prevent cargo from being thrown out are installed.
C. The side walls and the rear wall shall be made of the material with an equivalent performance
to the body, and there shall not be a window installed on the side walls and the rear wall of
the cargo compartment. However, the requirement is not applicable to the cargo compartment
where window frames supporting window glass are provided or where tow or more protective
bars are welded on the body of the side wall and the rear wall or rear door where protective
bars are installed.
D. The floor surface area of the cargo compartment shall be greater than that of the riding
compartment.
3. The cargo compartment of a truck shall have a structure suitable for the maximum loading
capacity determined in the range of the gross weight allowable for manufacturing and the gross
vehicle weight of an unfinished vehicle written in the vehicle specification table of Form 25 of
the Enforcement Regulations of the MVMA. However, in the cases where the loading capacity
is calculated pursuant to other Acts such as the Enforcement Regulations of the High-Pressure
Gas Safety Control Act, etc., the structure shall comply with the criteria of the applicable laws.
4. The cargo compartment of the micro truck shall meet the requirements as below.
A. A maximum payload shall be 100 kg or more
B. The floor surface shall be 1m or less from the ground and the length shall not exceed 1.4
times tread (it means the front/rear tread, whichever is greater, specified in Form 25, Vehicle
specification of the Enforcement Regulations of the MVMA)
C. Space for the cargo compartment shall meet " length of cargo × width of cargo ≥ length of
vehicle × width of vehicle × 0.3
D. It shall be able to load a regular hexahedron with a side length of 60cm
(2) The cargo compartment for carrying a dead body, poisonous materials, high pressure gas,
explosives or other safety hazardous materials shall be completely separated from the occupant
compartment and shall be of a structure enabling loading and unloading from outside.
(3) In the case where an opening/closing cover is installed to meet the closed structure pursuant to
the main text of Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 1, a cover that meets the requirements of each of the

following Subparagraphs shall be installed. However, this shall not apply to a case of falling under

1. The cover shall be of a material with the waterproof function and shall not be easily damaged.
2. The shape of the cover shall be of a structure which completely covers the entire top of the cargo
