3. The cover shall be operated automatically or shall be operable with tools or control devices, etc.,
on the ground by users. However, this shall not apply to a case of falling under any of the
following Items.
A. As a case where equipment to protect users, such as footrests, etc., is installed, in the case of
a structure that requires the user to manually cover it
B. In the case of a structure in which the user cannot cover it through tools or operating devices
on the ground due to special purposes such as grain transportation, etc.

Article 33 (Gas Transportation Device) A gas transportation device, installed in a vehicle for gas
transportation, shall meet the requirements in each of the following Subparagraphs.
1. The gas container shall be securely fixed to the body so that it will not be loosened by the
movement of a vehicle.
2. The gas container shall be isolated from the occupant compartment by a wall or protection panel
so that the gas if leaked will not penetrate into the compartment, or surroundings of its valve
shall be shall be sealed with solid material to prevent gas leaking, and shall be of a structure
which protects the container from impacts, and shall be installed at a place which provides
ventilation of outside air.
3. The pipe (excluding an oil resistant rubber pipe) with both ends fixed shall be routed smoothly
and fixed to the body for at least every meter.
4. The gas charge valve shall be installed close to the charging inlet, and the control (including a
switch operated by an ignition key) for the intermediate cutoff valve shall be so installed that a
driver can easily operate it.
5. The pipe shall be made of steel, copper or oil resistant rubber.
6. The pipe (except oil resistant rubber pipe) with both ends fixed shall be routed smoothly and
fixed to the body for at least every meter.
7. The pipe in the high pressure portion shall be cable of withstanding the pressure 1.5 times the
charging pressure of the gas container.
8. The gas charge valve shall be installed close to the charging inlet, and the control (including a
switch operated by an ignition key) for the intermediate cutoff valve shall be so installed that a
driver can easily operate.
9. The gas container and container valve shall be installed at least 300 mm inward of the rearmost
edge of the body and at least 200 mm inward of the outmost area of the body. However, if the
gas container and its valve are protected by a steel plate with a strength not less than the standard
SS41 and of a thickness not less than 3.2 mm, they may be installed at least 200 mm inward
from the rearmost edge of the body and at least 100 mm inward of the outmost edge of the body.

Article 34 (Window Glass, Etc.)
(1) The windshield of a vehicle shall be of a laminated glass or glass-plastics and the other window
glasses shall be of a toughened glass, laminated glass, double-glazed unit, plastic glass or glass-
plastics. However, the requirement is not applicable to the window glass other than the windshield
of convertibles or vehicles with special structures such as camping cars, or the window glass of
camping trailers.(2) (Deleted)

(4) In passenger cars and buses (gross vehicle weight of 4.5 tons or less), the windows, sunroof or
partitions (hereinafter "windows, etc.") which are closed with electrical power system shall meet
the requirements of Paragraph 5, except that the windows are closed under one or more of the
following conditions:
1. When the ignition key is in the ignition control or in ACC position which radio or convenient
devices are operable (equivalent condition in case of a non-mechanical device).
2. By muscular force unassisted by power supply of the vehicle
3. On continuous activation by a locking system on the outside of the vehicle (limited to the
continuous activation for closure such as holding a control button pressed)
4. During the interval of time between the moment the ignition key has been removed and the
moment that neither of the two front doors has been opened
5. When the closing movement of a power-operated window etc. starts at an opening not exceeding
4mm
6. When the power-operated window of a vehicle's door without an upper door frame closes
automatically whenever the pertinent door is closed. In this case the maximum opening prior to
window closing shall not exceed 12mm.
7. Remote closing shall be allowed by continuous activation of a remote actuation device from a
distance of 11 meters (or 6 meters if an opaque surface is present) or less from the vehicle.
8. When the power-operated window of the driver's door and the roof panel is one-touch closed in
the following cases:A. When the ignition key is in the engine running position
B. During the interval of time between the moment the ignition has been switched from "on" to
"off" and/or the key has been removed and the moment that neither of the two front doors has
been opened sufficiently to permit egress of occupants (including a non-mechanical type
ignition system in the equivalent condition as above)
(5) The auto-reversing device shall meet at least one of the following requirements before contacting,
or before exerting a squeezing force of 100 Newton or more on a semi-rigid cylindrical rod from
4 mm to 200 mm in diameter that has the force-deflection ratio of 1kg/mm:
1. The window shall return to the position at the time of closing initiated.
2. The window shall open 50 mm or more from the position where the semi-rigid cylindrical rod
is contacted or where the squeezing force is exerted
3. The window shall open 200 mm or more.
4. In the case of tilting motion of a roof panel, the roof shall open with the maximum angular
opening.

Article 35 (Noise Prevention System) The noise prevention system of a vehicle shall meet the noise
standards specified in Article 30 and Article 35 of the Noise and Vibration Control Act.

Article 36 (Exhaust Emission System) The exhaust emission of a vehicle shall meet the emission
standards specified in Article 46 of the Clean Air Conservation Act.

Article 37 (Exhaust Pipes)
(1) The opening of the exhaust pipe of a vehicle shall not direct left or right exceeding 45o in a
longitudinal direction of the vehicle, and the end of exhaust pipe shall be installed not to be
extruded to the outside of the vehicle body.
(2) (Deleted)
(3) The exhaust pipe of a vehicle shall not cause fire of the vehicle or its loaded material, shall not

Article 38 (Headlamp)
(1) Driving beam headlamp to illuminate the forward of a vehicle shall be installed on the front of a
vehicle (except trailers), which meets each of the following requirements.
1. One or two headlamps shall be installed each on the left and right side of a vehicle. However,
one headlamp may be installed on the micro vehicle with a width of 130 cm or less
2. The color of the light shall be white.
3. The requirements for installation and luminous intensity of the headlamps shall meet Table 6-3.
However, a micro vehicle may apply to the requirements specified in Table 35.
(2) Passing beam headlamps to illuminate the forward of the vehicle(except trailer) without causing
undue dazzle or discomfort to oncoming drivers and other road users shall be installed and meet
each of following requirements.
1. One headlamp shall be installed each on the left and right of a vehicle. However, one headlamp
may be installed on the micro vehicle with a width of 130 cm or less
2. The color of the light shall be white.
3. The requirements for installation and luminous intensity of the headlamps shall meet Table 6-4.
However, a micro vehicle may apply to the requirements specified in Table 36.
(3) In the case that the adaptive front lighting system providing beams with differing characteristics
for automatic adaptation to varying conditions is installed on the front of a vehicle (except trailer),
each of following requirements shall be met.
1. One headlamp shall be installed each on the left and right of a vehicle.
2. The color of the light shall be white.
3. The requirements for installation and luminous intensity of the headlamps shall meet Table 6-5.
(4) Main passing beam with the luminous flux exceeding 2,000 lumens shall be installed with a
headlamp cleaner in accordance with the following requirements.
1. It shall operate at the speed of 130 km/h or less
2. The luminous intensity shall be 70 percent or more of the initial luminous intensity, after the
headlamp cleaner is operated

Article 38-2 (Fog Lamp)
(1) The front fog lamp, if installed on the front of vehicles (except trailer), shall meet each of the
following requirements:
1. One lamp shall be installed each on the left and right of a vehicle. However, one lamp may be
installed on the micro vehicle with a width of 130 cm or less
2. The color of the light shall be white or yellow.
3. The requirements for installation and luminous intensity of the front fog lamp shall meet Table
6-6. However, a micro vehicle may apply to the requirements specified in Table 37.
(2) The rear fog lamp, if installed on the rear of vehicles, shall meet each of the following
requirements:1. The number of the lamps installed shall be two or less.2. The color of the light shall be red.
3. The requirements for installation and luminous intensity of the rear fog lamp shall meet Table
6-7. However, a micro vehicle may apply to the requirements specified in Table 38.

Article 38-3 (Exterior Courtesy Lamp) The exterior courtesy lamp meeting requirements specified
in Table 6-30 may be installed on exterior of the vehicle.

Article 38-4 (Daytime Running Lamp) Daytime running lamp shall be installed on the front of a
vehicle (a trailer shall be excluded.) so that the vehicle can, in daytime driving, be easily detected,
meeting each of the following requirements:
1. One lamp shall be installed each on the left and right of a vehicle. However, one lamp may be
installed on the micro vehicle with a width of 130 cm or less
2. The color of the light shall be white.
3. The luminous intensity of the lamp shall meet the requirements of Table 6-8. However, a micro
vehicle may apply to the requirements specified in Table 39.

Article 38-5 (Cornering Lamp) The cornering lamp which is installed on the front of the vehicle or
the forward corner of the vehicle at a side shall meet each of following requirements
1. One lamp shall be installed each on the left and right of a vehicle.
2. The color of light shall be white.
3. The requirements of installation and luminous intensity for cornering lamp shall meet Table 6-
9.

Article 39 (Backup Lamp) Back up lamp shall be installed on a vehicle (except the trailer with a
GVW not exceeding 0.75 tons) and, if installed, shall meet each of following requirements
1. The number according to the following categories of each item on the rear side of the vehicle
shall be installed. However, in case of Item B, two more can be installed rearward at the rear or
one each rearward at the rear of both sides.
A. Motor vehicles with the length of 6 meters or less: 1 or 2
B. Motor vehicles with the length exceeding 6 meters: 2
2. The color of light shall be white.
3. The requirements of installation and luminous intensity for backup lamp shall meet Table 6-10.
However, a micro vehicle may apply to the requirements specified in Table 40.

Article 39-2 (Maneuvering Lamp) The maneuvering lamp meeting the requirements specified in
Table 6-31 may be installed on the vehicle (except trailers).

Article 40 (Position Lamp) The position lamp shall be installed on the front of passenger cars
(including the trailer with a length not less than 160 cm) and, if installed, shall meet each of following
requirements.
1. One lamp shall be installed each on the left and right of a vehicle. However, one lamp may be
installed on the micro vehicle with a width of 130 cm or less
2. The color of light shall be white.
3. The requirements of installation and luminous intensity for position lamp shall meet Table 6-11.
However, a micro vehicle may apply to the requirements specified in Table 41.

Article 40-2 (End-out Line Marker Lamp)
(1) For a motor vehicle exceeding 210 cm in width, end-out line marker lamps that meet the criteria
of each of the following Subparagraphs shall be installed.
1. The number specified in the relevant Item shall be installed at the location of the motor vehicle
according to the categories of each Item below. However, one additional lamp may be installed
each on the left and right sides of the vehicle (referring to the left and right sides of any side
falling under one side out of the front and rear sides, or side surfaces; hereinafter the same shall
apply in this Paragraph). In this case, the apparent surface shall be installed to face the direction
determined by the relevant Item, and if an end-out line marker lamp is installed on the side, at

Article 40-3 (Parking Lamp) If installing the parking lamps on a vehicle that is 600 cm or less in
length and 200 cm or less in width, it shall be installed as specified in Table 6-32.

Article 41 (License Plate Lamp) The license plate lamp meeting each of the following requirements
shall be installed on the rear of a vehicle:
1. The color of light shall be white
2. The requirements of installation and brightness intensity of the lamp shall meet Table 6-13.
However, a micro vehicle may apply to the requirements specified in Table 42.
3. It shall illuminate the site of the license plate.

Article 42 (Real Position Lamp) The rear position lamps meeting each of the following requirements
shall be installed on the rear side of a vehicle:
1. One lamp shall be installed each on the left and right of a vehicle. However, rear position lamps
may be installed on the vehicles of the following items in accordance with the following
classification.
A. Vehicles not equipped with end-outline marker lamps falling under any of the followings:
One additional rear position lamp may be installed each on the left and right.
1) Buses
2) Trucks and special purpose vehicles (except rescue vehicles) with GVW exceeding 3.5 tons.
B. Rescue vehicles: One additional rear position lamp may be installed each on the left and right.
C. Micro vehicles with a width of 130 cm or less: One rear position lamp may be installed.
2. The color of the light shall be red.
3. The requirements for installation and luminous intensity of the lamp shall meet Table 6-14.
However, a micro vehicle may be subject to the requirements specified in Table 43.

Article 43 (Stop Lamp)
(1) The stop lamps meeting each of the following requirements shall be installed on the rear side of a
vehicle:
1. One lamp shall be installed each on the left and right of a vehicle. However, stop lamps may be
installed on the vehicles of the following items in accordance with the following classification.
A. Micro vehicles with a width of 130 cm or less: One stop lamp may be installed.
B. Rescue vehicles: One additional stop lamp may be installed each on the left and right.
2. The color of light shall be red.

3. The requirements of installation and luminous intensity of the lamp shall meet Table 6-15.
However, the requirements specified in Table 44 shall be applied to micro vehicles.
(2) Passenger cars, as well as trucks and special purpose vehicles with a GVW of 3.5 tons or less,
shall have auxiliary stop lamps installed on the rear in accordance with each of the following
requirements. However, micro vehicles and trucks with structural limitations that make
installation impossible or equipped with open cargo compartments are exempted.
1. One lamp shall be installed on the median longitudinal plane of the rear of the vehicle. Two
lamps may be installed symmetrically on both sides, if the structure makes it impossible to meet
the requirements.2. The color of light shall be red.
3. The requirements for installation and luminous intensity of the auxiliary stop lamp shall meet
Table 6-16.
(3) Buses as well as trucks and special purpose vehicles with GVW exceeding 3.5 tons may have
auxiliary stop lamps installed on the rear that meet the requirements of each Subparagraph of
Paragraph 2.

Article 44 (Turn Signal Lamp) The turn signal lamps meeting each of the following requirements
shall be installed on the front, rear and side of a vehicle (except the front for a trailer).
1. One lamp shall be installed in the front, rear and left-side and right-side of a vehicle. However,
two additional rear turn signal lamps may be installed in the vehicles except PC, trucks and
special purpose vehicle (except rescue vehicles) with GVW of 3.5 tons or less
2. The color of light shall be amber
3. The requirements for the number, installation and luminous intensity of turn signal lamp shall
meet Table 6-17. However, a micro vehicle may apply to the requirements specified in Table 45.

Article 44-2 (Side Marker Lamp)
(1) For a motor vehicle with a length exceeding 6 meters, side marker lamps that meet requirements
in each of the following Subparagraphs shall be installed.
1. The color of the light shall be amber (amber or red if the rear side-marker lamp is installed on
the side of the vehicle's rearmost part)
2. The criteria of installation and t intensity for side-marker lamps shall meet Table 6-18. However,
the criteria of Table 46 may apply to micro vehicles.
(2) Notwithstanding Paragraph 1, a side-marker lamp that meets the criteria in each Subparagraph of
Paragraph 1 may be installed on a motor vehicle with a length of 6 meters or less.

Article 45 (Hazard Warning Lamp) The hazard warning lamp shall be activated in accordance with
each of following requirements.
1. The hazard warning lamp shall be given by simultaneous operation of the turn signal lamps
2. Hazard warning lamp shall be operated in accordance with Table 6-19. However, a micro vehicle
may apply to the requirements specified in Table 47.

Article 45-2 (Rear-end Collision Alert Lamp) The leading vehicle may generate the rear-end
collision alert lamp to avoid a collision with the following vehicle.
1. The rear-end collision alert lamp shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the direction
indicator lamps.
2. The rear-end collision alert lamp shall be installed as conforming to Table 6-20.

(1) A pintle hook (referring to the towing hook; hereinafter the same shall apply) shall be installed in

(2) The dimensions and installation requirements of the pintle hook required by Paragraph 1 shall

Article 47 (Limitations on Other Lamps)
(1) No red lamps, retro-reflectors, or flashing lamps which may be perceived as turn signal lamps,
shall be installed on the front of a vehicle. However, the requirement is not applicable to the red
lamps used in vehicles carrying explosives, signal lamps installed in the upper side of buses or
buses for transportation of children, and the lamps installed in emergency vehicles.
(2) No lamps or flashing lamps which may be perceived as stop lamps, turn signal lamps, end-out
line marker lamp or side marker lamp shall be installed on the rear of a vehicle. However, the
requirement is not applicable to the lamps installed in buses for transportation of children or the
red lamps used in vehicles carrying explosives.
(3) Lamps or retro-reflectors other than those specified in Article 38, Article 38-2 through Article 38-
5, Article 39, Article 39-2, Article 40, Article 40-2, Article 40-3, Article 41 through Article 44,
Article 44-2, Article 45, Article 45-2, Article 48, Article 49, and Article 58 shall not be installed
in a vehicle, except the following cases:
1. If destination display for buses is installed
2. If the rear-wheel lamps are installed for buses, trucks or special purpose vehicles as conforming
to each of following requirements.A. One white lamp shall be installed each on both sidesB. light source should not be visible3. (Deleted)
4. If work area illumination lamp (trucks or special purpose vehicles) are installed as conforming
to each of following requirements.
A. The lamp shall be designed to be turned off when the vehicle is traveling forward at a speed
exceeding 20 km/h.B. The lamp shall be white color.

Article 48 (Other Regulations for Lamps)
(1) Two or more lamps installed in a vehicle may be combined into one. However, this requirement
is not applicable to the red signal lamps used in vehicles carrying explosives.
(2) (Deleted)
(3) Light source used in the lighting system of a vehicle shall meet the requirements specified in Table
6-21.
(4) Signal lamps meeting each of the following requirements shall be installed in buses for
transportation of children:
1. Two red signal lamps each and two yellow or amber signal lamps each shall be installed on the
front and rear of a vehicle which flash not less than 60 times nor more than 120 times per minute.
2. The red signal lamps shall be installed outward and the yellow signal lamps shall be installed
inward, symmetrical to the longitudinal center line of a vehicle.
3. The front signal lamps shall be installed above windshield as high as possible, and the bottom
of the lens of the rear signal lamps shall be higher than the upper line of the rear window, but
the height of the right and left lamps shall be same.
4. The luminous area of each signal lamp shall be not less than 120cm2.
5. The system shall be wired so that,
A. By the manual operation of the driver, the yellow or amber signal lamps shall flash when the

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)vehicle is making a stop
B. The red signal lamps shall flash when the vehicle is stopped and the door is open for loading
or unloading
C. The yellow or amber signal lamps shall flash when the door is closed to start
D. However, the red and yellow or amber signal lamps shall not flash simultaneously
6. The signal lamps installed on the front and rear of the vehicle shall meet the requirement for
luminous intensity specified in Table 28-2.
(5) The chromaticity of lamps and retro-reflecting devices shall meet the requirements of Table 6-22.

Article 49 (Rear Retro-Reflector, Etc.)
(1) The retro-reflectors meeting each of the following requirements shall be installed on the rear of a
1. One shall be installed on the left and right of a vehicle. However, one may be installed on the
micro vehicle with a width of 130 cm or less
2. The color of reflected light shall be red.
3. The installation requirements of retro-reflectors shall meet Table 6-23. However, a micro vehicle
may apply to the requirements specified in Table 48.
(2) In the rear side of the trailer, a triangular reflector for trailer which conforms to each of the
following shall be installed.
1. One reflector shall be installed each on the left and the right of a vehicle.
2. Reflective light shall be red.
3. The installation of a triangular reflector for the trailer shall meet the requirements of Table 6-24.
(3) In the front side of the trailer, a front reflector for the trailer which conforms to the each of the
following shall be installed.
1. One reflector shall be installed each on the left and the right of a vehicle
2. Reflective light shall be white or colorless.
3. The installation of the front reflector shall meet the requirements of Table 6-25.
(4) The side reflector meeting each of the following requirements shall be installed in the trailer and
the vehicle with a length of 600 cm or more, and if the side reflector is installed in other vehicles,
it shall meet each of the following requirements.
1. The color of the side reflector shall be amber (amber or red if the side reflector is installed on
the side of the vehicle's rearmost).
2. The requirements for installation of the side reflector shall meet Table 6-26. However, a micro
vehicle may apply to the requirements specified in Table 49.
(5) The reflecting performance of reflectors pursuant to Paragraph 1 through Paragraph 4 shall meet
the requirements specified in Table 6-27.
(6) (Not translated)
(7) The rear reflector meeting the requirements specified in Article 112-13 for low-speed vehicles
with a maximum speed not exceeding 40 km/h shall be installed.
(8) The retro-reflecting band meeting the following requirements shall be installed on the side (limited
to the vehicles with a length exceeding 6.0 meters) and rear (limited to the vehicles with a width
exceeding 2.1 meters) of truck/special purpose vehicle with a GVW exceeding 7.5 tons (except
the incomplete vehicle and towing vehicle) or trailer with a GVW exceeding 3.5 tons (except the
incomplete vehicle). However, the retro-reflecting band meeting the following requirements may
be installed to the vehicles except the trailer with a GVW not more than 0.75 tons.
1. The color of reflected light of retro-reflecting band shall meet the following requirements.
A. Front: WhiteB. Side: Yellow or white

2. The installation and reflecting performance of retro-reflecting band shall meet the requirements
specified in Table 32-2.
(9) Notwithstanding Paragraphs 6 and 8, rear reflecting plate/paper and reflecting band may be
installed on the fire truck pursuant to Table 1 Subparagraph 1 Item A of Enforcement Ordinance
of the Act on Management of Firefighting Equipment in accordance with the requirements for
painting and cover pursuant to Article 11 of the Act on Management of Firefighting Equipment.

Article 50 (Devices for Indirect Vision)
(1) Devices for indirect vision applicable to anyone of the following Subparagraphs shall be installed
in a vehicle, so that a driver may be able to check the traffic condition.
1. Devices for indirect vision, using a mirror, shall be installed as specified in Table 5-6 and its
field of view should meet the requirements in Table 5-7. However, in case of micro vehicle,
installation of device for indirect vision and its field of view shall meet the requirements
specified in Table 50.
2. Devices for indirect vision using Camera-monitor system shall be installed as specified in Table
5-6 and Table 5-8, and its field of view should meet the requirements in Table 5-7.
(2) School bus (excluding vehicles with the engines in front of the driver's seat) shall be equipped
with an additional device for indirect vision to identify obstacles in front of the vehicle
(3) A device for indirect vision installed on the left and right of the school shall have the structure
such that the entire length of the observation rod (30 mm in diameter and 1200 mm in height) can
be seen, when installing the observation rod at a point vertically 300 mm away from a longitudinal
direction of vehicle body where entrance is closed latest (for the vehicle body without an entrance,
it refers to a symmetrical point with the location of entrance in vehicle body) and checking the
observation rod at a height of 635 mm above the driver's seating reference point
(4) In addition to the device for indirect vision pursuant to Paragraph 1, if a vehicle is equipped with
optical side mirror having an average curvature radius of at least 200 millimeters and a reflective
surface of at least 10,000 square millimeters or camera-monitor devices and meets the
requirements specified in Paragraph 3, is deemed as complied with the requirements of school
bus.(5) (Deleted)

Article 51 (Wiping System, Etc.)
(1) Each vehicle shall be fitted with wiping and washing systems, defrosting and defogging systems
in the windshield(except the upper deck of double-decked vehicles without a roof) of a vehicle,
and may be fitted with wiping and washing systems, defrosting and defogging systems in the rear
window and other windows if necessary.
(2) The wiping system installed in the windshield of vehicle (except micro vehicle) shall meet each
of the following requirements:1. At least two frequencies
2. The lowest frequency of at least 20 cycles per minute and the higher one of at least 45 cycles per
3. The difference between the highest and the other frequencies shall be at least 15 cycles per
minute.
4. The wiping system shall return to its original position when the operation is stopped.
(3) The wiping system installed in the windshield of a micro vehicle shall meet each of the following
requirements:1. It shall operate at least 40 cycles per minute.

Article 52 (Deleted)

Article 53 (Horn) The horn of a vehicle shall meet each of the following requirements:
1. The horn shall produce a continuous and uniform sound in the same tone.
2. The sound level measured at 2 meters in front of the vehicle and 1.2±0.05 meters high above
ground shall be not less than 90 dB(C).

Article 53-2 (Rear Pedestrian Safety Device)
(1) The vehicle shall be equipped with at least any one of each of following safety devices. However,
the school bus shall be equipped with all the devices applicable to Subparagraph 1 and
Subparagraph 3.
1. Rear camera-monitor system which can see an observation rod (89 millimeters in diameter and
500 millimeters in height) installed in a rectangle on a horizontal place consisting of its left and
right sides composed of the lines parallel to the x-axis from the point of 1,000 mm away in each
of the +/-y directions from the vehicle centerline, and the other two remaining sides composed
of the lines parallel to the y-axis from the point between 300 mm to 2,300 mm from the rear end
of the vehicle along the center line of the vehicle, if the gear shift (including button-type gear)
is positioned in the reverse (R)
2. Audible Warning Sound System notifying the driver of the pedestrian closes to the rear side of
vehicle when the vehicle is driving in rearward direction
3. Rearward-warning sound system notifying the pedestrian of the vehicle in rearward motion.
(2) Audible Warning Sound System shall meet each of the following requirements pursuant to
Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 2.
1. When the gear shift (including button-type gear) is positioned in reverse, detect a detection rod
(76 millimeters in diameter and 1,000 millimeters in height) installed in a rectangle on a
horizontal plane consisting of its left and right sides composed of the lines parallel to the x-axis
from the left and right exterior sides of the vehicle, and the other two remaining sides composed
of the lines parallel to the y-axis from the point between 250 mm to 1,000 mm from the rear end
of the vehicle along the center line of the vehicle, and trigger an audible warning sound to alert
the driver.
2. The audible warning sound pursuant to Subparagraph 1 shall meet each of the following
requirements of Item.
A. The alarm shall be triggered and stopped repeatedly. However, the audible warning sound
may be generated continuously at the closest proximity to the pedestrian.
B. The audible warning sound inside the cabin shall be at least 55 dB(A) and louder than the
motor noise.
(3) Rearward Audible Warning Sound System shall meet each of the following requirements pursuant
to Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 3.
1. The audible warning sound shall be triggered and stopped repeatedly, and the audible warning
sound shall be generated with the same tone and at a regular interval.
2. The loudness of the audible warning sound shall meet each of the following Items when
measured 2 meters test from the rearmost edge of the vehicle.
A. 60 dB(A) or more and 85 dB(A) or less for PC, bus, light-weight & small-sized trucks/special
purpose vehicle
B. 65 dB(A) or more and 90 dB(A) or less for vehicles other than Item A.
3. The audible warning sound tone shall have the highest volume where 1/3 octave band is between

Article 53-3 (Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System (AVAS) for Quiet Road Transport Vehicles
(QRTV)) Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System specified in Table 6-33 shall be installed on the vehicle
of which power generating device is an electric motor such as HEV, EV, and FCV (hereinafter
"QRTV").

Article 53-4 (Child Check System) Buses for transportation of children shall be equipped with a
child check system meeting each of the following requirements.
1. The device shall be a structure that the warning sound system and signal lamps (hazard warning
lamp pursuant to Article 45 or signal lamps pursuant to Article 48 Paragraph 4) are activated, if
not pressing the check button (including a short-range wireless communication contact) installed
near the seat at the last row of the bus within 3 minutes after stopping the bus engine or removing
the ignition key from the operating position.
2. The device shall be a structure that the warning sound system and signal lamps are deactivated
if pressing the check button (including the short-range wireless communication contact) when
the warning sound system and signal lamps pursuant to Subparagraph 1 are activated or if
restarting the bus engine (except that the engine is started by the auxiliary starting system
pursuant to Article 13 Paragraph 6).
3. The warning sound system pursuant to Subparagraph 1 shall meet each of the following
requirements.
A. The warning sound shall be activated and deactivated repeatedly and the warning sound or
voice message of the same tone shall be generated at regular intervals.
B. The warning sound shall be 60 dB(A) or more if measured at a distance of 2 meters from the
front or rear end of the bus.

Article 54 (Speedometer and Odometer)
(1) A speedometer pursuant to Article 110 and an odometer which may display the total traveled
distance shall be installed in each vehicle:
(2) A maximum speed limiting device shall be installed in each of the following vehicles (except
emergency vehicles pursuant to Article 2 Subparagraph 22 of the Road Traffic Act and vehicles
with a maximum speed not exceeding the speed specified in Paragraph 3):
1. Buses (including school buses pursuant to Article 2 Subparagraph 32)
2. Trucks with or special purpose vehicles with a gross vehicle weight exceeding 3.5 (including a
tow vehicle if linked with a trailer)
3. Trucks (including a tow vehicle if linked with a trailer) in which tanks necessary to carry high-
pressure gas pursuant to Article 2 of the Enforcement Ordinance of the High-Pressure Gas Safety
Control Act are installed.4. Low-speed electric vehicles
(3) The maximum speed limiting device required by Paragraph 2 shall be capable of limiting the
maximum speed at a speed set forth below:
1. Each vehicle under Paragraph 2 Subparagraph 1: 110 km/h
2. Each vehicle under Paragraph 2 Subparagraph 2 and Subparagraph 3: 90 km/h
3. Each low-speed electric vehicle under Paragraph 2 Subparagraph 4: 60 km/h
(4) (Deleted)

Article 56 (Tachograph) The scope of vehicles for transportation business which shall be equipped
with a tachograph and its installation requirements shall be subject to Article 55 Paragraph 1 of the
Traffic Safety Act.

Article 56-2 (Event Data Recorder)
(1) “Accidents such as vehicle collision prescribed by Ordinance of MOLIT” in Article 2
Subparagraph 10 of the MVMA refers to the cases where any of the following situations have
occurred.
1. A longitudinal cumulative delta-V of 8 km/h or more is reached within a 0.15 second (for
vehicles that record "delta-V, lateral," where a lateral cumulative delta-V of 8 km/h or more is
reached within a 0.15 second)
2. Deployment of a non-reversible deployable restraint such as an airbag or seat belt pretensioner.
3. Deployment of a safety device (hereinafter the "pedestrian protection system") installed outside
the passenger compartment in order to mitigate injuries to pedestrians, etc., in the event of a
collision with pedestrians or bicycle riders, etc.
(2) "Motor vehicles pursuant to standards prescribed by Ordinance of MOLIT, such as motor vehicle
type, usage, and seating capacity" under Article 29-3 Paragraph 1 of the MVMA refers to the
following motor vehicles.1. Passenger cars (excluding micro passenger cars)2. Buses with gross vehicle weight not exceeding 3.85 tons
3. Trucks with gross vehicle weight not exceeding 3.85 tons (excluding micro trucks and trailers)
(3) The installation standards for EDR under Article 29-3 Paragraph 4 of the MVMA shall comply
with Table 5-25.

Article 57 (Fire Extinguisher) The scope of motor vehicles required to be installed or placed with a
fire extinguisher and the standards of installation and placement shall be subject to Article 11 of the
Act on Installation and Management of Firefighting Systems.

after 12 hours of conditioning at any ambient temperature between −18°C and +52°C.
1. The throttle shall return to the idle position within 1 second from the first removal of the
opposing actuating force by the driver, whenever the driver removes the opposing actuating
force from the accelerator control, or one source of energy returning the throttle to the idle
position is disconnected.
2. In case of the electrical control transmission of accelerator control system, the throttle shall

Article 88 (Instrument Panel) In each passenger car, and in each bus, truck, and special purpose
vehicle with a gross vehicle weight of 4.5 tons or less (except light-weight trucks and light-weight
special purpose vehicles), when the area of the instrument panel, with the exception of each of the
following area, that is within the head impact area is impacted by a 165 mm diameter, 6.8 kg head
form at a relative velocity of 24.2 km/h (19.2 km/h if inflatable restraint system is provided on the
instrument panel on the passenger side), the deceleration of the head form shall not exceed 80 g
continuously for more than 3 milliseconds, and the interior compartment doors, if provided, shall
remain closed. However, it shall not be applied to the micro vehicle.
1. Console assemblies where a radio, gearshift lever or ashtray are installed
2. Areas less than 127 mm inboard from the juncture of the instrument panel attachment to the
body side inner structure
3. Areas from the instrument panel juncture to the windshield if the windshield and the instrument
panel are contactable by the head form simultaneously
4. Areas outboard of any point of tangency on the instrument panel of a head form tangent to and
inboard of a vertical longitudinal plane tangent to the inboard edge of the steering wheel
5. Areas below any point at which a vertical line is tangent to the rearmost surface of the panel

Article 88-2 (Tire) In the event of rapid loss of inflation pressure with a vehicle (except micro PC)
traveling in a straight line at a speed of 97 km/h, each rim shall retain the deflated tire until the vehicle
can be stopped with a controlled braking application without a wheel lock.

Article 88-3 (Tire Pressure Monitoring System) The TPMS installed according to Article 12-2 shall
meet the detailed requirements for performance, malfunction telltale, and detailed standards
determined and announced by the Minister of MOLIT.

Article 89 (Steering Control System)
(1) In each passenger car, and in each bus, truck, and special purpose vehicle with a gross vehicle
weight of 4.5 tons or less, the impact withstanding capability of the steering control system shall
meet each of the following requirements. However, if conforming to the passenger protection
criteria in the event of a frontal offset deformable barrier crash in Table 14 or criteria for a frontal
crash with a fixed barrier in Table 14-7, it is deemed to meet these requirements. It does not apply
to the micro vehicle.
1. When the steering control system is impacted by a body block at a relative velocity of 24.2km/h,
the impact force developed on the chest of the body block transmitted to the steering control
system shall not exceed 1,130 kg. However, the requirement is not applicable to the vehicles in
which the angle of the steering shaft against the horizontal plane exceeds 35 °.
2. When a vehicle (except forward control vehicles) is impacted perpendicularly into a fixed
collision barrier at a relative velocity of 48.3 km/h, the upper end of the steering column and

(2) The steering control system of a vehicle shall meet the detailed requirements for structure,

Article 89-2 (Lane Departure Warning System (LDWS)) Lane departure warning systems installed
pursuant to Article 14-2 shall comply with the standards determined and announced by the Minister
of MOLIT.

Article 90 (Brake System) The brake performance of a motor vehicle shall meet each of the
following requirements. However, for a trailer, this requirement applies to those fitted with a
pneumatic service brake system (including an air boosted hydraulic service brake system).
1. The brake performance of passenger cars shall meet the requirements specified in Table 7.
However, the brake performance of the micro PC shall meet the requirements specified in Table
51.
2. The brake performance of buses, trucks (except trailers) and special purpose vehicles shall meet
the requirements specified in Table 7-2. However, the brake performance of micro trucks and
micro special purpose vehicles shall meet the requirements specified in Table 51.
3. The brake performance of the trailer shall meet the requirements specified in Table 7-3.
4. The brake performance of the vehicle fitted with an anti-lock service brake system shall meet
the requirements specified in Table 7-4. However, the brake performance of the micro vehicle
shall meet the requirements specified in Table 51.
5. The brake performance of the trailer fitted with an anti-lock service brake system shall meet the
requirements specified in Table 7-5.
6. The brake performance of the tow vehicle-trailer when turning fitted with a pneumatic service
brake system (including an air boosted hydraulic service brake system) shall meet the
requirements specified in Table 7-6. However, this requirement does not apply to the tow
vehicle-trailer of a full trailer type with a maximum speed not greater than 60 km, or vehicles
meeting Subparagraph 2 or Subparagraph 3 above.

Article 90-2 (Electronic Stability Control System) The ESC system installed in vehicles (except
micro vehicles) shall meet the detailed requirements for structure, performance, malfunction telltale,
etc. specified in Table 7-7.

Article 90-3 (Advanced Emergency Braking System (AEBS)) AEBS installed in vehicles (except
light-weight buses and micro vehicles) shall meet the requirements specified in each of the following
categories of each Subparagraph.
1. AEBS installed on buses, trucks and special purpose vehicles with a GVW exceeding 3.5 tons:
Requirements of Table 7-8
2. AEBS installed on passenger cars, trucks and special purpose vehicles with a GVW of 3.5 tons
or less: Requirements of Table 7-9

Article 91 (Safety of Flammable Liquid Fuel Systems in the Event of a Crash) The fuel system
of passenger cars, buses with a GVW (gross vehicle weight) of 4.5 tons or less, and trucks with a
GVW of 3.5 tons or less which use flammable liquids for its fuel shall meet Table 10 - Fuel System
crash test standards for flammable liquid vehicles.

Article 91-3 (Safety of High-power Devices in the Event of a Crash) Hybrid vehicles, electric
vehicles, and fuel cell vehicles that fall under any of the following Subparagraphs shall meet the crash
test criteria for high-power devices in Table 11-4.
1. Passenger cars2. Buses with a GVW of 4.5 tons or less3. Trucks with a GVW of 3.5 tons or less

Article 91-4 (Safety of Fuel System in Overturning) Motor vehicles that use flammable liquids as
fuel or that use high-power devices, which fall under any Subparagraph of Article 91-3, shall meet
the static overturning test criteria of Table 11-5 after a crash test.

Article 92 (Roof Structure) The roof of each passenger car (except convertibles) shall be so
constructed that the test device with its lower surface formed as a flat rectangle of 75 cm x 180 cm or
greater shall not move more than 127 mm when it is forced to the roof at a rate not more than 12.7
mm/s within 120 seconds until the force reaches 1.5 times the vehicle weight or 2,270 kg, whichever
is less.

Article 93 (Bumper) In case of passenger cars (except micro PCs), the bumper to meet the safety
standard specific in Table 11-6 shall be installed.

Article 94 (Driver's Vision, Etc.)
(1) Each passenger car and each light-weight bus shall be so constructed that the forward field of
view specified in Table 12 and rearward field of view specified in Article 50 are secured. However,
the requirements specified in Table 12 shall not apply to a micro vehicle.
(2) The light transparency of the windshield [including rear window glass or window for passenger
cars (including passenger cars of a special structure such as convertibles)] and window glasses or
windows to the immediate right and left of the driver shall be not less than 70%, except those area
for sunshade not in the driver's field of view.
(3) The light transparency of all window glasses or windows of school bus shall be not less than 70%

Article 95 (Flammability of Interior Materials) The portions of each of the following components
of vehicle occupant compartments shall not burn at a rate of 102mm per minute or more.
1. Seat cushions, seat backs and seat belts
2. Arm rests, head restraints and sun visors
3. Headlining, floor coverings and mattress covers
4. All trim panels

Article 96 (Rear Underrun Protection Bar) The rear underrun protection bar pursuant to Article 19
Paragraph 4 shall meet the strength requirements specified in Table 13.

Article 97 (Driver's Seat and Passenger Seats)
(1) Each occupant seat (except side-facing seats, or auxiliary folding seats or passenger seats in a bus)
shall withstand the force specified in Subparagraph 1 or Subparagraph 2 with the seat in any
position to which it can be adjusted, or the force in Subparagraph 3 with the seat in the rearmost
position, without being separated from its original position before the force is applied.
1. In the case of the seat without a seat belt assembly attached, the force 20 times the mass of the
seat in a forward and rearward longitudinal direction
2. In the case of the seat with a seat belt assembly attached, the force specified in Subparagraph 1
applied simultaneously with the forces imposed on the seat by the seat belt assembly as specified
in Article 103 Paragraph 3
3. A force that produces a 38 kg.m rearward moment about the seating reference point in the case
of a forward-facing seat, or a force that produces a 38 kg.m forward moment about the seating
reference point in the case of a rearward-facing seat
(2) (Except for seats in a truck and a special purpose vehicle, and for passenger seats in a bus) a
hinged or folding occupant seat or occupant seat back shall be fitted with a self-locking device
for restraining the hinged or folding seat or seat back and a control for releasing that restraining
device.
(3) Once engaged, the restraining device for a seat shall not release or fail when each of the following
force is applied to the restraining device:

2. A rearward longitudinal force equal to 8 times the mass of the hinged or folding portion of the

Article 98 (Seat Back) In each passenger car and each bus for transportation of children, and in each
bus, truck, and special purpose vehicle with a gross vehicle weight of 4.5 tons or less, when the seat
back (or head restraint if installed) within the head impact area is impacted by a 165 mm diameter,
6.8 kg head form at a relative velocity of 24.2 km/h, the deceleration of the head form shall not exceed
80g continuously for more than 3 milliseconds, and the interior compartment doors, if provided, shall
remain closed. However, the requirement is not applicable to each of the following seat backs:
1. A seat back of the seat in the rearmost row
2. A seat back of the side-facing seat3. A seat back of back-to-back seats4. A seat back of the auxiliary folding seat
5. A seat back recognized by Minister of MOLIT as unavoidable in structure
6. A seat back installed in the micro vehicle

Article 99 (Head Restraint) Each head restraint installed in the front seat (except inboard seats) and
the other seats (equipped with head restraint only) of vehicles specified in Article 26 shall meet the
detailed requirements determined by the Minister of MOLIT. However, the requirement is not
applicable to auxiliary folding seat, side-facing seats, or rear-facing seats.

Article 100 (Arm Rest) Each arm rest installed in passenger cars, and in buses, trucks, and special
purpose vehicles with a gross vehicle weight of 4.5 tons or less shall meet at least one of the following
requirements. However, the requirements are not applicable to the arm rests installed in the micro
vehicle and folding type arm rests constructed with energy-absorbing material:
1. The arm rest shall be constructed with energy-absorbing material and shall deflect or collapse
laterally at least 50 mm without permitting contact with any underlying rigid material.
2. Along not less than 50 continuous millimeters of its length, the arm rest shall, when measured
vertically in side elevation, provide at least 50mm of coverage within the pelvic impact area.

Article 101 (Sun Visor) In each passenger car, and in each bus, truck and special purpose vehicle
with a gross weight of 4.5 tons or less, a sun visor meeting the following requirements shall be
provided for each front outboard designated seating position (except inboard seating positions).
However, it shall not be applied to the micro vehicle.
1. The sun visor shall be constructed of or covered with energy-absorbing material.
2. The sun visor mounting within the head impact area shall present no rigid material edge radius
of less than 3.2 mm that is statically contactable by a spherical 165 mm diameter head form.

Article 102 (Occupant Crash Protection)
(1) Passenger cars shall meet the criteria for passenger protection in the event of a crash according to
the category of the following Subparagraphs.
1. Passenger cars with a GVW of 3.5 tons or less (excluding low-speed electric vehicles and micro
passenger cars): The criteria for passenger protection in the event of a frontal offset deformable
barrier crash in Table 14 and the criteria for passenger protection in the event of a side crash in

KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)Table 14-2
2. Passenger cars exceeding a GVW of 3.5 tons (excluding low-speed electric vehicles): The
criteria for passenger protection in the event of a side crash in Table 14-2
(2) Trucks shall meet the criteria for passenger protection in the event of a crash under the category
of the following Subparagraphs. However, in the case where a front-seating vehicle meets the
criteria for full frontal barrier impact in Table 14-7, among the trucks of Subparagraph 1, it shall
be considered to meet the passenger protection criteria for frontal offset deformable barrier crash
in Table 14.
1. Trucks with a GVW of 2.5 tons or less (excluding low-speed electric vehicles and micro trucks):
The criteria for passenger protection in the event of a frontal offset deformable barrier crash in
Table 14 and the criteria for passenger protection in the event of a side crash in Table 14-2
2. Trucks with a GVW exceeding 2.5 tons but not more than 3.5 tons (excluding low-speed electric
vehicles): The criteria for passenger protection in the event of a side crash in Table 14-2
(3) Buses shall meet the criteria for passenger protection in the event of a crash under the category of
the following Subparagraphs. However, in the case where a motor vehicle of Subparagraph 1
meets the criteria for full frontal barrier impact in Table 14-7, it shall be considered to meet the
criteria for perpendicular impact into a fixed collision barrier under Table 14-3.
1. Each bus (except trailer) with a gross vehicle weight of 4.5 tons or less: the body structure criteria
requirement in the crash test specified in Table 14-3
2. Each bus with a gross vehicle weight exceeding 4.5 tons (except double-decked large-sized
buses): the body strength criteria specified in Table 14-4.
(4) A vehicle equipped with an airbag in the front passenger seat shall display a warning label
conforming to the requirements set out in Table 14-5.

Article 102-2 (Pedestrian Protection) Passenger cars, buses, trucks or special purpose vehicles with
GVW not exceeding 4.5 tons shall meet each of the following requirements, except micro vehicles,
buses, trucks or special purpose vehicles in which distance between the center of front wheel axis and
driver's seating reference point it not more than 1,100 mm.
1. Each vehicle shall meet the injury criteria requirement for pedestrian headform specified in Table
14-6 when the pedestrian headform is impacted on the pedestrian head impact zone at the speed
of 35 km/h with an angle of 65 degrees in case of adult headform, or 50 degrees in case of child
headform, downwards on vertical longitudinal plane.
2. When the pedestrian legform is impacted on the pedestrian leg impact zone as follows the injury
criteria requirement for pedestrian legform specified in Table 14-6 shall be met:
A. If the lower bumper reference line at the impact point is below 425 mm above the ground,:
the pedestrian lower legform is impacted on the pedestrian leg impact zone at the speed of 40
km/h.
B. If the lower bumper reference line at the impact point is above 425 mm and below 500 mm
above the ground: the pedestrian lower legform or upper legform is impacted on the pedestrian
leg impact zone at the speed of 40 km/h.
C. If the lower bumper reference line at the impact point is above 500 mm above the ground: the
pedestrian upper legform is impacted on the pedestrian leg impact zone at the speed of 40
km/h.

Article 102-3 (Frontal Impact with Fixed Barrier) Passenger cars and trucks with a GVW not more
than 3.5 tons (except micro vehicle) shall meet the criteria for frontal crash with fixed barrier specified
in Table 14-7.

Article 102-4 (Pole Side Impact) Passenger cars and trucks with a GVW not more than 3.5 tons shall

1. Low-speed electric vehicles2. Micro vehicles

Article 103 (Seat Belt Assembly)
(1) The seat belt assembly installed in a vehicle shall meet the adjustment requirements specified in
Table 15 and static strength specified in Table 16.
(2) (Deleted)
(3) The seat belt assembly anchorage of a vehicle shall meet each of the following requirements:
1. The anchorage for a pelvic restraint of a 2-point seat belt assembly or 3-point seat belt assembly
where a pelvic body block and an upper torso body block are detached shall withstand a 2,270
kg force at least for 10 seconds. However, the anchorage installed in a light-weight vehicle shall
withstand a 1,820 kg force, and the one installed in a bus other than the frontmost seating
positions shall withstand a 300 kg force (or 1,130 kg force for a bus with a gross vehicle weight
of 4.5 tons or less) for at least 0.2 seconds.
2. The anchorage for a 3-point seat belt assembly shall withstand a 1,360 kg force for at least 10
seconds applied simultaneously to a pelvic body block and an upper torso body block. However,
the anchorage installed in a light-weight vehicle shall withstand a 1,100 kg force, and the one
installed in a bus other than the frontmost seating positions shall withstand a 300 kg force (or
690 kg force for a bus with a gross vehicle weight of 4.5 tons or less) for at least 0.2 seconds.
3. For the anchorage for a pelvic restraint of a 2-point or 3-point seat belt assembly, the angle
between the horizontal plane and the plane which is through the seating reference point and the
anchorage of the restraint simultaneously and perpendicular to the vehicle's center plane (the
plane perpendicular to the ground which includes the vehicle's center line) shall be not less than
30 degrees nor more than 75 degrees, and the planes through the anchorages and parallel to the
vehicle's center line shall be located at least 165 mm apart.
4. The anchorage for the upper torso restraint of the 3-point seat belt assembly shall be located
within the acceptable range specified in Table 17. However, the anchorage for the upper torso
restraint in the seats other than first-row seats of school bus, if meeting all of following
requirements, may be installed so that its height can be adjusted in a lower range than specified
in Table 17.
A. The height of the seat belt for the upper torso restraint shall be able to be adjusted with a belt
adjustment device for height, etc.
B. The belt adjustment device for height shall not be moved up regardless of occupant's intention.
(4) (Deleted)

Article 103-2 (Child Seat Anchorage System) The child seat anchorage system installed in each
passenger car (except micro PC) shall meet each of the following requirements.
1. It shall conform to the requirements in Article 27-2.
2. The tether anchorage shall be of a structure to withstand the application of a force of 816 kg (to
the static force application device (SFAD)) in a forward direction for a minimum of 0.2 seconds,
and (the loading point of the SFAD) shall not be displaced more than 125mm.
3. The lower anchorages shall be of a structure to withstand the application of a force of 816 kg in
a forward direction and 510 kg in a lateral direction in a vertical longitudinal plane that is 75
degrees to either side of a vertical longitudinal plane for a minimum of 0.2 seconds, and any

Article 104 (Side Door)
(1) Each side door of a passenger car (except micro PC) shall meet at least one of the following
requirements when a load is applied to the side door with a loading device consisting of a rigid
steel cylinder or semicylinder 305 mm in diameter at a rate of not more than 12.7 mm per second:
1. when tested with the seat adjacent to the side door removed;
A. The average crush resistance until the deformation reaches 152mm shall be not less than 0.83
times the vehicle weight or 10,000 Newton, whichever is less.
B. The average crush resistance until the deformation reaches 305mm shall be not less than 1.3
times the vehicle weight or 15,569 Newton, whichever is less.
C. The peak crush resistance until the deformation reaches 457mm shall be not less than 2 times
the vehicle weight or 31,138 Newton, whichever is less.
2. when tested with the seat adjacent to the side door installed;
A. The average crush resistance until the deformation reaches 152mm shall be not less than 0.83
times the vehicle weight or 10,000 Newton, whichever is less.
B. The average crush resistance until the deformation reaches 305mm shall be not less than 1.63
times the vehicle weight or 19,460 Newton, whichever is less.
C. The peak crush resistance until the deformation reaches 457mm shall be not less than 3.5
times the vehicle weight or 53,378 Newton, whichever is less.
(2) The door locks and the door retention components of the side door and the back door designed to
accommodate passenger loading or cargo loading of a vehicle, except for micro vehicles, medium-
sized buses and large-sized buses, shall meet each of the following requirements. However, side
doors which are equipped with wheelchair lifts, folding doors, roll-up doors, and doors that are
designed to be easily attached to or removed from vehicles need not conform to the requirements.
1. Hinged doors:
A. Each door latch and striker assembly shall be provided with two positions consisting of a
fully latched position and a secondary latched position.
B. The door latch and striker assembly, when in the fully latched position, shall withstand a load
of 11,000 Newton in the direction perpendicular to the face of the latch and a load of 9,000
Newton in the direction of the forkbolt opening and parallel to the face of the latch separately,
and back door shall also withstand a load of 9,000 Newton in a direction orthogonal to the
direction perpendicular to the face of the latch and the direction of the forkbolt opening and
parallel to the face of the latch. However, the door and striker assembly installed in light-
weight vehicles shall withstand a longitudinal load of 8,800 Newton and a transverse load of
7,200 Newton, or a vertical load of 7,200 Newton for the back door.
C. The door latch shall not disengage from the fully latched position when a longitudinal and
transverse inertia load of 30 g is applied to the door latch system, and when a longitudinal
inertia load of 30 g is applied to the door latch system of the back door.
D. The door latch and striker assembly, when in the secondary latched position, shall withstand
a longitudinal load and a transverse load of 4,500 Newton. However, the door and striker
assembly installed in light-weight vehicles shall withstand a longitudinal load and a transverse
load of 3,600 Newton.
E. Each door hinge system shall withstand a longitudinal load of 11,000 Newton and a transverse
load of 9,000 Newton, and a longitudinal load of 9,000 Newton for the back door. However,
the system installed in light-weight vehicles shall withstand a longitudinal load of 8,800
Newton and a transverse load of 7,200 Newton, and a longitudinal load of 7,200 Newton for
the back door.

KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
2. For each sliding door (except for light-weight vehicles):
A. Door latches shall have a fully latched position and intermediate latching position.
B. Door latches shall withstand a longitudinal load of 11,000 Newton and a transverse load of
9,000 Newton in the fully latched position.
C. The door latch assembly shall not disengage from the fully latched position when a
longitudinal or transverse load of 30 g is applied to the door latch system.
D. Door latches shall withstand a longitudinal load of 4,500 Newton and a transverse load of
4,500 Newton in the intermediate latched position.
E. The door, while in the closed position, shall not separate from the door frame more than 100
mm when an outward transverse load of 9,000 Newton is applied to the load-bearing members
at the opposite edges of the door, and the total transverse displacement of each of the loading
devices shall be limited to 300 mm.
(3) The door latch system and the door hinge system of the side door and the back door of a micro
vehicle shall meet each of the following requirements.
1. The door latch system shall be in the fully latched position.
2. The door latch system, when in the fully latched position, shall withstand a load of 8,800 Newton
in the direction perpendicular to the face of the latch system and a load of 7,200 Newton in the
fork-bolt opening direction and parallel to the face of the latch system separately. In this case,
the door latch system of back door shall also withstand a load of 7,200 Newton in the direction
perpendicular to the face of the latch system and the in a direction orthogonal to fork-bolt
direction opening and parallel to the face of the latch system.
3. The door latch system shall not disengage from the fully latched position when a longitudinal
and transverse inertia load of 30 g is applied to the door latch system. In this case, the door latch
system of back door shall also not disengage from the fully latched position when a longitudinal
inertia load of 30g is applied to the door latch system.
4. Each door hinge system shall withstand a longitudinal load of 8,800 Newton and a transverse
load of 7,200 Newton. In this case, the hinge system of back door shall also withstand a
longitudinal load of 7,200 Newton.
5. The door, while in the fully closed position, shall withstand a transverse load of 2,000 Newton
either at the same height with the center of door or the seating reference point, or at the height
not more than 500 mm vertically. In this case, the deformation of outside of the vehicle is
allowed.

Article 105 (Windshield Mounting and Windshield Zone Intrusion)
(1) The window glass specified in Article 34 Paragraph 1 shall have mechanical strength determined
by the Minister of MOLIT.
(2) The windshield of a passenger car, when it is traveling longitudinally forward at a speed of 48.3
km/h impacts a fixed collision barrier that is perpendicular to the line of travel of the vehicle, shall
meet each of the following requirements:
1. Vehicles fitted with passive restraint systems such as airbags or automatic seat belts shall retain
not less than 50% of the portion of the windshield periphery on each side of the vehicle
longitudinal centerline.
2. Vehicles not fitted with passive restraint systems shall retain not less than 75% of the windshield
periphery.
3. No part of the vehicle outside the occupant compartment, except windshield molding and other
components designed to be normally in contact with the windshield, shall penetrate the protected
zone template, affixed according to Table 18, to a depth of more than 6.3 mm, and no such part
of a vehicle shall penetrate the inner surface of that portion of the windshield, within the daylight

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)opening, below the protected zone.
(3) The requirements in Paragraph 2 are not applicable to each of the following vehicles:
1. Open-body-type vehicles with fold-down or removable windshields
2. Forward control vehicles3. Light-weight vehicles

Article 106 (Engine Power) The vehicle (except micro vehicles) engine power (including a traction
motor, internal combustion engine and fuel cell) shall meet each of the following requirements:
1. The permissible specification tolerance of the internal combustion engine power and the
corresponding engine speed declared shall not exceed each of the following limits. However, +/-
5% shall apply for production vehicles:A. For maximum power: +/-2%B. For other power: +/-4%C. Engine speed: +/-1.5%
2. The permissible specification tolerance of the traction motor power and the corresponding
engine speed declared shall not exceed each of the following limits. However, -5% shall apply
for production vehicles:A. For maximum power: +/-5%
B. For other power (excluding maximum 30 minutes power): +/-5%
C. Engine speed: +/-2%D. Maximum 30 minutes power: +/-5%.
3. The permissible specification tolerance for maximum power of the fuel cell used for a vehicle
shall not exceed -5%.
4. The requirements for the engine power specified in Article 63-2 are applied to the internal
combustion engine of a micro vehicle.

Article 107 (Electromagnetic Compatibility) The electromagnetic compatibility of a vehicle and
electric/electronic components installed in a vehicle shall comply with the requirements specified in
Table 24 for EMC and EMI.

Article 108 (Interior Compartment Door) In each passenger car, and in each bus, truck and special
purpose vehicle (except light-weight trucks and light-weight special purpose vehicles) with a gross
vehicle weight of 4.5 tons or less, each interior compartment door assembly located in an instrument
panel, seat back, or side panel adjacent to a designated seating position shall meet the requirements
of either Subparagraph 1 and Subparagraph 2 or Subparagraph 1 and Subparagraph 3 below when
tested with the locking device in an unlocked position. However, it shall not be applied to the micro
vehicle:
1. When the interior compartment door latch system is subjected to an inertia load of 10 g in a
vertical direction and a horizontal transverse direction, the interior compartment door shall
remain closed.
2. When the vehicle is impacted perpendicularly into a fixed collision barrier at a forward
longitudinal velocity of 48.3 km/h (40 km/h for buses), the interior compartment door shall
remain closed.
3. When the interior compartment door latch system is subjected to a horizontal inertia load of 30g
in a longitudinal direction, the interior compartment door shall remain closed.

Article 109 (Windshield Wiping, Etc.)
(1) The windshield wiping and washing systems, defrosting and defogging systems installed in each
passenger car (except micro vehicle) and each light-weight bus shall meet each of the following
requirements:
1. The windshield wiping system shall meet the requirements of Article 51 Paragraph 2 and each
of the following requirements:
A. The windshield wiping system shall wipe at least 98% of Area A and at least 80% of Area B
as established by Table 25.
B. The windshield wiping system shall be operable at least for 2 minutes after the vehicle is
conditioned in the ambient temperature of –18℃ for 4 hours.
C. When air is applied to the windshield with a relative velocity of either 80% of the maximum
speed or 120 km/h the windshield wiping system shall wipe at least 98% of Area A as
established by Table 25.
2. The defrosting system shall meet each of the following requirements when activated after the
vehicle is conditioned in the ambient temperature of –18℃ for 10 hours:
A. The defrosting system shall defrost at least 80% of Area A as established by Table 25 within
20 minutes after activation.
B. The defrosting system shall defrost Area A as established by Table 25 and at least 80% of the
windshield symmetrical to the longitudinal direction of a vehicle within 25 minutes after
activation.
C. The defrosting system shall defrost at least 95% of Area B as established by Table 25 within
40 minutes after activation.
3. The defogging system shall defog at least 90% of Area A and at least 80% of Area B as
established by Table 25 when activated within 10 minutes after the vehicle is conditioned in the
ambient temperature of –3℃ for 10 hours.
4. The washing system shall meet each of the following requirements:
A. The washing system shall be able to inject sufficient amount of washer fluid necessary to
wash at least 60% of Area A as established by Table 25 when the wiping system is activated
for 10 cycles at a maximum speed.
B. The washing system shall be operable when activated after the vehicle is conditioned in the
ambient temperature of –18℃ for 4 hours.

(2) The windshield wiping and washing systems installed in the micro vehicle shall meet each of the

2. The washing system shall meet each of the following requirements:

Article 110 (Speedometer)
(1) The speedometer display installed in a vehicle shall meet each of the following requirements:
1. The speedometer display shall be situated in the driver's direct field of vision and shall be clearly
legible both by day and by night.
2. The range of speeds indicated shall include the maximum speed given by the manufacturer for
the type of vehicle.
3. The graduations shall be of 1, 2, 5, or 10 km/h (the indicated speed value intervals need not be
uniform), and the values of the speed shall be indicated on the display as follows:
A. When the highest value on the display does not exceed 200 km/h, speed values shall be
indicated at intervals not exceeding 20 km/h.
B. When the maximum value on the display exceeds 200 km/h, then the speed values shall be
indicated at intervals not exceeding 30 km/h.
(2) The tolerance of the speedometer installed in a vehicle shall conform to the following formula at
the speed not less than 25km/h on an even road:
0=< V₁－V₂=< V₂/10＋6 (km/h)V₁: Indicating speed (km/h)V₂: Sctual speed (km/h)

Article 110-2 (Maximum Speed Limiter) The maximum speed limiter shall meet the requirements
specified in Table 26.

Section 3 Safety Standards For Automated Driving System

Article 111 (Automated Driving System) The types of Automated driving system are specified as
follows.
A. "Partially automated driving system" means a device that can operate a vehicle under specified
conditions but requires driver intervention if necessary, such as operating constraints, etc.
B. "Conditionally and fully automated driving system" means a device that can operate a vehicle
without driver intervention under specified conditions.
C. "Fully automated driving system" means a device that can operate a vehicle without driver
intervention in all domains.

Article 111-2 (Setting Operation Design Domain)

KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

automated driving system is designed to properly and safely operate in the specific conditions.
(2) The ODD should include the following information for automated driving.
1. Driving environment such as roadway types, weather conditions, etc.
2. Other domain constraints3. Other conditions for safe driving

Article 111-3 (Partially Automated Driving System of PC) The safety standard for partially
automated driving system installed on the PC shall be as shown in Table 27.

Section 4 Performance Test Standards

Article 112 (Performance Tests Standards for Parts or Systems) The relevant provisions of
Chapter 2 and this Chapter shall apply mutatis mutandis to the test standards for safety and
performance of the parts or systems used in a motor vehicle pursuant to Article 32 Paragraph 1 of the
MVMA.

CHAPTER 3-2 SAFETY STANDARDS FOR PARTS

Article 112-2 (Brake Hose) The brake hose used for motor vehicles (except micro vehicles) shall
meet the requirements of Table 30-4 and other brake hoses except air brake hose shall be of an integral
structure which can't be disassembled.

Article 112-3 (Seat Belt Assembly) The seat belt used in motor vehicles shall meet the requirements
of Table 16.

Article 112-4 (Lamp) The head lamp used in motor vehicles (except micro vehicles) shall meet the
requirements of the luminous intensity under Table 6-3 to 6-5 and chromaticity under Table 6-22.

Article 112-5 (Rear Reflex Reflector) The rear reflex reflector (including auxiliary reflector) used
in motor vehicles (except micro vehicles) shall meet each of following requirements
1. The shape of illuminating surfaces of rear reflex reflector shall not be a triangle. However trailer
shall be exempted.
2. The color of reflected light of rear reflex reflector shall be red. However auxiliary retro-reflector
may be yellow or amber.
3. The reflecting performance of rear reflex reflector shall meet the requirements specified in Table
6-27

Article 112-6 (Rear Underrun Protection Bar) Rear underrun protection bar used in motor vehicles
shall meet the requirements specified in Table 13.

Article 112-7 (Windows) The windows used in a vehicle (except micro vehicles) shall meet the
requirements of Article 105 Paragraph 1.

Article 112-8 (Warning Triangle) The warning triangle used in a vehicle (except micro vehicles)
shall meet the requirements specified in Table 30-5.

Article 112-9 (Rear Reflecting Plate and Paper) The rear reflecting plate used in a vehicle shall

2. The reflecting light in reflecting part shall be yellow or red and the reflecting light in fluorescent
parts shall be red.

Article 112-10 (Brake Lining) The brake lining used in a vehicle (except micro vehicles) shall meet
the requirements specified in Table 30-6.

Article 112-11 (Wheels) The wheels used in a vehicle shall meet the requirements specified in Table
30-7. However, it shall not be applied to the micro vehicle.

Article 112-12 (Reflecting Band) The reflecting band used in a vehicle shall meet the requirements
specified in Table 32-2.

Article 112-13 (Rear Marking Plates for Low-Speed Vehicle) The vehicle with a max speed of 40
km/h or less shall equip with the rear marking plates for low-speed vehicle and its shape and reflecting
performance shall meet the requirements specified in Table 30-8.

Article 112-14 (Traction Batteries Used in Electric Vehicles, Etc.) Traction batteries used in
electric vehicles and motorcycles using electric energy as power source (excluding motorcycles using
electric energy generated from hydrogen) shall comply with the standards specified in each
Subparagraph of Article 18-3.

CHAPTER 4 SUPPLEMENTS

Article 113 (Designated Seating Capacity and Maximum Loading Capacity)
(1) The designated seating capacity or maximum loading capacity of a vehicle shall be within the
limit conforming to the requirements as specified in Chapter 2 Section 1 and Chapter 3.
(2) The seating capacity or the maximum loading capacity of a motorcycle shall be within the limit
conforming to the requirements as specified in Chapter 2 Section 2 and the following
requirements.1. Seating capacity:
A. For two-wheeled type or three-wheeled type: two persons or less,
B. For four-wheeled type: one person2. Maximum loading capacityA. For two-wheeled type: 60 kg or lessB. For four-wheeled type: 100 kg or less

Article 114 (Exceptions to Standards)
(1) The Minister of MOLIT may apply the standards specified in Table 31 regarding the length, width,
maximum stable inclination angle, and minimum turning radius to press vehicles, vehicles
transporting standardized goods that cannot be separated for transport, vehicles with a maximum
speed of less than 25 km/h, double-deck large-sized buses (limited to a specified license pursuant
to Article 17 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 1 Item A 2) of the Enforcement Regulations of Passenger
Transport Service Act), and other special purpose vehicles.
(2) Motor vehicles with a maximum speed of less than 25 km/h are not governed by Article 12-2,
Article 13 Paragraph 2, Article 14-2, Article 15, Article 15-2, Article 15-3, Article 16, Article 22,

(3) In consideration of the purpose of manufacture, application and features of a vehicle, Minister of

relieved of its observance of other regulations related to the operation of the vehicles such as, but
not limited to, the Road Acts and the Road Traffic Acts.
(6) (Deleted)
(7) The minister of MOLIT may notify foreign safety and performance standards by each country
which may be regarded as more stringent than the ones in the Standards, and in this case, the
manufacturer's test report for the foreign standards notified may be substituted for the one for this
safety standards.
(8) The regulations are not applied to the system, such as shock absorber or sand sprayer, temporarily
fixed on a vehicle for public purpose for road repair, snow removal, etc.
(9) For module trailers, the following regulations shall not apply; Article 4 Paragraph 1
Subparagraphs 1, Subparagraph 2, Article 6, Article 7, Article 12, Article 15 and Article 90

provisions shall not apply; Articles 35, Article 36, Article 38 and Article 40 through Article 44
(11) For the vehicles subjected to the exceptions to standard for length and width pursuant to
Paragraph 1, Paragraph 9 and Paragraph 10 (except articulated buses, sidewalk vehicles,
environmental measurement vehicles, and double decked buses), retroactive reflecting bands shall
be attached on the left, right and rear sides of the vehicle as specified in Table 32-2 for easily
viewable from outside, and its applicable identification shall be made.
(12) For low-speed electric vehicles the following provisions shall not apply; Article 12-2, Article
15-2 and Article 87, Article 88, Article 88-2, Article 88-3, Article 89 Paragraph 1, Article 90-2,

requirements notwithstanding the requirements in Article 48 Paragraph 3, Article 51, Article 109
Subparagraph 1 Subparagraph 2 and Subparagraph 4, Table 7 Subparagraph 4, Subparagraph 6
and Subparagraph 8.
(13) In the event that the FTAs agreed upon with foreign countries concerning the safety standards is
enforced, the foreign safety standards recognized pursuant to the corresponding FTA shall be
considered to be complied with the Regulation notwithstanding the requirements of the
Regulation. In this case, the Minister of MOLIT may establish and notify the details.
(14) Amphibious vehicles may be granted exceptions to the applicable safety standards according to
the classifications specified in the following subparagraphs. In such cases, the Minister of MOLIT
may impose necessary conditions for their operation.
1. Height of the room for standing pursuant to Article 28 Paragraph 1: 168 cm or more.
