Article 114-2 (Exception to Device Standards) In the event that a new system superior to the system
(except the device for the warning sound system and signal lamps pursuant to Article 53-4
Subparagraph 1 and 2) as specified by these standards or a new system to secure safety is installed in
a vehicle, the Minister of MOLIT may allow installation of the system not specified by these standards.

Article 115 (Tolerance of Specifications) In the event that the specifications of structures and
systems declared by manufacturer, etc. for the manufactured, assembled, or imported vehicle defer
from the those specified by the Regulation, the Minister of MOLIT may acknowledge the deviation
as being complied with the Regulation if the deviation is within the tolerance specified in Table 3 3.

Article 116 (Test Procedures) The Minister of MOLIT may establish the detailed requirements and
test procedures necessary for the implementation of the standards of the regulation and post it through
a Ministerial Notice.

Requirements for Identification and Performance of Pneumatic Tire (Article 12 Paragraph 1)

I. Identification, structure and performance requirements of pneumatic tire

1. Identification of pneumatic tire

b) Nominal aspect ratio (ratio of the width to the height of a tire)
c) Inner structure composed of tire
d) Rim diameter expressed either in inches (numbers of 100 or less) or in millimeters (numbers

Remark)
1. The name of each part consisting of tire is as followings.
A. "Carcass" means a cord layers to form tire structure.
B. "Tread" means a rubber layer part of tire which comes into contact with the ground.
C. "Bead" means a part of tire made of steel wires wrapped by rubber to fit the rim and hold
the tire
D. "Belt" means a part of tire, located between the tread and carcass of radial tire, which
has the function of reinforcement which increases the tread strength by tightening the
carcass in the circumferential direction and increases the driving stability by widening
the tire tread in contact with the road.
E. "Cord" means the textile strands or steel strands forming a rubber layer such as carcass
and belt, etc.
F. "Sidewall means a rubber layer between the tread and the bead.
G. "Inner liner" means a rubber layer with high air tightness which is attached inside the
carcass to maintain the inflation pressure for tubeless tire.
2. "Radial tire" means a pneumatic-tire structure in which the ply cords extend to the beads
and are laid substantially at 90° to the center line of the tread, the carcass being stabilized
by an essentially inextensible circumferential belt. (Refer to Figure 1)

3. "Tubeless tire" means a tire designed not to use a tube when fitting the tire into the wheel.
4. "Reinforced (Extra Load) tire" means a pneumatic-tire structure in which the carcass is
more resistant than that of the corresponding standard tire.
5. "Snow tire" means a tire whose tread pattern and whose material or structure are primarily
designed to ensure in snow a starting or driving performance better than that of an ordinary
(road-type) tire.
6. "Spare tire" means a tire, manufactured for the temporary use, whose weight and volume is
reduced, where the tire fitted in the vehicle cannot be used due to the failure such as damage.
There is the folding spare tire which is carried in the folded state and T-type spare tire which
has the less section and higher inflation pressures than normal standard tire.
7. "HIWAY TREAD-J (HW-J)" means the symbol of Highway Tread-J to identify a tire with
a thin groove for the use for mid-sized and large sized truck and bus.
8. "EXTRA HEAVY TREAD (EHT)" means the symbol of Extra Heavy Tread to identify a
tire with a deep groove for the use for mid-sized and large sized truck and bus.
9. "Bias tire" means a pneumatic-tire structure in which the ply cords extend to the beads and
are laid substantially less than 90° to the center line of the tread (Refer to figure 2)

Figure 2.

5) Tire model name
6) Manufacture time (Week and Year): The manufacturer year is identified as the first two
digits for "week" and the last two digits for "year". Ex) 4012: 40th week of 2012
7) Manufacture country

2. Tire structure requirements
A. The tire load in the loaded state shall not exceed the maximum load rating specified by the tire
manufacturerB. Maximum allowable speed shall be identified in a tire
C. The maximum allowable speed shall be not less than the maximum speed of the vehicle
concerned, except the following cases1) Spare tire2) Winter tire
3) Professional off-road tire with a tread pattern designed under special conditions
D. There shall be no crack on the tire or cord layers exposed, and the tread depth shall be maintained
more than 1.6mm around the tire.

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)3) Endurance performance requirement 'a

Figure 5. Endurance and High speed performance tester

a) There shall be no visual evidence of tread, sidewall, rubber layer, cord, inner liner, belt or
bead unseating, chunking, broken cords, cracking, or open splices.
b) The tire pressure at the end of the test shall not be less than each of following initial
pressures.(1) PC: 180kPa(2) T-type spare tire: 360kPa(3) Reinforced or extra load tire: 220kPa
(4) Other tires: The inflation pressure corresponding to maximum load (If it is different
depending on single wheel or double wheels, the inflation pressure corresponding to
maximum load when double wheel is used)Remark)
1. Test condition and procedures for Endurance performance requirement A is
determined and notified by the Minister of MOLIT.
2. "Separation" means a breaking down of bond or a parting of tread, bead, sidewall,
cord, ply, belt or inner liner from adjacent components.
3. "Chunking" means the breaking away of pieces of rubber from the tread pattern.
4. "Cracking" means any parting of the rubber within the tread, sidewall, or inner liner
of the tire.
5. "Open splice" means any parting at any junction of tread, sidewall, or inner liner

4) High speed performance requirements 'a
a) There shall be no visual evidence of tread, sidewall, rubber layer, cord, innerliner, belt
or bead unseating, chunking, broken cords, cracking, or open splices.
b) The tire pressure at the end of the test shall not be less than each of following initial
pressures(1) PC: 220kPa(2) T-type spare tire: 400kPa(3) Reinforced or extra load tire: 260kPa
(4) Other tires: The inflation pressure corresponding to maximum load (If it is different
depending on single wheel or double wheels, the inflation pressure corresponding to
maximum load when double wheel is used)
Remark) Test condition and procedures for high-speed performance requirement 'a are
determined and notified by the Minister of MOLIT.

Notes:
1. The identification of controls shall be visible to the driver restrained by the seat belt assembly and,
except the controls listed below, shall appear to the driver perceptually upright when the control is
in the off position:
A. A master lighting switch or headlamp/rear position lamp control that adjust control and display
illumination by means of rotation
B. Any other rotating control that does not have an off position
C. A horn control
2. Words or symbols in addition to the required symbol, word or abbreviation may be used at the
manufacturer's discretion for the purpose of clarity.
3. Identification shall be provided for each function of any automatic vehicle speed system control
and any heating and air conditioning system control, and for the extreme positions of any such
control that regulates a function over a quantitative range. If color coding is used to identify the
extreme positions of a temperature control, the hot extreme shall be identified by the color red and
the cold extreme by the color blue.
4. The identification of controls which require illumination shall be capable of being illuminated
whenever the headlamps are activated. However, this requirement does not apply to controls
mounted on the upper area of the instrument panel, steering column, floor, and floor console.
5. The identification for engine start and stop may be used when engine control is separate from the
key locking system.
6. Control identification for a heating and air conditioning system and fan need not be illuminated for
buses, trucks and special purpose vehicles with a gross vehicle weight exceeding 4.5 tons.
7. Separate identification or illumination is not required for the control if it is controlled by the master
lighting switch, and the tell-tale of master lighting switch may not be installed if the instrument
panel lights are lit on activation of the master lighting switch.
8. Words or symbols in addition to the required symbol, word or abbreviation may be used at the
manufacturer's discretion for the purpose of clarity, and the manufacturer may determine the telltale
for eco indicator.
9. The identification of tell-tales which require illumination shall be capable of being illuminated
whenever the headlamps are activated.
10. The identification of a telltale shall be in a color that stands out clearly against the background.

11. A telltale shall not emit light except when identifying the malfunction or vehicle condition for
whose indication it is designed or during a bulb check upon vehicle starting.
12. The identifying symbol of hazard warning telltale is not required when arrows of turn signal
telltales are used as hazard warning telltale.
13. "제동공기" or "Brake Air" may be used as Identifying Words for brake air pressure malfunction
telltale.
14. The manufacturer may choose the color of the TPMS telltale, ESC system malfunction and ESC
system Off telltales if the vehicle is not subject to the installation of the TPMS and ESC system
according to Article 12-2 and Article 15-2.
15. The appearance of a vehicle for the low tire pressure may be revised to show actual appearance
better, in case of TPMS telltale,
16. If a single tell-tale is used to indicate more than one brake system condition, the brake system
malfunction symbol shall be used.
17. If a single tell-tale is used to indicate the "airbag malfunction telltale" and the "side airbag
malfunction telltale", the "airbag malfunction telltale" shall be used.
18. The identification on the common space shall comply with each of the following requirements.
A. The identification for the following tell-tales (hereinafter "major tell-tales") shall not be shown
in the same common space.1) Tell-tale for the brake system malfunction2) Tell-tale for headlamp driving beam3) Tell-tale for direction indicator4) Tell-tale for seat belts of front seats
B. When the underlying condition exists for actuation of two or more tell-tales, the tell-tales shall
be identified as specified below. However, if the major tell-tales and others are displayed in a
common space it shall displace any other symbol in such common space if the underlying
condition exists for its activation.
1) The information shall be repeated automatically in sequence.
2) The information shall be indicated in the order or methods selected by the driver.
C. With the exception of major tell-tales, the information may be cancellable automatically or
manually.
19. Combination of the engine oil pressure symbol and the engine coolant temperature symbol in a
single tell-tale is permitted.
20. The symbol of the following tell-tales may be shown in other colours.
A. Tell-tale for the symbol of headlamp passing beams
B. Tell-tale for engine oil pressure symbol
C. Tell-tale for engine coolant temperature symbol
D. Tell-tale for electrical charging condition
E. Tell-tale for fuel levelF. Tell-tale for headlamp driving beamG. Position lampH. Tell-tale for seat belt of rear seatsI. Master lighting switch
21. Letter "D" (indicating the forward transmission gear of automatic transmission), if necessary, may
be identified by other alphanumeric character(s), number(s) or symbol(s) chosen by the
manufacturer to indicate additional selection modes.

Brake Performance and Control Force of Parking Brake System
(Article 15 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 12) <revised 03.2.25>

1. Brake performance and control force of parking brake system
Requirements1. Test Vehicle Weightunloaded state with a driver seated2. Control Force Passenger CarFoot-operated: 60kg or lessHand-operated: 40kg or less
Other VehiclesFoot operated: 70kg or lessHand-operated: 50kg or less3. Brake performance
The parking brake system shall be capable of holding the vehicle stationary
on a grade of 11o30' or more, or brake performance shall be not less than 20%
of vehicle weight.

2. Requirements for the electric transmission of the parking brake system
A. Brake performance and control force of parking brake system set forth in Subparagraph 1 above
shall be met.
B. In the case of a failure within the electric transmission, any unintended actuation of the parking
braking system shall be prevented.
C. In the case of a break in the wiring within the electric control transmission external to the electric
control unit(s) (and excluding the energy supply, and limited to the wiring connecting the
control(s) and the electric control unit(s) in the case of passenger cars and trucks with GVW not
greater than 3.5 tons (except trailers) and special purpose vehicles), or a failure in the control,
the following criteria shall be met:
(1) it shall remain possible to apply the parking braking system from the driver's seat, and thereby
be capable of holding the laden vehicle stationary on an 8% up or down gradient.
(2) Alternatively, in the case that the requirement in (1) cannot be met, an automatic actuation
of the parking brake is allowed when the vehicle is stationary, provided that the performance
in (1) is achieved and, once applied, the parking brake remains engaged independently of the
status of the ignition (start) switch. In this alternative, the parking brake shall be automatically
released as soon as the driver starts to set the vehicle in motion again. For buses, trucks with
a gross vehicle weight exceeding 3.5 tons (excluding trailers) and special purpose vehicles it
shall also be possible to release the parking braking system, if necessary by the use of tools
and/or an auxiliary device carried/fitted on the vehicle.
(3) For passenger cars, trucks with a gross vehicle weight of 3.5 tons or less (excluding a trailer)
and special purpose vehicles the manual transmission or the automatic transmission (park
position) may be used to achieve or assist in achieving the above performance in (1).
D. A break or a failure as specified in C above shall be signaled to the driver by a warning signal
positioned at a location easily recognizable by a driver in the driver's seat and sufficiently bright,
and it shall meet the following requirements:
(1) yellow warning signal shall be lit.
(2) the red warning signal shall flash as long as the electric control of the parking brake system
is in the "on" (activated) position and the ignition (start) switch is in the "on" (run) position
including a period of not less than 10 seconds thereafter.
E. Where actuation of the parking brake is normally indicated by a separate red warning signal the
requirement in D(2) shall be met.

Performance Requirement of Break Assist System (BAS)
(Article 15 Paragraph 12)

1. In case of a system which detects an emergency braking condition based on the brake pedal force,
the following requirements of each item shall be met.
A. the pedal force to cause full cycling of the ABS with BAS in operation shall be less than the
pedal force required without BAS in operation.
B. the pedal force, in case of BAS in operation, shall meet the following requirements.
1) FABS,min ≤ FABS ≤ FABS,max , where2) FABS,max = FT + (FABS,extrapolated - FT) * 0.63) FABS,min = FT + (FABS,extrapolated - FT) * 0.2

Figure 1.

Note:
1) t0: the moment when the brake pedal force reaches 20N after braking commences.
2) FT: the threshold force to activate BAS
3) FABS,min: minimum of FABS
4) FABS: the minimum pedal force that has to be applied for a given vehicle in order to achieve
maximum deceleration which indicates that ABS is full cycling.
5) FABS,max: maximum of FABS
6) FABS,extrapolated: The value of brake pedal force "F", at the point of intersection between the
straight line which is drawn from the origin through the point FT, aT and a horizontal line
defined by a = aABS.
7) aABS: the deceleration for a given vehicle at which ABS cycling commences
8) PABS: the brake pressure at which ABS cycling commences
9) aT: the threshold deceleration to activate BAS
10) PT: the threshold pressure to activate BAS

2. In case of a system which detects an emergency braking condition based on the brake pedal speed,
the following requirements of each item shall be met.
After t = t0 + 0.8s and until the vehicle has slowed down to a speed of 15km/h, a mean deceleration
of at least 0.85 * aABS shall be maintained.

Structure and Performance Requirements of Service Braking Systems for Passenger Vehicle
with Electrical Control Transmission (Article 15, Paragraph 14)

1. In the case that the nominal compensation value for tolerance of braking force exceeds the
following limits by the deterioration or defect within the service braking system, the yellow
warning signal based on warning system shall be installed to indicate the status to the driver.
Limit of compensating value
If a difference in transverse braking pressures on any axle exceeding 25 per cent of the
higher valueIf an individual compensating value on any axleexceeding 50 per cent of the nominal value
2. Malfunctions of the electric control transmission shall not apply the brakes contrary to the driver's
intentions.
3. With the parking brake released, during 1 minute after the engine has been disconnected, at least
three brake applications shall generate the braking force conforming to 'Performance of service
brake system' specified in Subparagraph 4 of Table 7 of the KMVSS.
4. With the parking brake released, after 1 minute from engine disconnection, or as from the fourth
brake application within the 60 second period, the braking system shall be generated as conforming
to 'Performance of service braking system in case of the failure of transmission device' specified
in Subparagraph 6 of Table 7 of the KMVSS.
5. A failure within the electric control transmission that affects the function and performance of
systems shall be indicated to the driver by the warning signal. However, if 'Braking performance
of service brake system' in Subparagraph 4 of Table 7 of the KMVSS cannot be achieved due to
this failure, the color of warning signal shall be red.
6. In the event of failure in components or function of electric control transmission, 'Performance
requirements of service braking system in case of the failure of transmission device' specified in
Subparagraph 6 of Table 7 shall be met.
7. In the event of the failure of the energy source of the electric transmission, the braking force,
breaking pressure or the output value of electric transmission shall make the nominal braking
operation possible or shall generate the braking force conforming to 'Performance requirements of
service braking system' specified in Subparagraph 4 of Table 7 of the KMVSS, at 21st actuation
after twenty consecutive full stroke actuations of the service braking control.
8. Due to the drop of battery voltage, if the braking performance cannot meet 'Performance
requirements of service braking system' specified in Subparagraph 4 of Table 7 or 'Performance
requirements of service braking system in case of the failure of transmission device' specified in
Subparagraph 6 of Table 7, the red warning signal shall be activated in advance. After the warning
signal has been activated, it shall conform to 'Performance requirements of service braking system
in case of the failure of transmission device' prescribed in Subparagraph 6 of Table 7.

Requirements for Insulation Safety Of High Voltage Electric Device
(Article 18-2 and Article 18-6 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 3)

1. The live parts of high voltage electric devices shall comply with the requirements specified in each
of the following Items.
A. The protection against direct contact with the live parts shall not be opened, disassembled or
removed without the use of tools.
B. For protection of the live parts inside the passenger compartment or luggage compartment, the
direct contact shall not occur upon IPXXD approach.
C. For protection of the live parts in areas other than Item B, the direct contact shall not occur upon
IPXXB approach.
D. Notwithstanding Item C, for protection of the live parts of motorcycles not having the passenger
compartment, the direct contact shall not occur upon IPXXD approach.
2. The connectors of high voltage electric devices (including charging inlet of electric vehicle) shall
comply with all the requirements specified in each of the following Items of Subparagraph 1.
However, the requirements of Subparagraph 1 Item A are not applied to the connector falling under
any of the following Items.
A. Connectors comply with Subparagraph 1 Item b, Item c when separated
B. Connectors are located underneath the floor and provided with a locking mechanism
C. Connectors are provided with a locking mechanism and other components shall be removed
with the use of tools in order to separate the connectors
D. The voltage of the live parts becomes equal or below DC 60V or AC 30V (referring to RMS
value; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Table) within 1 second after the connectors are
separated.
3. In the case the device, which disconnects the high voltage circuit for the inspection and repair of
high voltage electric device, can be opened, disassembled or removed without tools, the direct
contact shall not occur upon IPXXB approach.
4. The warning symbol meeting each of the following Items shall be identified on the enclosure or
barrier of high voltage electric device. However, it may be omitted for the high voltage connector
and the enclosures and barriers which are located underneath the vehicle floor or which cannot be
accessed, opened or removed easily.A. The warning symbol is as below.


Color: The symbol background shall be yellow, the bordering and the figure shall be black

B. The warning symbol shall be identified to be visible and shall not be easily discolored or erased.
C. In case of traction battery, the warning symbol shall be affixed at its upper part or surroundings.
5. Cables for high voltage buses which are not located within enclosures shall be identified by having
an outer covering with the color orange.
6. The exposed conductive parts of the enclosures and barriers of high voltage devices shall be
삭제함: 18-4

conductively connected to the electrical chassis by the connection with electrical wire, or welding
or connection using bolts, and the resistance between all exposed conductive parts and the electrical
chassis shall be less than 0.1 ohm.
7. The insulation resistance between the live parts of the high voltage electric device and the electrical
chassis shall comply with the requirements in each of the following Items.
A. In case of consisting of separate DC- or AC- buses, the insulation resistance shall have a
minimum value of 100ohms/volt (DC) and a minimum value of 500 ohms/volt (AC).
B. In case of consisting of combined DC- and AC- buses, the insulation resistance shall have a
minimum value of 500 ohms/volt. However, if all AC high voltage buses meet any of the
following, it may have a minimum value of 100 ohms/volt.
1) Double or more layers of solid insulators inside barriers or enclosures of high voltage electric
devices that meet the requirement in Subparagraph 6,
2) Mechanically robust protections that have sufficient durability over vehicle service life
such as motor housings, electronic converter cases or connectors.
C. The AC high voltage buses in hydrogen fuel cell vehicles shall have the insulation resistance
monitoring system with a warning to the driver if the insulation resistance drops to 100 ohms/volt
or less.
D. The insulation resistance between the live parts of charge inlet of electric vehicles and the
electrical chassis shall be at least 1M ohms.
E. Insulation resistance requirements shall not apply to vehicles of which live parts of high voltage
electric device and the electrical chassis are connected where the voltage between live parts and
the electrical does not exceed 30V AC or 60 V DC.
8. For charging the traction battery of electric vehicles, the vehicle shall be connected to the grounded
external power supply before the external power supply (charge volt and current) is applied and it
shall be maintained until the external power supply is disconnected. During the charge of traction
battery, the vehicle movement shall be impossible.

Remark)
1) IPXXB: A test finger to check the access safety of fingers specified in (IEC 60529) of
International Protection Code
2) IPXXD: A test wire to check the access safety of wire specified in (IEC 60529) of International
Protection Code

B. Requirements for operation
1) Stop lamps or turn signal lamp shall flash in phase at a frequency of emergency stop signal
(4.0±1.0Hz, 4.0 +0.0/-1.0Hz in filament light sources).
2) The lamps activated by emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.

A Tell-tale device on whether or not emergency stop signal is operated may be installed
optionally.D. Other requirements
1) Except for 3) and 4), if a motor vehicle is equipped to tow a trailer, the control of the
emergency stop signal on the motor vehicle shall also be capable of operating the emergency
stop signal on the trailer.
2) When the motor vehicle is electrically connected to a trailer, the operation of the emergency
stop signal shall conform to Item 'B,1.
3) If a motor vehicle is equipped to tow a trailer fitted with a service braking system of either
continuous or semi-continuous type, it shall be ensured that a constant power supply is
provided via the electrical connector for the stop lamps to such trailers while the service brake
is applied.
4) The emergency stop signal on any such trailer may operate independently of the towing
vehicle and is not required to operate either at the same frequency as the towing vehicle.

1) Stop signal device shall consist of the indication part for warning that children are getting on
and off and the support part mounted in a vehicle body.
2) Support part shall be affixed firmly to a vehicle in order not be detached while driving and
there shall exist no sharp protrusion or edges. In this case, a part of support part shall be folded
and indication part shall be detachable.
3) Indication part of the device shall be double-faced and the specification of both sides are as
follows.

<Specification of indication area>Remark)
1. The background color shall be red, colors of letters and outline shall be white
2. The curvature of each edge shall not be less than 10 mm.
3. The material shall be polycarbonate.
4. The indication part of the device for mid-sized or large-sized buses with seating capacity
of 16 persons or more shall be sized as 125 - 150% of the specification above.

B. Operation requirements of indication area of stop signal device
1) Stop signal device shall be extended automatically in the direction perpendicular to vehicle
body, when the entrance is opened for children boarding.
2) Stop signal device shall be folded automatically in the direction parallel to vehicle body, when
the entrance is closed for children boarding.

Camera-Monitor System Performance Criteria
(Article 50 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 2)

1. General criteria
A. Structure which CMS shall be possible to adjust without tools if necessary to adjust.
B. Structure which CMS shall be activated within 0.2 seconds and meet the requirements in Article
107 (Electromagnetic compliance).

2. Functional criteria
A. To fulfil field of view of interior rear-view, exterior rear-view class Ⅱ, exterior rear-view class
Ⅲ, wide angle rear-view, following criteria should be met:
1) It shall be possible to adjust the average luminance of the monitor either manually or
automatically to the ambient conditions.
2) If CMS is not operational, it shall be indicated to the driver.
3) Monitor shall conform to optical requirements as in the following:
a) Does not exceed 35 per cent of the luminance white level for the monitor standard isotropy
range and shall not exceed 50 per cent of the luminance white level for the monitor extended
isotropy range.b) Side luminance deviation shall be within 35 per cent.
4) Luminance and contrast of CMS shall conform to following requirements:
RequirementsFor direct sunlight condition2 : 1For day condition with diffuse ambient light3 : 1For sunset condition
2 : 1For night condition
10:1 except in the case of Mirror and CMS dual function system of
class I: 5:1.

5) CMS shall be able to display 8 or more achromatic colors.
6) Monitor shall satisfy the following requirements:
A) Red colour coordinates shall not exceed the range of (0°-44.8°) or (332.2°-360°)
B) Green colour coordinates shall not exceed the range of (96.6°-179.9°)
C) Blue colour coordinates shall not exceed the range of (209.9°-302.2°)
D) Yellow colour coordinates shall not exceed the range of (44.8°- 96.6°)
E) To distinguish from the white colour, define distance from white as Ri ≥ 0.02,

Installation and Operational Requirements for Safety-Belt Reminder
(Article 27 Paragraph 4)

1. Installation requirements for safety-belt reminder
A. Visual warning
1) Visual warning shall be located as to readily visible and recognizable in the day and night
time by the driver, distinguishable from other warning devices.
2) Visual warning shall be by continuous or intermittent signal.
3) Visual warning meet each of following requirements.
a) Driver seat and passenger seat beside driver seat: it shall meet the requirements for
identification for seat belt in Table 2.
b) Seats other than Item a): Visual warning shall be located as to readily visible so that a driver,
while seating on driver seat and facing forward, can easily check the location of seats where
a seat belt is not fastened.B. Audible warning
1) Audible shall be by continuous or intermittent sound signal (the interval of intermittent sound
shall not exceed 1 second) or by continuous vocal information. In this case, vocal information
sound shall use Korean.2) Audible warning shall be recognizable by the driver.

2. Operational requirements for safety-belt reminder
A. First level warning
1) Visual warning appropriate for each of following Items shall be provided when any one of
safety belts is not fastened and the ignition switch is engaged.
a) Driver seat and passenger seat beside driver: 30 seconds or longer
b) Seats other than Item a: 60 seconds or longer
B. Second level warning
1) When the vehicle is in normal operation (running forward with 10km/h or more) and if
applicable to 2) operating condition, visual and audible signal shall be activated for 30 seconds
or more (except when the interval between periodic warnings exceeds 3 seconds) before
exceeding any one of the following Items. In this case, even if first level warning is
continuously operated, second level warning shall override first level warning.
a) Driving distance: 500 mb) Vehicle speed: 25 km/hc) Driving time: 60 seconds
2) Second warning shall be provided in case of each of the following Items.
a) Driver seat and passenger seat beside driver: seat belt is or becomes unfastened
b) Seats other than Item a) : seat belt becomes unfastened

Installation Requirements for Event Data Recorder (Article 56-2 Paragraph 3)

1. General Installation Requirements for EDR
A. EDR shall record the pre- and post-accident driving information in accordance with
Subparagraph 2 of this Table, in the event of an accident (hereinafter "accident" in this Table)
pursuant to Article 56-2 Paragraph 1.
B. Driving information recorded in any of the following circumstances shall not be overwritten
even if the driving information of any subsequent accident is recorded.
1. Article 56-2 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 2
2. Article 56-2 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 3
3. Where the vehicle’s velocity change in x-axis direction exceeds 25 km/h within 0.15 seconds
or less interval (limited to vehicles not equipped with a non-reversible restraint system)

C. EDR shall be able to record and store the driving information of three or more accidents.
D. In addition to those prescribed in Items A through C, details for the driving information
recording method of EDR, etc. shall be prescribed and notified by the Minister of MOLIT.

2. EDR Data Elements
A. The following driving information shall be recorded through EDR in accordance with the
requirements prescribed in the relevant section. However, in case of driving information that
requires a separate device for recording, such as a sensor, in addition to EDR, if the relevant
device is not installed in the vehicle or was not activated at the time of the accident, such
information may not be recorded. In this case, if the failure to record is due to a malfunction of
the relevant device, the EDR shall record the reason.

1. "Time zero" means whichever of the following occurs first as the base point for recording
interval or time when an event is recorded.
A. For systems with "wake-up" airbag control systems, the moment at which the occupant
restraint control algorithm is activated;
B. For continuously running algorithms, the moment at which "delta-V, longitudinal" within
a 0.02 second time period becomes more than 0.8 km/h (including the moment at which
"delta-V, lateral" within a 0.005 second time period becomes more than 0.8 km/h, for
vehicles that record the velocity change along the lateral axis); or
C. When a non-reversible deployable restraint such as airbag or safety belt pretensioner is
deployed or when a pedestrian protection system is deployed
2. "End of event time" means whichever of the following occurs first, serving as the baseline
point for ending event recording
A. The moment at which "delta-V, longitudinal" within a 0.02 second time period (referring
to the moment at which the resultant delta-V along the vector-added longitudinal and lateral
axes within a 0.02 second time period, for vehicles that record the velocity change along
the lateral axis) becomes 0.8 km/h or less;
B. The moment at which the crash detection algorithm of the control unit for non-reversible
deployable restraint such as airbag or pretensioner of seat belt resets; or
C. The moment at which the control unit for a pedestrian protection system resets
3. Notwithstanding 1) through 3), if the longitudinal acceleration is recorded in accordance with
2) of Item B, the driving information specified in 1) through 3) of this Item may not be
recorded.
4. "Service brake" in 6) may include the brake pedal switch or other driver-operated service
brake control.

5. "Ignition cycle, crash" in 7) means the number (count) of power mode cycles applied to the

6. "Ignition cycle download" in 8) means the number (count) of power mode cycles applied to
the recording device at the time when the data was downloaded since the first use of the EDR.
7. "Multi-event crash, interval of event" in 13) means the time interval from 0 second of the first
accident to 0 second of the second accident in cases where the number of multiple accidents
is 2 or more.
8. Whether all items are recorded without problems in 14) includes the optional data elements
additionally recorded in accordance with Item B.
9. Notwithstanding 15) through 17), if the lateral acceleration is recorded in accordance with 3)
of Item B, the driving information specified in 15) through 17) of this Item may not be
recorded.
10. "Time for maximum delta-V, resultant" in 18) means the time for the maximum delta-V both
in the longitudinal and the lateral direction after time zero.
11. Notwithstanding 18), if the longitudinal and lateral acceleration is recorded in accordance
with 2) and 3) of Item B, the time for maximum delta-V, resultant specified in 18) of this Item
may not be recorded.
12. "Vehicle roll rate" in 20) shall be recorded if the system control algorithm is activated.
13. Frontal air bag deployment, each stage deployment time from 2nd to nth, driver in 26) and
frontal air bag deployment, each stage deployment time from 2nd to nth, front passenger in
27) shall be recorded by adding as many items as the number of stages remaining except for
Stage 1.
14. The seat track position switch, foremost, status, driver in 34) and seat track position switch,
foremost, status, front passenger in 35) shall be recorded when the function is used to
determine the deployment of a non-reversible deployable restraint such as airbag or safety
belt pretensioner.
15. Notwithstanding 41), if the ESC status is recorded pursuant to 22), the TCS status under 41)
of this Item may not be recorded.
16. "Adaptive cruise control (ACC)" in 44) refers to a system that automatically accelerates or
decelerates the vehicle to maintain a preset speed and distance from the vehicle ahead as
predetermined by the driver.
17. When recording safety belt status, rear passengers in 47), the seat belt status for all rows,
excluding the first row, shall be recorded.
18. "Emergency call (eCall)" in 55) refers to a system that transmits information on vehicle
collision via public or private wireless communication networks through in-vehicle sensors
and activates an emergency voice channel between the vehicle occupant and response point.

be recorded according to the relevant requirements defined in the following.

the braking pressure for each wheel shall be recorded.

Standing Room Space and Handle Installation Criteria
(Article 23 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 5, Article 28 Paragraphs 2 and 3, Article 29 Paragraph
1 Subparagraph 3)

1. Standing room space for 1 personStanding room space per personBus with seating capacity of 23 persons or less0.125𝑚2or more

2. Space excluded from standing roomA. Driver's area
B. Entrance stairs, stairs with a depth of less than 300mm and area required for entrance operation
(including operative accessories)
C. A space measured vertically from the floor of the vehicle with a height of 1,350 mm or less
(1,200 mm, if the seating capacity is 23 persons or less,)
D. A space where passengers cannot access as a connecting part of articulated vehicle
E. Cargo and canteen spaceF. Floor space of the stairs installed in the vehicle
G. Spaces where standing passengers cannot access such that its floor inclination exceeds 8% in a
longitudinal direction of vehicle (12.5%, if the number of standing passengers is more than
seating passenger) or 5% in a transverse direction of vehicle.
H. Spaces where standing passengers cannot access, such as seating space (except folding seats)
I. Front space in a longitudinal direction of the vehicle from the center of driver's seat (if adjustable,
rearmost point)
J. 300mm space in front of all seats (225mm for side-facing seat, except folding seats)
K. Space where rectangular (400mm x 300mm) cannot be placed
L. Upper floor of large-sized double-decked large-sized bus
M. Wheelchair user's space (including space provided exclusively for wheelchair users)

3. Handlebar and handle
A. The length of handlebar shall be at least 100mm, and its cross section shall be 20mm or more
and 45mm or less, except handlebar installed on an entrance or seats.
B. The handlebar or handle shall be at least 40 mm from the inside or walls of the vehicle. However,
it shall be at least 35mm either if the vehicle is exclusively for seating passengers or the handle
or handlebar is installed in an entrance or seats of the vehicle which has a number of seating
passengers more than standing passengers.
C. At each point of the standing room, the number of handles shall be two or more within the
measurement range of the measuring device separately notified by the Minister of MOLIT. If a
handle strap is installed, it is regarded as a handle if properly fastened. However, if the minimum
cross-section of a handlebar is 15mm, the minimum cross-section of another handlebar shall be
25mm or more.
D. The handlebar or handle shall be installed at a height of 800mm to 1,950mm from the floor of
the vehicle

Driver's Seat Space (Article 24 Paragraph 3)

1. Behind the driver's seat, a protective bar or partition, meeting the requirements in each of following
Item, shall be equipped for being separated from passenger seats. However, it is not applied to the
bus with a seating capacity of 23 persons or less, if a seat belt pursuant to Article 27 is installed in
a seat behind the driver's seat.
A. The height above the vehicle floor shall be 800mm or more.
B. The width shall cover the space from the inside wall of vehicle wall to outside of driver seat and
shall extend at least 100mm from the center of the passenger's seat adjacent to passage behind
the driver's seat toward the aisle.
C. The distance between the uppermost corner of the space for storing an object, such as a table,
and the uppermost corner of the partition shall be at least 90mm.
2. It shall have a structure such that a sphere with a diameter of 50 mm cannot roll into the driver's
seat from the passenger seat right behind the driver's seat
3. It shall have a structure such that the driver's seat space can be protected from the reflection or
glare caused by sunlight and lighting provided in the vehicle.
4. In driver's seat space, defogger and defroster which can be controlled by driver shall be installed.
5. The driver's seat shall have an independent structure and equipped with a suspension. However, it
may not apply to the buses with a seating capacity of 23 passengers or less.
6. The driver's seat space shall have backrests curved and armrests. If armrests installed, the distance
between the left and right armrests shall be 450mm or more.
7. The width of the seat back shall be 450mm or more from the driver's seat center to 250mm vertically.

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)2. Installation requirements of entranceA. General requirements
1) At least one entrance shall be installed. However, a double-decked large-sized bus shall have
two entrance in the lower deck and articulated bus, which has a number of standing passengers
more than seating passengers, shall have one entrance or more in its front and rear side.
2) If electrical operating entrance, if not able to open it by manual operation after operating it in
emergency, is not regarded as emergency exit.
3) The entrance shall be installed on the right side of the bus, but one or more entrance shall be
installed for a bus with a seating capacity exceeding 23 persons in its front side of bus in the
longitudinal direction, except:
a) Entrance installed on rear or side of bus for getting on and off for wheelchair users
b) Entrance installed on rear or side of bus for loading cargo
c) Entrance installed on left side of bus, for which the driver can control its operation with a
However, in the case where the Minister of MOLIT recognizes that technology of preventing
malfunction has been applied, an additional entrance may be installed on the left side.
4) If two or more entrance are installed in a bus with passenger space of 10m² or more, the
distance between transverse vertical planes passing through the center of entrance area shall
satisfy following requirements, except the case defined and notified by minister of MOLIT
such as articulated vehicle, and etc.
a) It shall be 40% or more of total length of passenger space
b) It shall be 25% or more of total length of bus or 40% or more of total length of passenger
space for lower level in double-decked large-sized bus.
5) It shall be able be opened from inside and outside when stopped. However, if an external
locking device is installed, it shall be structured to be opened inside.
6) The device to open entrance from outside of bus shall be at a height from 1,000 to 1,500 mm
above the ground and 500 mm or less from the entrance.
7) A bus with a seating capacity exceeding 23 shall have device to open the entrance from inside,
and it shall be at a height 1,000 mm to 1,500 mm above the floor of the bus or the top of the
stairs, and shall be within 500 mm or less from the entrance. However, this shall not apply to
control device installed in driver's seat.
8) Hinged or rotatable entrance manually operated shall be structured to move in the direction
where it closes if the bus moves forward and is in contact with an external object.
Every one-piece manually-operated service door which is hinged or pivoted shall be so hinged
or pivoted that if the open door comes into contact with a stationary object while the vehicle
is moving forwards it tends to close.
9) The entrance manually operated, if equipped with door latches, shall have a double locking
structure
10) If the entrance closes toward inside, it shall be structured not to affect any danger to internal
structures such as stairs and passengers.
11) Device securing field of view that driver can check inside and outside of the entrance shall
be installed, and it shall be installed inside of the entrance, stairs, and upper floor, for a double-
decked large-sized bus, with a number of standing passenger more than seating passenger and
with a seating capacity exceeding 23 persons.
12) If installed on a bus with seating capacity of 23 or less, open angle of entrance shall be from
85 to 115 degrees and upon complete open, it shall be structured to be fixed automatically.
However, it does not apply if the entrance opens 270 degrees for a purpose of riding with a
high platform and allowing to enter it through a riding space identified in the rear of bus.

13) The height of the first step of the entrance shall be 40 centimeters or less.
B. It shall comply with any one of the following requirements, if external locking system for the
entrance is installed.
1) When the ignition key is in "ON", it shall be deactivated
2) When the ignition key is in "ON", a driver shall be warned if it is activated. In this case, two
or more entrance can be used at the same time.
C. The electrical entrance operated by the driver shall comply with each of following requirements.
1) In emergency, entrance shall be able to open from inside or outside complying with following
requirements at a speed of 5 km / h or less., except when locking device is activated from
outside.
A) It shall open first when entrance operating device is operated.
B) The internal operating device shall be located 300mm or less from the entrance and
exceeding 1,000mm above the first step, except the case for traffic vulnerable.
C) Start prevention device may be activated
D) The entrance measuring device shall be able to pass within 8 seconds of the device
operation.
E) The emergency operating device may be provided with a protective device which is easy
to remove, and shall warn the driver by visual and auditory warning when the device is
operated or protective cover is removed.
F) The entrance, if not meeting the requirements in 5) c) of Subparagraph 2 Item c', shall not
be closed until the driver operates to close the entrance, even if the device is operated to
open the door and then returned to the normal position
G) The door shall not open at speed of vehicle exceeding 5 km / h
2) A device to prevent operation of emergency operating device installed outside may be
installed on the position where it can be controlled in the driver's seat. In this case, the
deactivation function of emergency operating device shall not be operated automatically
without driver's control and the deactivation function shall be released before the engine is
started or running at a speed of 20 km/h.
3) If the entrance is installed other than the front of the bus body, a visual warning shall be
provided for driver that it's open, upon 30 mm before the door is closed. In the case of two
entrances or more, one visual warning may be provided for each entrance.
4) The entrance operating device shall be able to operate reversely by the driver, even while
being opened and closed.
5) Protection function complying to following requirements shall be equipped, when electrical
entrance is closing.
A) If a load of 150N or less (temporarily exceeding 150N but not exceeding 300N) at a point
150mm above the middle point and the lower end of entrance is applied, the entrance shall
be automatically in fully open state and it shall be kept. In this case, a measuring device
having a height of 60 mm, a width of 30 mm, and a cross section with a radius of 5 mm in
its corner may be applied.
B) If a finger or a wrist is caught in entrance, any of the following requirements shall be met.
(1) The state shall be kept until the entrance is operated to be closed after its open.
(2) The measuring device of circular truncated cone shape which has a length of 300 mm,
an upper diameter of 5 mm and lower diameter of 30 mm shall be able to go through.
(3) The state position, where measuring device having a height of 60 mm, a width of 20 mm,
and a cross section with a radius of 5 mm in its corner can pass (it means a position not
exceeding 30 mm from entrance close), shall be kept.
C) If the front entrance meets the following each Item, it shall be deemed to comply with the

(1) Requirements specified in 5) a) and b) of Subparagraph 2 Item c'
(2) Following shall be excluded, if the end is made of a soft material, if the measuring
device specified in 5) a) of Subparagraph 2 Item c' is applied, and if the rigid structure
of entrance is completely closed.
6) When the electrical entrance has been closed only by the continuous power supply, if its
power supply cuts off, it shall be visually informed to the driver.
7) If the device preventing the start with doors open (hereinafter "anti open-door start) is installed
in a bus, it shall operate at a speed of 5 km/h or less.
8) If the Anti open-door start is not installed, the driver should be audibly warned when the
entrance is opened.
D. An automatic electrical entrance (An automatic electrical entrance that can be opened by the
passenger's operation after operated automatically by the driver, thereby automatically-closing
entrance), if installed, shall comply with the following requirements.
1) Automatic activation of automatic-electrical entrance shall comply to following requirements
in Item
A) Activation and deactivation of all entrances, except emergency, shall be controllable in the
driver's seat.
B) If the driver's operation for opening is activated, the indicator shall be installed on inside
of the bus. If the entrance opens outside, the indicator shall be installed outside of the bus.
In this case, the indicator such as lighting push button, lighting indication, etc. shall be
installed on or adjacent to the applicable entrance.
C) If it is directly operated by a switch, the function status of the automatic operating entrance
shall be indicated to the driver with the position of the switch, indicator lighting or lighting
switch etc., and the switch shall not be confused with other operating devices
2) The automatic-electrical entrance, after activated by the driver's operation, shall be able to
open if passengers perform the following operations.
A) For inside, if push button is applied or light detector passes
B) For outside, if light pushbutton is applied, pushbutton under the light indication is applied,
or similar device with appropriate indication is applied.
3) The closing method of the automatic-electrical entrance shall meet the following requirements.
For the closing process after the limited automatic closing function specified in Subparagraph
2 Item d' 4), it shall meet the following A) and B).
A) Automatic electrical entrance, upon opened, shall be closed automatically after a certain
period of time has elapsed and the safety device shall be installed to delay the automatic
closing.
B) If the passengers want to get on and off while entrance is closing, the entrance shall be
structured to open again using the safety device.
4) For the entrance used by traffic vulnerable, etc. specified in Article 2 Subparagraph 1 of "Act
on Promotion of the Transportation Convenience of Mobility Disadvantaged Persons" for
easy getting on and off, automatic closing shall be restricted as complying the following
requirements. If the function is operated in accordance with the following A), the automatic
indicator shall be provided to warn the driver visually.
A) The driver shall be able to limit the automatic closing by operating special device and
passengers also shall be able to limit the closing by operating the pushbutton
B) The limited automatic closing function shall only be recovered by the driver.

B. Installation requirements
1) In case of double decked bus (except for the upper-level open-top type), they shall be installed
in the lower and upper floors, however, except bathroom and the canteen.
2) Front and rear part of passenger cabin shall be separated for articulated bus. (front and rear
connecting passages shall be excluded from passenger space.)
3) Entrance is included in the emergency exit and is considered to be two if two entrance-
measuring devices as specified in Table 5-30 pass at the same time.
4) If the size of the emergency window is twice than those specified in Subparagraph 3 Item a),
it is regarded as 2 windows.
5) Bus with a seating capacity of 23 persons or less, shall meet the following requirements.
A) Install at least one on left and right of the vehicle
B) Install at least one on front and rear passenger space
6) Emergency exit (for double decked bus, the lower and upper decks are applied separately)
shall be installed in equal numbers of left and right sides, except if exceeding the minimum
installation number.
7) At least one should be installed on the front or rear of the vehicle.
8) Bus with a number of standing passenger more than seating passenger and a seating capacity
exceeding 23 persons and Bus with standing passenger and a seating capacity exceeding 23
persons, if installing emergency exit on left and right as exceeding the limit, are deemed as
satisfying the requirement specified in 7).
9) In the case of double decked bus, the requirement specified in 7) applies only to upper deck.
10) Emergency doors other than entrance may be installed on the rear side of the vehicle.
11) Upon driver's seat adjusted to rearmost, if the front edge of the aisle-measuring device
specified in Table 5-29 fails to pass horizontally at the front side of the driver's seat, and if the
panel notified by the minister of MOLIT fails to pass through the front side of the cushion in
driver's seat, the driver seat space shall meet the following requirements.
A) Two exits shall be installed for driver's seat. In this case, the exit shall not be installed on
the same side, and any one of entrance may be installed as an emergency window.
B) If passenger seats are installed parallel with the driver's seat, the exit designated by the

12) If the aisle pursuant to Article 31 is installed in passenger seats in parallel with direction of

be installed on each side of the wall.
13) The entrance may, if installed on driver's seat accessible into cabin on bus with a seating

14) The entrance installed on driver's seat is, if partition is installed between driver's seat and
passenger seats, not deemed as emergency exit.
15) Escape hatch shall not be installed in locations where high-voltage systems, systems
containing hazardous liquids or gases are installed.
16) Stairway connecting the lower and upper floors of a double decked bus shall be regarded as
one emergency exit for upper floor.
17) Passengers on lower deck of double decked bus shall be able only to escape to the lower
deck only in an emergency.
18) Double decked bus shall be provided with staircase to upper floor 3m or less from the
entrance. However, if the upper floor passenger is 30 or more persons, additional staircase
notified by the Minister MOLIT shall be installed.
19) If one or less passenger seat parallel passenger seats in parallel with direction of vehicle's
width and the driver's seat is installed in bus with a seating capacity of 23 or less persons, the
entrance installed in passenger seat may be deemed as an emergency exit.
20) If emergency door and escape hatch is installed, the location of emergency door, escape
hatch and opening method shall be identified clearly in that area.

2. Emergency door
Emergency door shall meet the requirements specified in any one of each following Items.
A. A-type Emergency door
1) Its width shall be 600mm or more and height be 1,450mm or more. However, for bus with a
seating capacity of 23 persons or less, its width shall be 550mm or more and height be
1,250mm or more.
2) If emergency door is installed in upper part of the wheel, the door width may be 300mm from
lowermost of emergency door to the height of 400mm, and the radius curvature of curvature
of the upper corner of the emergency door may be 150mm or less.
3) It shall open from inside and outside when stopped. However, if an external locking device is
installed, it shall be structured to be opened inside.
4) The electrical-operating emergency door shall not be closed, until the driver operates to close
the door, even if the operating device returned to the normal position after the device is
operated in emergency.
5) The entrance-measuring device specified in Table 5-30 shall pass within 8 seconds of
operation of the electrical emergency operating device.
6) The sliding door type shall not be applied, except that emergency door should be opened
without a tool upon the vehicle crash test among the vehicle body structure requirements under
Article 102 Paragraph 2 for bus with a seating capacity of 23 or less persons.
7) The device to open emergency door (lower floor if double decked bus) from the outside of
the vehicle shall be 1,000 mm to 1,500 mm above ground and 500 mm or less from the
emergency door.
8) For bus with a seating capacity exceeding 23 persons, the device to open the emergency door
from inside shall be 1,000 mm to 1,500 from the floor of the bus or from top of the stairs, and
shall be 500 mm or less from the entrance, except the operating device installed in driver's

9) The hinge fixed to the side of the vehicle shall be installed in front side of the vehicle in a
longitudinal direction and be structured to open to the outside of vehicle. And check ropes,
chains or other restraint devices may be used at least at an angle of 100 degrees.
10) If all emergency doors are not completely closed, a warning sound device actuated by a latch
or knob movement shall be installed for the driver.
11) Night lock device, if installed, shall comply with the following requirements.
A) Shall be deactivated automatically if the ignition key is in "ON".
B) The night lock shall have a warning function to indicate that it remains active in one or
more doors when the ignition key is in "ON". One signal can be connected and used for
one or more doors.B. B-type emergency door
1) The emergency door shall be installed at the rear of the left side of the passenger cabin (which
means that the center of effective width of the emergency door is behind the intermediate
position of the passenger cabin in the vehicle length direction) or the back of the passenger
cabin.
2) Its size shall be not less than 400 mm effective width and not less than 1,200 mm effective
height, except the following.
a) If the emergency door is installed above the vehicle wheel, and if its effective width is 250
mm or more from the floor of the passenger cabin to 450 mm, 400 mm or more to the other
part, and its effective height is 1,200 mm or more,
b) If the seat is installed near the emergency door, the seat should be easily separated or folded,
and If effective width of the emergency door is 300 mm or more from the floor of the
passenger cabin to 650 mm, 400 mm or more to the other part, and its effective height is
1,300 mm or more,
c) For emergency door of school bus, if its effective width is not less than 300 mm and its
effective height is not less than 1,000 mm,
d) For emergency door of medium-sized buses with three or more exits excluding emergency
door, when it opened, if a space of its effective width of 1,200 mm or more and effective
height of 400 mm or more is secured,
3) The emergency door can be safely closed under normal conditions and it shall be able to be
opened inside and outside the passenger cabin without using special equipment in an
emergency. In this case, the structure shall not be closed by self-weight after the emergency
door is opened.
4) The obstacles that may interfere with the escape, such as bumpers, towing devices, etc., shall
not protrude around the emergency doors and shall not be provided with a staircase leading to
the above between the floor of the passenger cabin and the lower part of the emergency doors.
5) The position of the emergency door and the method of operating the emergency door shall be
marked near the emergency door or in an easily recognizable place. If the emergency door
position is indicated using a lighting system, green shall be used.
6) A warning system shall be provided to notify the driver when the emergency door is opened.

3. Emergency windows
A. A specification of emergency window shall be 500 mm x 700 mm rectangular or more with an
area of 0.4 m2 or more. However, in the rear side, the width may be 1,550mm or more and height
be 350mm or more, and the radius of curvature of each corner shall be 250mm or less.
B. Installation requirements
1) The hinged or detachable type shall open toward outside and the detachable type shall be

2) Emergency windows shall comply with any one of following requirements.
A) It shall be operated inside and outside of the vehicle.
B) It shall be a safety glass (excluding laminated glass or plastic material), and if applied it
shall be equipped with an accessory to break each emergency window near it.
3) Emergency windows that can be locked from outside the vehicle, shall be able to open from
inside.
4) A horizontal emergency window fixed with a hinge at the upper end shall be equipped with a

5) The floor of emergency windows of safety glass shall be located in between 500 mm or more

vehicle except the engine and tires installed space. However, for a hinged emergency window
equipped with 650mm structure, if meeting specification of emergency window except the

1,200 mm or less from the floor of vehicle except the engine and tires installed space.
6) If the hinged emergency window is not easily visible from the driver's seat, warning sound
device shall be installed to inform the driver if it is open or not.

4. Escape hatchA. Number of installation
Escape hatch shall be installed as the following for bus with a seating capacity of 16 persons or
more and seating passengers more than standing passengers room and bus without standing
passengers and a seating capacity of 23 or less. However, escape hatch may not be installed for
the lower floor of double decked bus, upper floor of opened double decked bus, and articulated
bus.1) Seating capacity of 30 persons or less: 1 or more2) Seating capacity of exceeding 30 persons: 2 or moreB. Installation location and size
1) If there is one escape hatch, it shall be installed on the middle part of cabin divided into three
sections.
2) If there are two escape hatches, the minimum distance between emergency exits shall be 2m
or more.
3) Escape hatch area shall be 0.45 m2 or more, and the size of the escape hatch shall cover
600mm × 700mm rectangle.C. Installation requirements
1) Escape hatch shall operate not interfering with moving in inside or outside of the vehicle.
2) Ceiling escape hatch shall be made with safety glass as hinge type, and detachable type.
3) Floor escape hatch shall be connected with hinge or be detachable.
4) Warning sound device shall be installed to notify the driver if the floor escape hatch is not
closed safely. However, it excludes floor escape hatch that automatically locks if the speed
exceeds 5 km/h.
5) Detachable escape hatch shall not be completely detached from the vehicle body during
operation, and detachable escape hatch installed on the floor shall be detached only toward
inside of the vehicle.
4) The hinged escape hatch shall open at an angle of 100 degrees or more in a direction of the
front or rear of the vehicle. However, the hinged escape hatch on floor shall only open toward
inside of the vehicle.

Steering Control Effort Requirements (Article 89 Paragraph 2)

1. Construction provisions for motor vehicles and trailers
A. The direction of operation of the steering control shall correspond to the intended change of
direction of the vehicle and there shall be a continuous relationship between the steering control
deflection and the steering angle. These requirements do not apply to systems that incorporate
an automatically commanded or corrective steering function, or to auxiliary steering equipment.
These requirements may also not necessarily apply in the case of full power steering when the
vehicle is stationary and when the system is not energized.
B. The maximum steering angle shall not be limited by any part of the steering transmission unless
specifically designed for this purpose.
C. Advanced driver assistance steering system (ADASS), additional to the main steering equipment,
shall have the function that does not cause any deterioration in the performance of the basic
steering system. In addition, they shall be designed such that the driver may, at any time and by
deliberate action, override the function. In this case, the ADASS may comprise one or more of
an automatically commanded steering function, corrective steering function or emergency
steering function.
D. Steering transmission which can be disconnected to cover different configurations of a vehicle
(e.g. on extendable semi-trailers), shall have locking devices which ensure positive relocation of
components; where locking is automatic, there shall be an additional safety lock which is
operated manually.
E. The same energy supply may be used for the steering equipment and other systems. However in
the case of a failure in any system which shares the same energy supply steering shall be ensured
in accordance with the relevant failure conditions of paragraph A.3) of Subparagraph 3 (Failure
provisions and performance).
F. A purely pneumatic transmission, autonomous steering systems, full power steering systems
fitted to trailers where the energy necessary for operation is transmitted from the towing vehicle,
the electric control of full power steering systems fitted to trailers, other than additional steering
equipment shall not be installed on vehicles or trailers. However, an autonomous driving vehicle,
for which a temporary driving permit pursuant to the proviso of Article 27 Paragraph 1 of the
MVMA is supposed to be received, may be equipped with an autonomous steering system.

Remark:
1. "Steering equipment" means all the equipment the purpose of which is to determine the
direction of movement of the vehicle, and which consists of the steering control, the steering
transmission, the steered wheels and the energy supply, if any.
2. "Steering control" means the part of the steering equipment which controls its operation; it
may be operated with or without direct intervention of the driver. For steering equipment in
which the steering forces are provided solely or partly by the muscular effort of the driver the
steering control includes all parts up to the point where the steering effort is transformed by
mechanical, hydraulic or electrical means.
3. "Steering forces" mean all the forces operating in the steering transmission.
4. "Steering angle" means the angle between the projection of a longitudinal axis of the vehicle
and the line of intersection of the wheel plane (being the central plane of the wheel, normal to
the axis around which it rotates) and the road surface.
5. "Auxiliary steering equipment" means a system in which the wheels on axle(s) of vehicles


<!-- Page 142 -->

© KAIDA
142
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
(except trailers) are steered in addition to the wheels of the main steering equipment in the
same or opposite direction to those of the main steering equipment and/or the steering angle
of the front and /or the rear wheels may be adjusted relative to vehicle behavior.
6. "Main steering system" means the steering equipment of a vehicle which is mainly responsible
for determining the direction of travel. It may comprise:
A. "Manual steering equipment" in which the steering forces result solely from the muscular
effort of the driver.
B. "Power assisted steering equipment" in which the steering forces result from both the
muscular effort of the driver and the energy supply (supplies). Steering equipment in which
the steering forces result solely from one or more energy supplies when the equipment is
intact, but in which the steering forces can be provided by the muscular effort of the driver
alone if there is a fault in the steering (integrated power systems), is also considered to be
power assisted steering equipment.
C. "Full-power steering equipment" in which the steering forces are provided solely by one
or more energy supplies.
7. "Steering transmission" means all components which form a functional link between the
steering control and the road wheels.
8. "Advanced driver assistance steering system (ADASS)" means a system, additional to the
main steering system, that provides assistance to the driver in steering the vehicle but in which
the driver remains at all times in primary control of the vehicle.
9. "Energy supply" includes those parts (classified as the following Items.) of the steering
equipment which provide it with energy, regulate that energy and where appropriate, process
and store it. It also includes any storage reservoirs for the operating medium and the return
lines, but not the vehicle's engine (except for the purpose of power assisted steering systems),
or its drive to the energy source.
A. "Energy source" means the part of the energy supply, which provides the energy in the
required form.
B. "Energy reservoir" means that part of the energy supply in which the energy provided by
the energy source is stored, for example, a pressurized fluid reservoir or vehicle battery.
C. "Storage reservoir" means that part of the energy supply in which the operating medium is
stored at or near to the atmospheric pressure, for example a fluid reservoir.
10. "Autonomous steering system" means a system that incorporates a function within a complex
electronic control system that causes the vehicle to follow a defined path or to alter its path in
response to signals initiated and transmitted from off-board the vehicle. The driver will not
necessarily be in primary control of the vehicle.
11. "Additional steering equipment" means a system, independent of the main steering system,
by which the steering angle of one or more axle(s) of the steering system can be influenced
selectively for maneuvering purposes.

2. Additional requirements for trailers(not translated, not applicable to PC)

3. Failure provisions and performanceA. General
1) The requirements in Article 14 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 4, paragraph 1.A. above
(Construction provisions for motor vehicles and trailers) and Item 5.A. below (Provisions for
motor vehicles (except trailers)) shall also be satisfied with a failure in the steering equipment
as long as the vehicle can be driven with the speeds required in Article 14 Paragraph 1


<!-- Page 143 -->

© KAIDA
143
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
Subparagraph 4, paragraph 1.A. above and paragraph 5.A. below. However, the requirement
in paragraph 1. A. does not apply to the full-power steering equipment of vehicle which is in
a stationary state.
2) Any failure in a transmission other than purely mechanical shall clearly be brought to the
attention of the vehicle driver as given in paragraph 4. When a failure occurs, a change in the
average steering ratio is permissible if the steering effort given in paragraph 5.C. is not
exceeded.
3) In the case where the braking system of the vehicle shares the same energy source or energy
supply as the steering system and this energy source or energy supply fails, the steering system
shall have priority and shall be capable of meeting the requirements below as applicable.
a) energy source failure
(1) power assisted steering system: paragraphs 3.B. and 7.A.
(2) full power steering system: paragraphs 3.C. and 7.A.
b) energy supply failure
(1) power assisted steering system: paragraphs 3.B. and 7.B.
(2) full power steering system: paragraphs 3.C. and 7.B.
4) In the case of trailers the requirements of Items 2.C. and 6.D. shall also be met when there is
a failure in the steering system.B. Power assisted steering system
1) Should the engine stop or a part of the steering wheel fail, with the exception of those parts
listed in Article 14 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 9, there shall be no immediate changes in
steering angle.
2) As long as the vehicle is capable of being driven at a speed greater than 10km/h the
requirements given in paragraph 5.C. relating to a system with the failure, shall be met.
C. Full power steering systems
1) The system shall be designed such that the vehicle cannot be driven indefinitely at speeds
above 10km/h where there is any fault which requires operation of the warning signal referred
to in paragraph 4.B.1).a).
2) In case of a failure within the control transmission, with the exception of those parts listed in
Article 14 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 9, it shall still be possible to steer with the performance
laid down in paragraph 5.A. through C. for the intact steering system.
3) In the event of a failure of the energy source of the control transmission, it shall be possible
to carry out at least 24 "figure of eight" maneuvers, where each loop of the figure is 40m
diameter at 10km/h speed and at the performance level given for an intact system in paragraph
5.A. through C.
4) In the event of a failure of the energy transmission, with the exception of those parts listed in
Article 14 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 9, there shall not be any immediate changes in steering
angle. As long as the vehicle is capable of being driven at a speed greater than 10km/h the
requirements of paragraph 5.C. for the system with a failure shall be met after the completion
of at least 25 "figure of eight" maneuvers at 10km/h minimum speed, where each loop of the
figure is 40m diameter.

Remark:
1. "Control transmission" means all components by means of which signals are transmitted
for control of the steering equipment.
2. "Energy transmission" means all components by means of which the energy required for
control/regulation of the steering function of the wheels is transmitted.
3. "Steering control effort" means the force applied to the steering control in order to steer the

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)vehicle.
4. "Mean steering ratio" means the ratio of the angular displacement of the steering control to
the mean of the swept steering angel of the steered wheels for a full lock-to-lock turn.

4. Warning signalsA. General provisions
1) Optical warning signal shall meet the following requirements
a) The signals shall be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat, even by daylight
b) Distinguishable from other alerts
c) The failure of a component of the warning devices shall not entail any loss of the steering
system's performance
2) Acoustic warning signal shall meet the following requirements
a) It shall be by continuous or intermittent sound signal or by vocal information.
b) Use Korean, where vocal information is employed
c) It shall be easily recognized by the driver
3) If the same energy source is used to supply the steering system and other systems, an acoustic
or optical warning shall be given to the driver, when the stored energy/fluid in the
energy/storage reservoir drops to a level liable to cause an increase in steering effort. This
warning may be combined with a device provided to warn of brake failure if the brake system
uses the same energy source.
4) In the case where additional steering equipment is in operation and/or where the steering angle
generated by that equipment has not been returned to normal driving position a warning signal
shall be given to the driver.B. Special provisions for full-power steering equipment
1) Power-driven vehicles shall be capable of providing steering failure and defect warning
signals, as follows:
a) A red warning signal, indicating failures defined in paragraph 3.A.2).
b) Where applicable, a yellow warning signal indicating an electrically detected defect within
the steering equipment, which is not indicated by the red warning signal.
c) If a symbol is used, it shall be:

d) The warning signal(s) mentioned above in a) and b) shall light up when the electrical
equipment of the vehicle (and the steering system) is energized. With the vehicle stationary,
the steering system shall verify that none of the specified failures or defects is present before
extinguishing the signal. Specified failures or defects which should activate the warning
signal mentioned above in a) and b), but which are not detected under static conditions,
shall be stored upon detection and be displayed at start-up and at all times when the ignition
(start) switch is in the "on" (run) position, as long as the failure persists.

5. Provisions for motor vehicles (except trailers)
A. It shall be possible to leave a curve with a radius of 50m at a tangent without unusual vibration
in the steering equipment at the following speed:
1) passenger cars: 50km/h
2) vehicles other than passenger cars: 40km/h or the maximum design speed if this is below the
speeds given above.
B. When the vehicle is driven in a circle with its steered wheels at approximately half lock and a
constant speed of at least 10km/h, the turning circle shall remain the same or become larger if
the steering control is released.

Measurement
The measurement of steering efforts on motor vehicles with intact steering equipment, and
with a failure in the steering equipment.
The vehicle shall be driven from straight ahead into a spiral at a speed of 10km/h. The
steering wheel control effort shall be measured at the nominal radius of the steering
control until the position of the steering control corresponds to turning radius given above
for the particular category of vehicle with intact steering, and with a failure in the steering
equipment.Remark:
1. 500 for rigid vehicles with 2 or more steered axles excluding self tracking equipment.
2. "Steering time" means the period of time from the beginning of the movement of the steering
control to the movement at which the steered wheels have reached a specific steering angle.
3. "Turning circle" means the circle within which are located the projections onto the ground plane
of all the points of the vehicle excluding the external mirrors, when the vehicle is driven in a
circle.
4. "Nominal radius of steering control" means in the case of a steering wheel the shortest dimension
from its center of rotation to the outer edge of the rim. In the case of any other form of control it
means the distance between its center of rotation and the point at which the steering effort is
applied. If more than one such point is provided, the one requiring the greatest effort shall be
used.
