8. Additional provisions for vehicles equipped with auxiliary steering equipment (ASE)
A. Specific provisionsMechanical steering transmissionsArticle 14 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 9 applies.Hydraulic steering transmissionsShall be protected from exceeding the maximum permittedservice pressure T.
Electric steering transmissionsShall be protected from excess energy supply.Combination of steering transmissionsA combination of mechanical, hydraulic and electric
transmissions shall comply with each of the above requirements.
Remark:
1. "Purely mechanical steering transmission" means a steering transmission in which the steering
forces are transmitted entirely by mechanical means.
2. "Purely hydraulic steering transmission" means a steering transmission in which the steering
forces, somewhere in the transmission, are transmitted only by hydraulic means.
3. "Purely electric steering transmission" means a steering transmission in which the steering
forces, somewhere in the transmission, are transmitted only through electric means.
4. "Hybrid steering transmission" means a steering transmission in which part of the steering
forces is transmitted through one and the other part through another of the above mentioned
means. However, in the case where any mechanical part of the transmission is designed only
to give position feedback and is too weak to transmit the total sum of the steering forces, this
system shall be considered to be purely hydraulic or purely electric steering transmission.

9. Provisions for trailers having hydraulic steering transmissions
(not translated, not applicable to PC)

10. Provisions for the vehicle equipped with Advanced Driver Assistance Steering Systems
A. Provisions for ADASS equipped with ACSF
1) ACSF of Category Aa) General
(1) The electronic control system shall only operate until 10 km/h (+2 km/h tolerance)
(2) The electronic control system shall be active only after a deliberate action of the driver
and if the conditions for operation of the electronic control system are fulfilled (all
associated functions - e.g. brakes, accelerator, steering, camera/radar/lidar - are working
properly)
(3) In case the electronic control system includes accelerator and/or braking control of the
vehicle, the vehicle shall be equipped with a means to detect an obstacle (e.g. vehicles,
pedestrian) in the manoeuvring area and to bring the vehicle immediately to a stop to
avoid a collision
(4) Whenever the electronic control system becomes operational, this shall be indicated to
the driver.
(5) Any termination of the electronic control system shall produce a distinctive driver
warning by signals specified in any one of the following items.
(a) an optical warning signal and an acoustic warning signal
(b) an optical warning signal and a haptic warning signal (except for the signal on the
steering control in parking manoeuvring)

(c) For RCP, an optical warning signal at the remote control device
b) Additional provisions for RCP
(1) The parking manoeuvre shall be initiated by the driver but controlled by the system. A
direct influence on steering angle, value of acceleration and deceleration via the remote
control device shall not be possible
(2) A continuous actuation of the remote control device by the driver is required during the
parking manoeuvre
(3) The vehicle shall stop immediately if it is applicable to any of the following items
during the parking manoeuvre(a) If the continuous actuation is interrupted
(b) If the distance between vehicle and remote control device exceeds the specified
maximum RCP operating range (SRCPmax)
(c) If the signal between remote control and vehicle is lost
(d) If a door or trunk of the vehicle is opened
(4) If the vehicle has reached its final parking position, either automatically or by
confirmation from the driver, and the start/run switch is in the off position, the parking
braking system shall be automatically engaged
(5) At any time during a parking manoeuvre that the vehicle becomes stationary, the RCP
function shall prevent the vehicle from rolling away
(6) The specified maximum RCP operating range shall not exceed 6m
(7) The electronic control system shall be designed to be protected against unauthorized
activation or operation of the RCP systems and interventions into the system
2) ACSF of Category Ba) General
(1) The electronic control system shall at any time, within the boundary conditions, ensure
that the vehicle does not cross a lane marking for lateral accelerations not exceeding the
maximum lateral acceleration specified by the vehicle manufacturer aysmax.
(2) The electronic control system may exceed the maximum lateral acceleration specified
by the vehicle manufacturer aysmax by not more than 0.3m/s², while not exceeding the
maximum value specified in the table of (4)(b).
(3) The vehicle shall be equipped with a means for the driver to activate (standby mode)
and deactivate (off mode) the electronic control system as specified below.
(a) It shall be possible to deactivate (off mode) the electronic control system at any time
by a single action of the driver.
(b) Following this action of (a), the electronic control system shall only become active
again as a result of a deliberate action by the driver.
(4) The electronic control system shall be designed so that excessive intervention of
steering control is suppressed to ensure the steering operability by the driver and to avoid
unexpected vehicle behaviour, during its operation. To ensure this, the following
requirements shall be fulfilled:
(a) The steering control effort necessary to override the directional control provided by
the electronic control system shall not exceed 50 N.
(b) The specified maximum lateral acceleration specified by the vehicle manufacturer
aysmax shall be within the limits as defined in the following table.

(5) When the electronic control system is active and in the speed range between 10 km/h

control, an optical warning signal shall indicate to the driver to place their hands on
the steering control.

showing hands and the steering control and may be accompanied by additional
explanatory text or warning symbols.

(c) Notwithstanding the optical warning signal pursuant to (a) above, if, after a period

hands or steering control in the pictorial information provided as optical warning
signal shall be shown in red and an acoustic warning signal shall be provided.
(d) The warning signals pursuant to (a) through (c) shall be active until the driver is
holding the steering control, or until the electronic control system is deactivated,
either manually or automatically.
(e) The electronic control system shall be automatically deactivated (off mode) at the
latest 30 s after the acoustic warning signal pursuant to (c) has started. After
deactivation the electronic control system shall clearly inform the driver about this
system status by an acoustic emergency signal which is different from the previous
acoustic warning signal, for at least five seconds or until the driver holds the steering
control again.
(6) Unless otherwise specified, the optical signals described in (1) through (5) above shall
all be different from each other (e.g. different symbol, colour, blinking, text).
3) ACSF of Category Ca) General
(1) A vehicle equipped with an ACSF of Category C shall also be equipped with an ACSF
of Category B complying with the requirements of A. 2) above
(2) When the ACSF of Category C is activated (standby) the ACSF of Category B shall
aim to center the vehicle in the lane.
b) Requirements for activation/deactivation of the electronic control system
(1) The default status of the electronic control system shall be off at the initiation of each
new engine start/run cycle. However, this requirement does not apply when a new
engine start/run cycle is performed automatically, e.g. the operation of a stop/start
system.
(2) The vehicle shall be equipped with a means for the driver to activate (standby mode)
and deactivate (off mode) the electronic control system as specified below. The same
means as for an ACSF of Category B may be used.
(a) It shall be possible to deactivate the electronic control system (off mode) at any time
by a single action of the driver.
(b) Following this action of (a), the electronic control system shall only be able to be
reactivated (standby mode) by a deliberate action of the driver.
(3) The electronic control system shall meet the operating conditions as below
(a) The electronic control system shall only be activated (standby mode) after a
deliberate action by the driver.
(b) The electronic control system shall be operated only on the road meeting the
conditions of the following roads and these conditions shall be ensured by the use of
at least two independent means(1) road where pedestrians and cyclists are prohibited
(2) road which, by design, are equipped with a physical separation that divides the
traffic moving in opposite directions such as median strip, etc.
(3) road which have at least two lanes in the direction the vehicles are driving
(c) In the case of a transition from a road type meeting the conditions of (b) to other road
types, an ACSF of Category C shall be deactivated automatically.
(4) Notwithstanding the requirements of (1) through (3) above, the test shall be able to be

KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
performed according to the test procedures determined and notified by the Minister of
MOLIT on the road owned by the testing agency pursuant to Article 29-2 Paragraph 1
of the MVMAC) Overriding
(1) A steering input by the driver shall override the steering action of the electronic control
system. However, the electronic control system may remain activated (standby mode)
provided that priority is given to the driver during the overriding period.
(2) The steering control effort necessary to override the directional control provided by the
electronic control system shall not exceed 50 N.
D) Lateral acceleration and lateral jerk
(1) The lateral acceleration induced by the electronic control system during the lane change
manoeuvre:
(a) Shall not exceed 1 m/s² in addition to the lateral acceleration generated by the lane
curvature
(b) Shall not cause the total vehicle lateral acceleration to exceed the maximum values
indicated in tables of A. 2). a). (4). (b) above
(2) The moving average over half a second of the lateral jerk (rate of change of lateral
acceleration) generated by the electronic control system shall not exceed 5 m/s³.
E) Human Machine Interface (HMI)
(1) Unless otherwise specified, the optical signals identified in (2) through (6) as below
shall be easily distinguishable from each other such as different symbol, colour,
blinking, text.
(2) When the electronic control system is in standby mode, an optical signal shall be
provided to the driver
(3) When the lane change procedure is ongoing an optical signal shall be provided to the
driver.
(4) When the lane change procedure is suppressed, in accordance with A. 3). F). (8) as
below, the electronic control system shall clearly inform the driver about this system
status by an optical warning signal and additionally by an acoustic or haptic warning
signal. In case the suppression is initiated by the driver, an optical warning is sufficient.
(5) If a failure occurs on the electronic control system, the following requirements shall be
met.
(a) A system failure shall be signalled immediately to the driver by an optical warning
signal. However, when the system is manually deactivated by the driver, the
indication of failure mode may be suppressed.
(b) If a system failure occurs during a lane change manoeuvre, the failure shall be
signalled to the driver by an optical, and an acoustic or haptic warning.
(6) The electronic control system shall provide a means of detecting that the driver is
holding the steering control.
(7) If, after a period of no longer than 3 seconds after the initiation of the lane change
procedure, the driver is not holding the steering control, an optical warning signal
specified in A. 2). b). (5). (b). shall be provided and be active until the driver is holding
the steering control, or until the system is deactivated, either manually or automatically.
F) Lane change procedure
(1) The initiation of a lane change procedure of an ACSF of Category C shall only be
possible if an ACSF of Category B is already active.
(2) The lane change procedure requires, and shall start immediately after, a manual
activation by the driver of the direction indicator to the intended side for the lane change.


<!-- Page 152 -->

© KAIDA
152
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
(3) When the lane change procedure starts, the ACSF of Category B shall be suspended,
and the ACSF of Category C shall carry on the lane keeping function of ACSF of
category B, until the lane change manoeuvre starts.
(4) The lateral movement, etc. on lane change procedure shall meet the requirements as
(a) The lateral movement of the vehicle towards the intended lane shall not start earlier
than 1 second after the start of the lane change procedure.
(b) Additionally, the lateral movement to approach the lane marking and the lateral
movement necessary to complete the lane change manoeuvre, shall be completed as
one continuous movement
(c) The lane change manoeuvre shall not be initiated before a period of 3.0 s and not
later than 5.0 s after a manual activation by the driver of the direction indicator to the
intended side for the lane change.
(5) The lane change manoeuvre shall be completed in less than:
(a) 5 s for PC, and Truck/SPV with GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons,
(b) 10 s for Bus, and Truck/SPV with GVW exceeding 3.5 tons.
(6) Once the lane change manoeuvre has completed, ACSF of Category B lane keeping
function shall resume automatically.
(7) The direction indicator shall remain active throughout the whole period of the lane
change manoeuvre and shall be deactivated by the electronic control system no later
than 0.5 seconds after the resumption of ACSF of Category B lane keeping function as
the lane change manoeuvre has completed.
(8) Suppression of the lane change procedure
(a) The lane change procedure shall be suppressed automatically by the electronic
control system when at least one of the following situations occurs before the lane
change manoeuvre has started:
(1) The electronic control system detects a critical situation as defined in A. 3). G).
(1),(2) The system is overridden or switched off by the driver,
(3) The system reaches its boundaries (e.g. lane markings are no longer detected)
(4) The system has detected that the driver is not holding the steering control at the
start of the lane change manoeuvre,
(5) The direction indicator lamps are manually deactivated by the driver,
(6) The lane change manoeuvre has not commenced within 5.0 s following the
activation by the driver of the direction indicator,
(7) The lateral movement of the vehicle is not continuous,
(b) Manual deactivation of the lane change procedure, using the manual control of the
direction indicator, shall be possible for the driver at any time
G) Critical situation and critical distance
(1) A situation is deemed to be critical when, at the time a lane change manoeuvre starts,
an approaching vehicle in the target lane would have to decelerate at a higher level than
3m/s², 0.4 seconds after the lane change manoeuvre has started, to ensure the distance
between the two vehicles is never less than that which the lane change vehicle travels in
1 second.
(2) The critical distance (Scritical) shall be calculated using the following formula:
Scritical=(Vrear-VACSF)×tB+ (Vrear-VACSF)2
(2×a)+VACSF×tGWhere:

H) Minimum distance and minimum operation speed
(1) The ACSF of Category C shall be able to detect vehicles approaching from the rear in
an adjacent lane up to a distance Srear specified in below.
(b) The minimum distance (Srear) shall be declared by the vehicle manufacturer. The

(c) The system shall be tested if it is able to detect vehicles approaching from the rear in

procedures determined and notified by the Minister of MOLIT

(e) Notwithstanding the requirements above A. 3). H). (1). (c) and (d), the ACSF of

(1) The system has detected another vehicle in the adjacent lane into which the lane

(2) The vehicle system detection area on ground level shall be at minimum as shown in the

(3) After each vehicle new engine start/run cycle (other than when performed
automatically, e.g. the operation of a stop/start systems), the ACSF of Category C
function shall be prevented from performing a lane change manoeuvre until the system
has detected, at least once, a moving object at a distance greater than minimum distance

(4) The ACSF of Category C shall be equipped with functions for the detect blindness as
follows;
(a) The ACSF of Category C shall be able to detect blindness of the sensor due to
accumulation of dirt, ice or snow, etc.
(b) The ACSF of Category C shall be prevented, upon detection of blindness, from
performing the lane change manoeuvre procedure
(c) The status of the electronic control system shall be signalled to the driver no later
than on the initiation of the lane change manoeuvre. In this case, the system failure
warning specified in A. 3). E). (5). may be used as a warning for sensor blindness.
B. Requirements for ADASS equipped with Corrective Steering Function (CSF)
1) Every CSF intervention shall immediately be indicated to the driver by an optical warning
signal which is displayed for at least 1 s or as long as the intervention exists, whichever is
longer. However, in the case of a CSF intervention which is controlled by an Electronic
Stability Control (ESC) or a Vehicle Stability Function as specified in Article 90-2, the ESC
flashing tell-tale indicating the interventions of ESC may be used, as long as the intervention
exists, as an alternative to the optical warning signal specified above.
2) In the case of a CSF intervention which is based on the evaluation of the presence and location
of lane markings or boundaries of the lane the following shall apply additionally:
a) In the case of an intervention longer than:
(1) 10 s for PC, and truck and special purpose vehicle with GVW≤ 3.5 tons,
(2) 30 s for bus, and truck and special purpose vehicle with GVW> 3.5 tons,
an acoustic warning signal shall be provided until the end of the intervention
b) In the case of two or more consecutive interventions within a rolling interval of 180
seconds and in the absence of a steering input by the driver during the intervention,
an acoustic warning signal shall be provided by the system during the second and any
further intervention within a rolling interval of 180 seconds. Starting with the third
intervention and subsequent interventions the acoustic warning signal shall continue
for at least 10 seconds longer than the previous warning signal.
3) The steering control effort necessary to override the directional control provided by the
A. 3). H). (1)A. 3). H). (1)

system shall not exceed 50 N in the whole range of CSF operations.
C. Requirements for ADASS equipped with Emergency Steering Function (ESF)
1) Any ESF shall only start an intervention in the case where a risk of a collision is detected.
2) Any vehicle fitted with ESF shall be equipped with means to monitor the driving environment
such as lane markings, road edge, other road users. These means shall monitor the driving
environment at any time the ESF is active.
3) An automatic avoidance manoeuvre initiated by an ESF shall not lead the vehicle to leave
the road.
a) In the case of an ESF intervention on a road or a lane delimited with lane markings, an
automatic avoidance manoeuver initiated by an ESF shall not lead the vehicle to cross a
lane marking. However, if the intervention starts during a lane change performed by the
driver or during an unintentional drift into the adjacent lane, the system may steer the
vehicle back into its original lane of travel.
b) In the absence of a lane marking on one or on both side(s) of the vehicle, a single ESF
intervention is permitted, provided that it does not produce a lateral offset of the vehicle
greater than 0.75 m in a direction where the lane marking is absent.
4) The ESF intervention shall not lead the vehicle to collide with another road user.
5) Any intervention of an ESF shall be indicated to the driver with an optical and with an
acoustic or haptic warning signal to be provided at the latest with the start of the ESF
intervention. However, for this purpose directionally appropriate signals used by other
warning systems, such as blind spot detection, lane departure warning, forward collision
warning, are deemed to be sufficient to fulfil the requirements for the respective optical,
acoustic or haptic signals above.
6) A system failure shall be indicated to the driver with an optical warning signal. However,
when the system is manually deactivated, the indication of failure mode may be suppressed.
7) The steering control effort necessary to override the directional control provided by the
system shall not exceed 50 N.Remark:
1. "Automatically commanded steering function (ACSF)" means a function within an electronic
control system where actuation of the steering system can result from automatic evaluation of
signals initiated on-board the vehicle, possibly in conjunction with passive infrastructure
features such as lane, to generate control action in order to assist the driver.
a) "ACSF of Category A" means a function that operates at a speed no greater than 10 km/h to
assist the driver, on demand, in low speed or parking maneuvering.
b) "ACSF of Category B" means a function which assists the driver in keeping the vehicle within
the chosen lane, by influencing the lateral movement of the vehicle.
c) "ACSF of Category C" means, a function which is initiated/activated by the driver and which
can perform a single lateral maneuver such as lane change when commanded by the driver.
2. "Corrective Steering Function (CSF)" means a control function within an electronic control
system whereby, for a limited duration, changes to the steering angle of one or more wheels may
result from the automatic evaluation of signals initiated on-board the vehicle, in order:
a) To compensate a sudden, unexpected change in the side force of the vehicle
b) To improve the vehicle stability for side wind, differing adhesion road conditions "μ-split",
etc.
c) To correct lane departure to avoid crossing lane markings, leaving the road, etc.
3. "Emergency Steering Function (ESF)" means a control function which can automatically detect
a potential collision and automatically activate the vehicle steering system for a limited duration,
to steer the vehicle with the purpose of avoiding or mitigating a collision, with:


<!-- Page 156 -->

© KAIDA
156
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
a) another vehicle driving in an adjacent lane, drifting towards the path of the subject vehicle
and/or,
b) another vehicle driving in an adjacent lane, into which path the subject vehicle is drifting
and/or,
c) another vehicle driving in an adjacent lane, into which lane the driver initiates a lane change
manoeuvre.
d) an obstacle obstructing the path of the subject vehicle or when the obstruction of the subject
vehicle's path is deemed imminent.
4. "Remote Controlled Parking (RCP)" means an ACSF of category A, actuated by the driver,
providing automatic parking or low speed maneuvering. The actuation is made by remote control
in close proximity to the vehicle.
5. "Specified maximum RCP operating range (SRCPmax)" means the maximum distance between the
nearest point of the motor vehicle and the remote control device up to which ACSF is designed
to operate.
6. "Specified maximum speed Vsmax " means the maximum speed up to which an ACSF is designed
to operate.
7. "Specified minimum speed Vsmin" means the minimum speed down to which an ACSF is
designed to operate.
8. "Specified maximum lateral acceleration aysmax" means the maximum lateral acceleration of the
vehicle up to which an ACSF is designed to operate.
9. An ACSF is in "off mode" or "switched off" when the function is prevented from generating a
steering control action to assist the driver.
10. An ACSF is in "standby mode" when the function is switched on but the system operating
conditions for being active are not all met. In this mode, the system is not ready to generate a
steering control action to assist the driver.
11. An ACSF is in "active mode" or "active" when the function is switched on and the conditions
for being active are met. In this mode, the system continuously or discontinuously controls the
steering system is generating, or is ready to generate, a steering control action to assist the driver.
12. A 'lane change procedure' starts when the direction indicator lamps are activated by a deliberate
action of the driver and ends when the direction indicator lamps are deactivated. It comprises
the following operations:
A. Activation of the direction indicator lamps by a deliberate action of the driver
B. Lateral movement of the vehicle towards the lane boundary
C. Lane change manoeuvreD. Resumption of the lane keeping functionE. Deactivation of direction indicator lamps

the vehicle have fully crossed the lane marking.

Installation And Luminous Intensity Requirements of Driving Beam (Main Beam) Headlamp
(Article 38 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirements of driving beam headlamp
A. Installation position
The lamp shall be installed so that it may not distract the driver through the direct or indirect
reflection of the vehicle structure.B. Observation angle
The visibility of the apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 5 degrees
upwards, downwards, inwards and outwards.
C. Orientationa. The illuminating direction shall be toward the front.
b. Not more than one main-beam headlamp on each side of the vehicle may swivel to produce
bend lighting.D. Operation requirements
1) Except when they are used to give intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals the main-
beam headlamps may be switched ON, only when the master light switch is in headlamps ON
position or in "AUTO" (automatic) position and the conditions for automatic activation of
dipped-beam exist. The main beam headlamps shall be switched off automatically when the
conditions for automatic activation of dipped-beam ceased to exist.
2) The control of the main-beam headlamps may be automatic regarding their activation and
deactivation, the control signals being produced by a sensor system which is capable of
detecting and reacting to each of the following inputs:
a) Ambient lighting conditions;
b) The light emitted by the front lighting devices and front light-signaling devices of
oncoming vehicles;
c) The light emitted by the rear light-signaling devices of preceding vehicles.
d) For the purpose of a) through c) above, "vehicles" means vehicles, motorcycles, and
bicycles according to Item F' 2), A), (2), (c), such vehicles being equipped with
retroreflectors, with lighting and light-signalling devices, which are switched ON
3) It shall always be possible to switch the main-beam headlamps ON and OFF manually and to
manually switch OFF the automatic control of the main-beam headlamps. Moreover, the
switching OFF, of the main-beam headlamps and of their automatic control, shall be by means
of a simple and immediate manual operation; the use of sub-menus is not allowed.
4) The main-beam headlamps may be switched on either simultaneously or in pairs. For
changing over from the dipped to the main beam at least one pair of main-beam headlamps
shall be switched on. For changing over from the main-beam to the dipped-beam all main-
beam headlamps shall be switched off simultaneously.
5) The dipped-beams may be switched on or off at the same time as the main beams.
6) Where four concealable headlamps are fitted, they shall prevent the simultaneous operation
of any additional headlamps fitted, even if the driving beam is used intermittently for a short
time.E. Tell-tale
1) The tell-tale to indicate the operation status of the lamp shall be installed.
2) If the control of the main-beam headlamps is automatic as described Item D' 1) above, an
indication shall be provided to the driver that the automatic control of the main-beam function

is activated. This information shall remain displayed as long as the automatic operation is
activated.F. Other requirements
1) The aggregate maximum intensity of the main-beam headlamps which can be switched on
simultaneously shall not exceed 430,000 cd.
2) Automatic activation and deactivation of the main-beam headlamps
A) The sensor system used to control the automatic activation and deactivation of the main-
beam headlamps, as described in Item D' 1) shall comply with the following requirements:
(1) The boundaries of the minimum fields in which the sensor is able to detect light emitted
from other vehicles defined in Item D' 1) above are defined by the angles indicated below
(a) Horizontal angle: 15° to the left and 15° to the right.
(b) Vertical angleUpward angle5 degreesMounting height of the sensor (center ofsensor aperture above the ground)Less than 2 m
Between 1.5 m and 2.5 mGreater than 2 mDownward angle2 degrees2-5 degrees5 degrees
These angles are measured from the center of the sensor aperture relative to a horizontal
straight line through its center and parallel to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.
(2) The sensor system shall be able to detect on a straight level road and the oncoming and
preceding power-driven vehicle (or vehicle-trailer combination) shall have position lamps,
rear position lamp and dipped-beam headlamps switched ON.
(a) An oncoming power-driven vehicle at a distance extending to at least 400 m;
(b) A preceding power-driven vehicle or a vehicle-trailers combination at a distance
extending to at least 100 m;
(c) An oncoming bicycle at a distance extending to at least 75 m, its illumination
represented by a white lamp with a luminous intensity of 150 cd with a light emitting
area of 10 cm² ± 3 cm² and a height above a ground of 0.8 m.
B) The transition from main-beam to dipped-beam and vice versa according to the conditions
indicated in Item D', 1) above may be performed automatically and shall not cause any
distraction.
C) The overall performance of the automatic control shall be verified by means of simulation
or other means of verification
D) The main-beam headlamps are switched ON automatically only when
(1) No vehicles, as mentioned in Item D', 1) above, are detected within the fields and
distances according to A) and B).
(2) The detected ambient lighting levels are as prescribed in E) below.
E) In the case where main-beam headlamps are switched ON automatically, they shall be
switched OFF automatically when
(1) oncoming or preceding vehicles, as mentioned in Item D', 1) above, are detected within
the fields and distances according to A) and B).
(2) the illuminance produced by ambient lighting conditions exceeds 7000 lx.
F) The automatic ON/OFF of main beam shall be demonstrated by the manufacturer, using
simulation or other means of verification. The illuminance shall be measured on a
horizontal surface on the same height as the mounting position of the sensor.

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Passing Beam (Dipped-Beam)
Headlamp (Article 38 Paragraph 2 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirements of passing beam headlamp
A. Installation requirements1) In width
A) The outermost edge of apparent surface for passing beam shall be not more than 400 mm
form the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
B) The apparent surfaces in the direction of reference axis shall be not less than 600mm apart
except passenger cars, trucks and special purpose vehicles with GVW not exceeding 3.5
tons. However, this distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the
vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.2) In height
The apparent surface for passing beam shall not be less than 500mm and not more than
1,200mm above the ground in unloaded state.
B. Observation angle
1) The visibility of the apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 15 degrees
upwards, 10 degrees downwards, 45 degrees outwards and 10 degrees inwards.
C. Orientation
1)The illuminating direction of the lamp shall be towards the front.
2) Vertical orientation
A) Depending on the mounting height (the lower edge of the apparent surface) the vertical
inclination of the cut-off shall meet the following requirements:
(1) Mounting height ≤ 0.8 meter(A) Limits: -0.5% - -2.5%(B) Initial aiming: -1.0% - -1.5%(2) 0.8 meter < Mounting height ≤ 1.0 meter(A) Limits: -0.5% - -2.5%(B) Initial aiming: -1.0% - -1.5%
Or, at the discretion of the manufacturer, Limits: -1.0% - -3.0% and Initial aiming: -1.5%
- -2.0% are acceptable.(3) Mounting height > 1 meter(A) Limits: -1.0% - -3.0%(B) Initial aiming: -1.5% - -2.0%
B) The vertical inclination of the cut-off shall be measured with a precision of 0.1%.
3) Headlamp leveling device
A) The passing beam headlamp shall be equipped with the head lamp leveling device in
compliance with the requirements in 2) above and the headlamp leveling device shall be
automatic.
B) However, devices which are adjusted manually, either continuously or non-continuously,
shall be permitted, provided they have a stop position at which the lamps can be returned
to the initial inclination by means of the usual adjusting screws or similar means.
C) These manually adjustable devices shall be operable from the driver's seat.
D) The devices which are not continuously adjustable shall be such as to ensure compliance
with the requirements of vertical inclination prescribed in 2).
E) In the event of a failure of the leveling devices subject to A) through D), the cut-off shall


<!-- Page 163 -->

© KAIDA
163
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
not be positioned higher than it was positioned at the time when the failure of the device
occurred.4) Horizontal orientation
The horizontal orientation of one or both passing beam headlamps or the elbow kink cut-off
may be varied to produce bend lighting, provided that the kink of the elbow of the cut-off
shall not intersect the line of the trajectory of the center of gravity of the vehicle at distances
from the front of the vehicle which are larger than 100 times the mounting height of the
respective passing beam headlamps.D. Operation requirements
1) For changing from the passing beams to the driving beams, the passing beam headlamps may
remain switched on.
2) In the case of the passing beam headlamps with the gas discharge light sources, the passing
beam headlamps shall remain switched on for changing from the passing beams to the driving
beams.
3) One additional light source, located inside the passing beam (except the driving beam
headlamp), may be activated to produce bend lighting, provided that the turning radius of the
vehicle is 500 m or less.
4) Passing beams may be switched ON or OFF automatically. However, it shall be always
possible to switch these passing beam headlamps ON and OFF manually.
5) If daytime running lamps are present and any one of following requirements shall be met.
A) The dipped-beam headlamps shall be switched ON and OFF automatically relative to the
ambient light conditions according to the requirements of Table in Item C) (3)
B) Daytime running lamps may operate in conjunction with the position lamp, rear position
lamp, end-outline marker lamp, side marker lamp, and license plate lamp, and, as a
minimum requirement, at least, shall be activated simultaneously with the rear position
lamps;
C) Distinctive means are provided to inform the driver that the headlamps, position lamps,
end-outline marker lamps and side marker lamps are not illuminated. Such means are:
(1) Two distinctly different levels of instrument panel illumination intensity are provided
during night and day
(2) Identification of hand controls that are required by Table 2 shall be illuminated when
the passing beam headlamps are activated;
(3) A tell-tale visual, auditory or both, shall be activated only in reduced ambient lighting
conditions as below to inform the driver that the dipped-beam headlamps should be
switched ON. The tell-tale shall not be activated, when the dipped-beam headlamps have
been switched on or the device which starts and/or stops the engine is set in a position
which makes it impossible for the engine to operate.

6) Notwithstanding 5) A), the dipped-beam headlamps may switch ON and OFF automatically
relative to other factors such as time or ambient conditions (e.g. time of the day, vehicle
location, rain, fog, etc.)E. Tell-tale
1) The tell-tale to indicate the operation status of the lamp may be installed
2) A flashing or lit-type tell-tale for failure shall be installed for any one of following cases. It
shall remain activated while the failure is present.
A) In the case where the whole beam or the kink of the elbow of the cut-off is moved to
produce bend lighting.
B) If one or more LED modules are used to produce the principal passing beam except when
they are wired so that the failure of any one LED module causes all of them to stop emitting
light.
3) A tell-tale for failure may be cancelled temporarily, but shall be repeated whenever the device,
which starts and stops the engine, is switched on and off.
F. Other requirements
1) Be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane, this requirement
is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp. But it shall not apply to dipped-
beam headlamps.
2) Dipped-beam headlamps with a light source or LED module (s) producing the principal
dipped-beam and having a total objective luminous flux which exceeds 2,000 lumen shall
only be equipped with the headlamp cleaning device, but the manual leveling device specified
in Item C', 3), B) shall not be installed.
3) If bend lighting is produced by a horizontal movement of the whole beam or the kink of the
elbow of the cut-off, it shall be activated only if the vehicle is in forward motion and is steered
to the right.

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Adaptive Front Lighting System
(AFS) (Article 38 Paragraph 3 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirements of AFSA. Installation position
1) The installation position of AFS shall, at the neutral state, meet the requirements.
2) In width and height
AFS lighting unit (it means a component which is designed to provide one or more front
lighting functions provided by the AFS) shall meet the requirements indicated in the Items. B)
through E) below by measuring the outermost apparent surface. It shall be fulfilled by those
lighting units (AFS in conjunction with other lighting systems) which are energized
simultaneously
A) Two symmetrically placed lighting units shall be positioned at a height in compliance with
the requirements specified in Subparagraph 1, Item A' of Table 6-3 and Subparagraph 1
Item A' of Table 6-4.
B) Two symmetrically placed lighting units shall be positioned at the height and at the distance
from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane within a tolerance of 50 mm.
C) Additional lighting units on either side of the vehicle shall be positioned at a distance not
exceeding 140 mm (E in the figure) and not exceeding 200 mm in case of "two
symmetrically placed lighting units" (C in the figure) in horizontal direction, and not
exceeding 400 mm in vertical direction (D in the figure) from the nearest lighting unit.
D) None of the additional lighting units shall be positioned lower than 250 mm (F in the figure)
nor higher than 1200mm (G in the figure) above the ground in unloaded state.
E) Additionally, for each mode of the passing beam
(1) The outer edge of the apparent surface of at least one lighting unit on each side of the
vehicle shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle (A in
the figure)
(2) The apparent surfaces for each mode shall be not less than 600 mm (B in the figure)
apart, except passenger cars, and trucks and special purpose vehicles with GVW not
exceeding 3.5 tons; this distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of
the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.

<Apparent surfaces of lighting units of AFS>

B. Observation angle
1) The observation angle of driving beam shall meet the requirements specified in Subparagraph
1. Item B' of Table 6-3.
2) The observation angle of passing beam shall meet the requirements specified in Subparagraph
1. Item B' of Table 6-4.
3) The requirements of 1) & 2) shall be met in case of the lighting units for each function.
C. Orientation
The illuminating direction shall be towards the front and the requirements shall be met where
the AFS is set to neutral state emitting the basic passing beam.
1) Vertical orientation
A) The inclination of cut-off shall be checked with a driver seated with a precision of 0.1
percent.
B) The vertical inclination of cut-off shall meet Subparagraph 1 Item C' 2) of Table 6-4.
C) In case the passing beam is generated by several beams from different lighting units, the
requirements specified in B) shall be met.
2) Headlamp leveling device


<!-- Page 171 -->

© KAIDA

KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
A) The leveling device to satisfy 1) may be installed and the device shall be automatic.
B) In the event of a failure of the leveling device, the cut-off shall not be positioned higher
than it was positioned at the time when the failure of the device occurred.
3) Horizontal orientation
For each lighting unit, the kink of the elbow of the cut-off line, if any, shall coincide with the
vertical line through the reference axis of said lighting unit. A tolerance of 0.5 degrees to the
right side shall be allowed.4) Measuring procedure
A) After the initial aiming, the vertical inclinations of the passing beam or of basic passing
beam illuminated from the different lighting units shall meet the requirements in 1), B)
B) The measurement of the variation of vertical inclination of passing beam shall comply with
Subparagraph 1 Item C', 2) in Table 6-4.
D. Operation requirements1) Driving beam
A) The lighting units for the driving beam may be activated either simultaneously or in pairs.
However, for changing over from the passing beam to the driving beam at least one pair of
lighting units for the main-beam shall be activated, and for changing over from the driving
beam to the passing beam, all lighting units for the main-beam shall be de-activated
simultaneously.
B) The main-beam may be designed to be adaptive, subject to the provisions in Item F' 3), the
control signals being produced by a sensor system (Additional sensor functions are allowed)
which is capable of detecting and reacting to each of the following inputs:
(1) Ambient lighting conditions;
(2) The light emitted by the front lighting devices and front light-signaling devices of
oncoming vehicles;
(3) The light emitted by the rear light-signaling devices of preceding vehicles.
(4) For the purpose of (1) through (3) above, "vehicles" means vehicles, motorcycles, and
bicycles according to Item F' 2), A), (2), (c) of Table 6-3 Subparagraph 1, such vehicles
being equipped with retroreflectors, with lighting and light-signalling devices, which are
switched ON.
C) It shall always be possible to switch the main-beam headlamps, adaptive or non-adaptive,
ON and OFF manually and to manually switch OFF the automatic control. Moreover, the
switching OFF, of the main-beam headlamps and of their automatic control, shall be by
means of a simple manual operation; the use of sub-menus is not allowed.
D) Where four concealable lighting units are fitted, it shall prevent the simultaneous operation
of any additional headlamps fitted, even if these are intended to provide light signals
consisting of intermittent illumination at short intervals.
2) Passing beam
A) For changing over to the passing beam, all driving beam headlamps or lighting units shall
be switched off.
B) For changing over from the passing beam to the driving beam, the passing beam may
remain switched on.
C) In the case of lighting units for the passing beam being equipped with gas discharge light
sources, for changing over to the driving beam the passing beam shall remain switched on.
3) Switching ON and OFF the passing beam may be automatic.
4) Automatic operation of the AFS
The selection of proper mode of AFS lighting functions and the change of its mode shall be
performed automatically and such that no distraction, neither for the driver nor for other road


<!-- Page 172 -->

© KAIDA
172
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
users, is caused. If AFS driving beam is operated, it shall meet the next following requirements
below.
A) The basic mode shall be activated if no mode of another passing beam class is activated.
B) The city mode (V signal) shall operate if one or more of the following conditions are
automatically detected
(1) Roads in built-up areas and the vehicle's speed not exceeding 60 km/h;
(2) Roads equipped with a fixed road illumination, and the vehicle's speed not exceeding
60 km/h;
(3) A road surface luminance of 1 cd/m2 and/or a horizontal road illumination of 10 lx being
exceeded continuously(4) The vehicle's speed not exceeding 50 km/h.
C) The highway mode (E mode) shall operate if the vehicle's speed exceeds 60 km/h and one
or more of the following conditions are automatically detected.
(1) E signal: Road characteristics correspond to highway conditions or the vehicle's speed
exceeds 110 km/h(2) E1 signal: the vehicle's speed exceeds 100 km/h(3) E2 signal: the vehicle's speed exceeds 90 km/h(4) E3 signal: the vehicle's speed exceeds 80 km/h
D) The wet road mode (W signal) shall operate if the front fog lamps are switched OFF and
one or more of the following conditions are automatically detected:
(1) The wetness of the road has been detected automatically;
(2) The windshield wiper is switched ON and its continuous or automatically controlled
operation has occurred for a period of at least two minutes.
E) For each mode, if the angle change of steering system or the trajectory of a vehicle's gravity
center is modified, a bending mode satisfying the requirements below shall be operable
(1) If bend lighting is produced by a horizontal movement of the whole beam or the kink
of the elbow of the cut-off, it shall be activated only if the vehicle is in forward motion
and is steered to the right.
(2) The kink of the elbow of the cut-off shall not intersect the line of the trajectory of the
center of gravity of the vehicle at distances from the front of the vehicle which are larger
than 100 times the mounting height of passing beam.
(3) One or more lighting units may be additionally energized only when the turning radius
the vehicle is 500 m or less.
F) It shall be possible for the driver to set the AFS to the neutral state and to return it to its
automatic operation.E. Tell-tale
1) The AFS shall meet Subparagraph 1 Item E' of Table 6-3 and Subparagraph 1 Item E' of Table
6-4.2) A lit-type failure tell-tale shall be installed.
3) A failure tell-tale shall be activated whenever a failure is detected with respect to the AFS
control signals or lighting source. It shall remain activated continuously while the failure is
present.
4) It may be cancelled temporarily when engine stops, but shall be reactivated when the engine
starts.
5) If the main-beam is adaptive, a visual tell-tale shall be provided to indicate to the driver that
the adaptation of the main beam is activated. However, for non-AFS driving beam, the
manufacturer may install the tell-tale optionally.

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Front Fog Lamp
(Article 38-2 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirements of front fog lamp
A. Installation requirements1) In width
The outermost point on the apparent surface shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme
outer edge of the vehicle.2) In height
A) The apparent surface of front fog lamp, installed in PC and trucks and special purpose
vehicles with GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons, shall not be less than 250mm and not more than
800mm above the ground in unloaded state, however, it shall be not more than 1,200mm
for other vehicles.
B) No point on the apparent surface shall be higher than the highest point on the apparent
surface of the passing beam.B. Observation angle
The visibility of apparent surface for front fog lamp shall be ensured in any angle of not more
than 5 degrees upwards, 5 degrees downwards, 45 degrees outwards and 10 degrees inwards.
C. Orientation
1) The illuminating direction shall be towards the front of vehicle.
2) Vertical orientation
A) In the case of class B front fog lamps (the fog lamp which is illuminated by the light source
of filament), the vertical inclination of the cut-off to be set in the unloaded vehicle state
with one person in the driver's seat shall be -1.5 percent or lower.
B) In the case of class F3 front fog lamp (it means a fog lamp illuminated by the light source
of filament, gas discharge, or a light-emitting display)
(1) When the total objective luminous flux of the light source does not exceed 2,000 lumens,
the vertical inclination of the cut-off to be set in the unloaded vehicle state with one
person in the driver´s seat shall be -1.0 per cent or lower
(2) When the total objective luminous flux of the light source exceeds 2,000 lumens, the
installation height is measured on the unloaded vehicles, the vertical inclination of the
cut-off shall automatically remain between the following values:
(A) h ≤ 0.8 meter(1) Limits: between -1.0 per cent and -3.0 per cent(2) Initial aiming: between -1.5 per cent and -2.0 per cent(B) h > 0.8 meter(1) Limits: between -1.5 per cent and - 3.5 per cent(2) Initial aiming: between -2.0 per cent and -2.5 per cent
C) The leveling device
(1) Where a levelling device is fitted for a front fog lamp, independent or grouped with
other front lighting and light signaling functions, it shall comply with the requirements
in 2) b) (2).
(2) In the case where the front fog lamp of category F3 is part of the passing beam headlamp
or is part of an AFS system, the requirements of Subparagraph 1. Item C in Table 6-4
shall be met when it is switched on. However, the orientation specified in Table 6-4
Subparagraph 1 Item C' may apply to F3 front fog lamp.


<!-- Page 178 -->

© KAIDA
178
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
(3) The levelling device may also be used to automatically adapt the inclination of the front
fog beam according to ambient conditions, if meeting the requirements in 2) b) (2).
(4) In the event of a failure of the leveling device, the cut-off shall not be positioned higher
than it was positioned at the time when the failure of the device occurred.
D. Operation requirements
1) It shall be possible to switch the front fog lamps ON and OFF independently.
2) The switching ON of the front fog lamps function shall have the priority over the function for
which the front fog lamps are used as a part of an AFS.
E. Tell-tale
The lit type tell-tale to indicate the operation status of the lamp shall be installed.
F. Other requirements
The luminous intensity of F3 front fog beam may be automatically adapted in relation to the
prevailing ambient conditions.

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Rear Fog Lamp
(Article 38-2 Paragraph 2 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirements of rear fog lamp
A. Installation requirements1) In width
If there is only one rear fog-lamp, it shall be on the left side of the median longitudinal plane
of the vehicle or the center of a vehicle.
2) In height
A) The apparent surface shall be not less than 250mm and not more than 1000mm above the
ground in unloaded state. However, if incorporated with other lamps installed in the rear
side (it means that the same body is used though the apparent surface and source of light
are separated from each other in the direction of reference axis), the maximum height may
be increased to 1,200 mm.B. Observation angle
The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 5 degrees
upwards and downwards and 25 degrees outwards and inwards.
C. Orientation
The illuminating direction shall be rearwards of the vehicle.
D. Operation requirements
1) The rear fog-lamp(s) can be switched on if the driving head lamps, passing head lamps or
front fog-lamps are lit;
2) The rear fog-lamp can be switched off independently of any other lamp;
3) Either of the following applies:
A) The rear fog lamp may continue to operate until the rear position lamps are switched off,
and the rear fog lamp shall then remain off until deliberately switched on again;
B) An audible warning shall be given if the ignition is switched off or the ignition key is
withdrawn and the driver's door is opened, whilst the rear fog lamp switch is in the "on"
position.
4) The rear fog lamp of a towing vehicle shall be automatically switched off while a trailer is
connected and the rear fog lamp of the trailer is activated.
E. Tell-tale
The lit type tell-tale to indicate the operation status of lamp shall be installed.
F. Other requirements
1) The apparent-surface distance between the rear fog-lamp and each stop-lamp shall exceed
100 mm.
2) Rear fog lamps with variable luminous intensity control are allowed.

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Daytime Running Lamp
(Article 38-4 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirements of DRLA. Installation requirements1) In width
The distance between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces of DRL shall not be less than
600mm. The distance may be reduced to 400mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less
than 1,300mm.2) In height
The apparent surfaces shall be positioned above the ground not less than 250mm nor more
than 1,500mm at unloaded status.B. Observation angle
The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 10 degrees
upwards and downwards and 20 degrees outwards and inwards.
C. Orientation
The illuminating direction shall be forwards of the vehicle.
D. Tell-tale
The lit type tell-tale to indicate the operation status of lamp may be installed.
E. Operation requirements
1) The DRL shall be switched on automatically when the engine is started, However, the daytime
running lamps may remain OFF while any one of the following conditions exist.
A) The automatic transmission control is in the park position; or
B) The parking brake is in the applied position; or
C) Prior to the vehicle being set in motion for the first time after engine on.
2) The daytime running lamps may be switched OFF manually when the vehicle speed does not
exceed 10 km/h provided they switch ON automatically when the vehicle speed exceeds 10
km/h or when the vehicle has travelled more than 100 m and they remain ON until deliberately
switched off again.
3) The DRL shall switch off automatically when headlamps or front fog lamps are switched on
or the engine is set in a position which makes it impossible for the engine to operate, except
that the driving beam headlamp is used momentarily for the purpose of warning.
4) The position lamp, rear position lamp, end-outline marker lamps, sider marker lamps and
license plate lamps may be illuminated, if DRL is incorporated with them. In this case, the
rear position lamps may be incorporated and switched on with DRL.
5) If the distance between the front direction indicator lamp and the daytime running lamp is
equal or less than 40 mm, DRL on the relevant side may be switched off, or the luminous
intensity may be reduced, during the activation of a front direction indicator lamp.
6) If a direction-indicator lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a daytime running lamp, the
electrical connections of the daytime running lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle shall be
such that the daytime running lamp is switched OFF during the entire period of activation of
the direction-indicator lamp.

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Cornering Lamp
(Article 38-5 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirements of cornering lamp
A. Installation requirements1) In width
The lamp shall be installed on the left and right side of vehicles.
2) In height
A) The apparent surface shall be not less than 250mm and not more than 900mm above the
ground in unloaded state.
B) No point on the apparent surface shall be higher than the highest point on the apparent
surface of the passing beam.3) In lengthThe lamp shall not be further than 1,000 mm from the front.B. Observation angle
The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 10 degrees
upwards and downwards and 30 degrees to 60 degrees outwards
C. Operation requirements
1) The cornering lamps shall be activated if the driving beam or the passing beam headlamps are
switched ON.
2) The cornering lamp on one side of the vehicle shall be a structure that switches ON
automatically when the direction indicator lamps on the same side of the vehicle are switched
ON and/or when the steering angle is changed towards the same side of the vehicle.
3) The cornering lamp shall be switched OFF automatically when the direction indicator lamp
is switched OFF /or the steering angle has returned in the straight-ahead position.
4) When the reversing lamp is switched ON, both cornering lamps may be switched on
simultaneously, independently from the steering wheel or direction indicator lamp position.
In this case, the cornering lamps shall be switched OFF if the vehicle speed exceeds 10 km/h
forward or when the reversing lamp is switched OFF.
D. Other requirements
The cornering lamps shall not be activated at vehicle speed exceeds 40 km/h.

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Reversing Lamp
(Article 39 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirements of reversing lamp
A. Installation requirements1) In height
The apparent surface shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the
ground in unloaded state.2) In length
If the reversing lamps are installed additionally according to Article 39 Subparagraph 1, it
shall be fitted on the lateral or rear side of the vehicle.
B. Observation angle
1) The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 15 degrees
upwards and 5 degrees downwards and 45 degrees outwards and inwards. However, it shall
be ensured in any angle of not more than 30 degrees inwards if the additional lamps are fitted.
2) If the additional reversing lamps are fitted on the side of vehicle, the reference axis of
reversing lamp is directed outwards with an angle not exceeding 15 degrees relative to the
median longitudinal plane of the vehicle. Their aim may be directed downwards.
C. Orientation
1) The illuminating direction shall be rearwards of the vehicle.
2) If the reversing lamp is fitted on the lateral side of vehicles, it shall meet Item B' 2)
D. Operation requirements
1) The lamp can light up only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the
starting and stopping of the engine is in such a position that operation of the engine is possible.
2) The additional lamps shall not be switched on, if the position lamps, reversing lamps, end-
liner marker lamps, sider marker lamps and license plate lamps are not switched on.
3) The reversing lamps fitted on the lateral side of the vehicle may be switched on in forward
motion of the vehicle up to a maximum speed of 10 km/h, if the following conditions are
fulfilled:
A) the devices shall be structured so that it may be activated and deactivated manually by a
separate switch
B) if so activated, it shall be structured so that they may remain illuminated after reverse gear
is disengaged
C) It shall be structured so that they shall be automatically switched off if the forward speed
of the vehicle exceeds 10 km/h, regardless of the position of the separate switch; in this
case they shall remain switched off until deliberately being switched on again.
F. Tell tale
The tell-tale to indicate the operation statue of lamp may be installed

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Position Lamp
(Article 40 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirements of position lamp
A. Installation requirements1) In width
A) The outermost point on the apparent surface shall be not more than 400 mm from the
extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
B) In the case of a trailer, the outermost point on the apparent surface shall not be more than
150 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
C) Except passenger cars, and trucks and special purpose vehicle with GVW not exceeding
3.5 tons, the distance between the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference
axes shall not be less than 600 mm. This distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the
overall width of the vehicle is not more than 1,300 mm.
2) In height
The apparent surface shall be not less than 250mm nor more than 1500mm above the ground
in unloaded state (2100mm or less if the trailer or the shape of bodywork makes it impossible
to keep within 1500mm.)B. Observation angle1) Horizontal angle
A) The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 45 degrees
inwards and 80 degrees outwards.
B) If reference axis of the lamps for vehicles except for the trailers where the lower edge of
the apparent surface of the lamps is below 750 mm above the ground, the value of 45
degrees inward may be reduced to 20 degrees or less under the horizontal plane containing
the reference axis of this lamp.
C) In the case of trailers, the angle inwards may be reduced to 5 degrees or less.
2) Vertical angle
A) The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 15 degrees
upwards and downwards.
B) The vertical angle below the horizontal may be reduced to 5 degrees or less in the case of
reference axis of the position lamps below 750 mm above the ground.
3) For passenger cars, and trucks and special purpose vehicles with GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons,
in the case where a side-marker lamp is installed on the front, the following standards may be
applied to the divergence angle of the position lamp despite the provisions of Subparagraph 1
Item B 1) and 2).
A) The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 45 degrees
of horizontal angle inwards and outwards. Where the lower edge of the apparent surface of
reference axis of the lamps is below 750 mm above the ground, the value of 45 degrees
inward may be reduced to 20 degrees or less under the horizontal plane containing the
reference axis of this lamp.
B) The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 15 degrees
of vertical angle above and below the horizontal. The vertical angle below the horizontal
may be reduced to 5 degrees or less if the reference axis of the lamps is below 750 mm
above the ground.
C) The position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
12.5 square centimeters, except the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does
not transmit light.C. The illuminating direction of lamp shall be forwards.D. Operation requirements
1) The position shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously as the rear position lamp, end-
liner marker lamps, sider marker lamps and license plate lamps.
2) If a position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction indicator lamp, it may be such
that it is switched off during the activation of the direction indicator lamp.
E. Tell tale
A non-flashing tell-tale or instrument panel lighting to indicate the operation state of the lamp
shall be installed. However, it shall not be required if conforming to Subparagraph 1 Item D' 5)
B) of Table 6-4.F. Other requirements
1) If one or more infrared radiation generators are installed inside the position lamp, it is allowed
to be activated only when the headlamp on the same side of the vehicle is switched on and the
vehicle is in forward motion.
2) In the event that the position lamp or the headlamp on the same side fails, the infrared radiation
generator shall be automatically switched off.
3) In case an AFS providing a bending mode is installed, the position lamp may be swiveled
together with a lighting unit to which it is reciprocally incorporated.

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of End-Outline Marker Lamp
(Article 40-2 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirements for end-outline marker lamp
A. Installation position1) In width
A) The lamp shall be installed to the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
B) The outermost point of apparent surface shall be not more than 400 mm from the extreme
outer edge of the vehicle.2) In height
A) An end-outline marker lamp with the apparent surface facing forward (a white end-outline
marker lamp)
(1) The upper edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the device
shall not be lower than the upper edge of the transparent zone of the wind-screen.
(2) For trailers, at the maximum height compatible with the requirements relating to the
design and operational requirements of the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle and
to the symmetry of the lamps.
B) An end-outline marker lamp with the apparent surface facing rearward (a red end-outline
marker lamp)
They shall be installed at the maximum height in consideration of the body and operational
requirements so that they become symmetric based on the median longitudinal plane of the
vehicle.
At the maximum height compatible with the requirements relating to the design and
operational requirements of the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle and to the
symmetry of the lamps.
C) Both additional and mandatory lamps to be fitted as far separated in height as practicable
and compatible with design/operational requirements of the vehicle and symmetry of the
lamps.3) Length
In the case where an additional end-outline marker lamp with the apparent surface facing
forward is installed, it shall be installed as close to the rear and its distance between the
additional lamps and the rear of the vehicle shall not exceed 400 mm.
B. Observation angle
1) The visibility shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 80 degrees outwards.
2) The visibility shall be ensured within in any angle of not more than 5 degrees upwards and
20 degrees downwards.
C. The illuminating direction shall be such that the lamps meet the requirements for visibility
forwards and rearwards.D. Operation requirements
It shall be switched on and off simultaneously as the rear position lamp, position lamp, side-
marker lamp and license plate lamp.E. Tell-tale
The tell-tale to indicate the operation state of the lamp may be installed, and its function shall be
carried out by the tell-tale required for the position lamp and rear position lamp.
F. Other requirements
1) White and red end-outline marker lamps shall be installed separately, but if installed together,

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)[Table 6-13]

Requirements for Installation and Brightness of License Plate Lamp
(Article 41 Subparagraph 2)

1. Installation requirements of license plate lamp
A. Installation requirements
Such that the device illuminates the site of the registration plate
B. Operation requirements
It shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously as the rear position lamp, position lamp, side
marker lamp and end-outline marker lamp.
C. Tell-tale
The tell-tale to indicate the operation status of the lamp may be installed. However, its function
shall be carried out by the tell-tale required for the position lamp and rear position lamp.
D. Other requirements
When the rear license plate lamp is combined with the rear position lamp, reciprocally
incorporated in the stop lamp or in the rear fog lamp, the photometric characteristics of the
license plate lamp may be modified during the illumination of the stop lamp or the rear fog lamp.

2. Brightness requirements of license plate lamp
A. Brightness Test Points on License Plate
1) For license plate of 335×155mm or 335×170mm

2) For license plate of 440×200mm or 440×220mm

3) For license plate of 520×110mm

B. Brightness requirements
1) At each of the points of measurement the brightness shall be at least equal to 2.5 cd/m2.
However, for a vehicle on production, it may be applied not more than ±20 percent.
2) The brightness difference measured at any two points which is divided by the distance(cm)
between two points shall not exceed two times of minimum brightness measured. However,

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Rear Position Lamp
(Article 42 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirements of rear position lamp
A. Installation requirements1) In width
A) The outermost point on the apparent surface shall be not more than 400 mm from the
extreme outer edge of the vehicle. This condition shall not apply to the additional rear
position lamps.
B) Except passenger cars, and trucks and special purpose vehicle with GVW not exceeding
3.5 tons, the distance between the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference
axes shall not be less than 600 mm. This distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the
overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
2) In height
A) The apparent surface shall be not less than 350mm nor more than 1500mm above the
ground in unloaded state, however, not more than 2100mm for any other vehicles the shape
of bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1500mm.
B) If the additional lamps are installed, they shall be placed symmetrically as conforming to
Item 'a and but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
B. Observation angle1) Horizontal angle
The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 45 degrees
inwards and 80 degrees outwards. However, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm, the
inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° or less under the Horizontal plane.
2) Vertical angle
A) The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured not more than 15 degrees upwards and
downwards.
B) The vertical angle below the horizontal may be reduced to not more than 5 degrees in the
case of the reference axis of the lamps below 750 mm above the ground.
C) The vertical angle above the horizontal may be reduced to not more than 5 degrees in the
case of the reference axis of the additional lamps exceeding 2,100 mm above the ground
3) In the case where a side-marker lamp is installed at the rear of the passenger cars, and trucks
and special purpose vehicles with GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons, the following standards may
be applied to the divergence angle of the rear position lamp, notwithstanding Subparagraph 1
Item B 1) and 2).
A) The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 45 degrees
of horizontal angle inwards and outwards. However, where a lamp is mounted below 750
mm, the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° or less under the Horizontal plane.
B) The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured not more than 15 degrees of vertical
angle above and below the horizontal. The vertical angle below the horizontal may be
reduced to not more than 5 degrees in the case of the reference axis of the lamps below 750
mm above the ground.
C) The rear position lamp shall provide the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimeters,
except the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
C. The illuminating direction of lamp shall be rearwards.
D. Operation requirements

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Stop Lamp
(Article 43 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirements of stop lamp
A. Installation requirements1) In width
a) The outermost point on the apparent surface of stop lamp shall be not more than 400 mm
from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle for passenger cars, and trucks and special
purpose vehicle with GVM not exceeding 3.5 tons.
b) In the case of other vehicles except passenger cars, and trucks and special purpose vehicle
with GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons, the distance between the two apparent surfaces in the
direction of the reference axes shall not be less than 600 mm. However, this distance may
be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
2) In height
a) The apparent surface shall be not less than 350mm nor more than 1,500mm above the
ground in unloaded state, not more than 2100mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it
impossible to keep within 1,500mm.
b) If the additional lamps are installed, they shall be positioned at a height compatible with
the requirements of 'a) and the symmetry of the lamps, and at a vertical distance not less
than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.3) In lengthIt shall be installed at the rear of the vehicle.B. Observation angle1) Horizontal angle
A) The apparent surface of the stop lamp should be visible from 45 degrees or less to the left
and 45 degrees or less to the right. However, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm, the
inward angle may be reduced to 20° or less under the Horizontal plane.
2) Vertical angle
A) The visibility of apparent surface of stop lamp shall be ensured not more than 15 degrees
upwards and downwards. However, the vertical angle below the horizontal may be reduced
to not more than 5 degrees in the case of lamps below 750 mm above the ground.
B) The vertical angle above the horizontal may be reduced to not more than 5 degrees in the
case of additional lamps exceeding 2,100 mm above the ground.
C. The illuminating direction of lamp shall be towards the rear of the vehicle.
D. Operation requirements
1) The stop lamps shall be operated in accordance with Article 15, Paragraph 9 and Paragraph
10.
2) The stop lamps need not function if the engine is not operated.
E. Tell tale
Tell-tale to indicate the operation state of the lamp may be installed. Where fitted, this tell-tale
shall be an operating tell-tale consisting of a non-flashing warning light which comes on in the
event of the malfunctioning of the stop lamps.
F. Other requirements
The control of variable luminous intensity may be applied to stop lamps, depending on variant
environmental condition and the contamination of light emitting surface

Installation and Luminous Intensity Requirements of Auxiliary Stop Lamp
(Article 43 Paragraph 2 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirements of auxiliary stop lamp
A. Installation requirements1) In width
A) The center of reference for auxiliary stop lamp shall be situated on the median longitudinal
plane of the vehicle. However, in the case where the two auxiliary stop lamps are installed
it shall be positioned as close as possible to the median longitudinal plane.
However, if difficult to install it in the center, two auxiliary stop lamps meeting the
luminous intensity of D-lamp shall be installed symmetrically or one auxiliary stop lamp
shall be installed as close as possible to the left or right side of median longitudinal plane.
B) The offset from the median longitudinal plane to the center of reference of the auxiliary
stop lamp shall not exceed 150 mm.2) In height
A) The horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface shall either not
be more than 150 mm below the lowest edge of the exposed surface of the glass of the rear
window or not be less than 850 mm above the ground.
B) The horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface shall be above
the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the apparent surface.
3) In lengthIt shall be installed at the rear of the vehicle.B. Observation angle1) Horizontal angle
The visibility of apparent surface of auxiliary stop lamp shall be ensured in any angle of not
more than 10 degrees to the left and to the right
2) Vertical angle
The visibility of apparent surface of auxiliary stop lamp shall be ensured in any angle of not
more than 10 degrees upwards and 5 degrees downwards.
C. The illuminating direction of lamp shall be towards the rear of the vehicle.
D. Other requirements
1) The auxiliary stop lamp may not be reciprocally incorporated with any other lamp.
2) The auxiliary stop lamp may be installed outside or inside the vehicle. And the auxiliary stop
lamp, if installed inside of the vehicle, shall not distract the direct vision of the driver.

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Direction Indicator Lamp
(Article 44 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirementsA. Arrangements
1) Two front direction indicator lamps shall be installed on a vehicle. However, when an adaptive
front lighting system (AFS) is installed, the distance between apparent surfaces shall be
determined by the lighting unit closest to the front direction indicator lamp among the lighting
units turned on during the operation of the passing beam headlamp.
A) Category-1, 1a, 1b
If the distance between the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference
axis of the front direction indicator lamp and that of the apparent surface of the passing
beam headlamp or the front fog lamp is at least 40 mm;
B) Category-1a, 1b
If the distance between the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference
axis of the front direction indicator lamp and that of the apparent surface of the passing
beam headlamp or the front fog lamp, if there is one, is greater than 20 mm and less than
40 mm;C) Category-1b
If the distance between the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference
axis of the front direction indicator lamp and that of the apparent surface of the passing
beam headlamp or the front fog lamp, if there is one, is less than or equal to 20 mm;
2) Two rear direction indicator lamps (category -2a or 2b) shall be installed in the vehicle.
However, one rear direction indicator lamp may be additionally installed on each side of the
rear, respectively on passenger cars, and trucks and special purpose vehicles with GVW
exceeding 3.5 tons.
3) Two auxiliary direction indicator lamps (categories -5, 6) shall be installed on a vehicle.
A) Category-5 auxiliary direction indicator lamps on passenger cars, and trucks and special
purpose vehicles with GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons and buses not exceeding 6 meters in
B) Category-6 auxiliary direction indicator lamps on trucks and special purpose vehicles with
