C) Buses exceeding 9 meters in lengthB. Installation position1) In width
A) The outer edge of the apparent surface shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme
outer edge of the vehicle. This condition shall not apply to the additional rear lamps.
B) The distance between the two apparent surfaces inside shall not be less than 600 mm. This
distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is not more than
1,300 mm.2) In height
A) The height of the light-emitting surface of the auxiliary direction indicator lamps
(categories-5, 6) shall not be less than 350 mm or not more than 1,500 mm from the ground
in unloaded state for passenger cars and trucks and special purpose vehicles with GVW not
exceeding 3.5 tons, and not less than 500 mm or not more than 1,500 mm for other vehicles.
B) The height of the apparent surfaces of the front and rear direction indicator lamps of
categories-1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b shall not be less than 350 mm or not more than 1,500 mm in
unloaded sate.
C) If the structure of the vehicle does not permit these upper limits, they may be increased to
2,300 mm for the auxiliary direction indicator lamps, and to 2,100 mm or less for the front
and rear direction indicator lamps of categories-1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b except the additional
direction indicator lamps.
D) If additional lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a height compatible with the
applicable requirements of 1), A) and B), the symmetry of the lamps, and at a vertical
distance not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
3) In length
The distance between the light-emitting surface of the auxiliary direction indicator lamp and
the front side of the vehicle shall not exceed 1,800 mm. However, this distance shall not
exceed 2,500 mm for passenger cars, and trucks and special purpose vehicles with GVW not
exceeding 3.5 tons; and all other categories of vehicles if the shape of bodywork makes it
impossible to comply with the minimum observation angles.

(1) Where a lamp is mounted below 750mm, the downward angle may be reduced to 5°;
(2) Where an optional rear lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm the upward angle may be
reduced to 5°.
B) The visibility of apparent surface of direction indicator lamp (Category-6) shall be ensured
from within 30 degrees above and 5 degrees or less below the horizontal.
C) For the direction indicator lamps (of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b) of passenger cars,
trucks and special purpose vehicles with GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons, mounted below 750
mm, the inward angle may be reduced to 20° or less under the Horizontal plane.
3) If side-marker lamps are installed for passenger cars, trucks and special purpose vehicles with
GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons, the front and rear direction indicator lamps shall be installed as
the figure below:

A) If the reference axis of the direction indicator lamps (Categories-1, 1a or 1b) mounted
below 750 mm above the ground, the inward angle may be reduced to 20° or less under the
Horizontal plane.
B) The visibility of apparent surface of direction indicator lamps shall be ensured in any angle
of not more than 15 degrees above and below the horizontal. However, if the reference axis
of an additional direction indicator lamp mounted below 750 mm, the inward angle may be
reduced to 20° or less under the Horizontal plane.
C) The apparent surface shall be at least 12.5 square centimeters, except for auxiliary direction
indicator lamps (Categories 5 and 6). The illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector

D ≤ 2.5m


<!-- Page 206 -->

© KAIDA
206
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)D. Operation requirements
1) The direction indicator lamps shall switch on independently of the other lamps.
2) If the direction indicator lamps (including front and rear direction indicator lamp, auxiliary
direction indicator lamp) are controlled to signal left or right, the direction indicator lamps in
that direction shall operate simultaneously, and the apparent surface of applicable direction
indicator lamps shall flash or switch on in phase.
3) On passenger cars less than 6m in length, and trucks or special purpose vehicles with GVW
not exceeding 3.5 tons less than 6 m in length, with an arrangement complying with Item C,
3) above, the amber side-marker lamps shall also flash at the same frequency (in phase) with
the direction indicator lamps.
4) For a turn signal lamp with a structure that can both flash and be turned on sequentially, the
two structures shall not be activated together.
5) Two turn signal lamps, which are additionally installed on trucks and special purpose vehicles
exceeding 3.5 tons of GVW as well as buses (Category -2a or 2b), shall operate with a
structure that can be turned on sequentially with or flash simultaneously with the rear direction
indicator lamps, which will be installed on both rear sides of the motor vehicle.
E. Tell-tale
1) The tell-tale shall be installed for the direction indicator lamps (Categories-1, 1a, 1b, 2a and
2b). It may be visual or auditory or both.
2) In the event of the malfunction of any of front and rear direction indicator lamps, any one of
the followings shall be met.
A) The visual tell-tale shall be either extinguished, or remain alight without flashing, or shows
a marked change of frequency.
B) In case of auditory warning, it shall be provided with a marked change of frequency at the
same time.
3) If auditory warning is provided for malfunction of direction indicator lamps, the function of
a marked change of frequency shall be provided at the same time.
4) If a motor vehicle is equipped to draw a trailer, it shall be fitted with a special visual
operational tell-tale for the direction indicator lamps on the trailer unless the tell-tale of the
drawing vehicle allows the failure of any one of the direction indicator lamps on the vehicle
combination thus formed to be detected.F. Other requirements
1) The light shall be a flashing light flashing 90 ± 30 times per minute.
2) Operation of the light-signal control shall be followed within one second by the emission of
light and within one and one-half seconds by its first extinction.
3) If a motor vehicle is equipped to draw a trailer, the control of the direction indicator lamps on
the drawing vehicle shall operate the direction indicator lamps of the trailer simultaneously.
4) In the event of failure, other than short-circuit, of one direction indicator lamp, the others shall
continue to flash. In this case, the flash frequency may be changed.
G. Others
The control of variable luminous intensity shall be applied to the rear direction indicator lamps.

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Side Marker Lamp
(Article 44-2 Subparagraph 2)

1. Installation requirements for side marker lamp
A. Installation
1) The SM1 type of side-marker lamp may be installed on all categories of vehicles however,
the SM2 type of side-marker lamps shall be installed on the passenger cars.
2) A side-marker lamp shall be installed in the case where Subparagraph 1 Item B 3) of Table
6-11 and Subparagraph 1 Item B 3) of Table 6-14 are applied to a motor vehicle of 6 meters
or less in length that falls under any of the following:
A) Passenger car
B) Trucks and special purpose vehicles with a GVW of 3.5 tons or less
B. Installation position1) In height
The apparent surface shall be not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground
in unloaded state (not more than 2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible
to keep within 1,500 mm).2) In length
a) At least one side-marker lamp shall be fitted to the middle third of the vehicle and shall not
be fitted further than 3,000 mm from the front.
b) The distance between two adjacent side-marker lamps shall not exceed 3,000 mm. If the
structure the vehicle makes it impossible to comply with such a requirement, this distance
may be increased to not more than 4,000 mm.
c) The distance between the rearmost side-marker lamp and the rear of the vehicle shall not
exceed 1,000 mm.
d) The criteria for longitudinal direction under the categories of each motor vehicle shall be
(1) Motor vehicle with a length of 6 meters or less: A lamp may be installed by trisecting it
in the longitudinal direction of the car (x-axis) and selecting a part from the front part,
the rear part, or the front part and the rear part.
(2) Passenger car exceeding 6 meters but not more than 7 meters in length: One side marker
lamp shall be installed 3,000 millimeters or less from the foremost part of the vehicle,
and another side marker lamp may be installed on the rear of the vehicle by trisecting it
in the longitudinal direction (x-axis) of the vehicle.
C. Observation angle1) Horizontal angle
a) The visibility of the apparent surface of the side marker lamp that is installed on a motor
vehicle exceeding 6 meters in length shall be ensured not more than 45 degrees to the front
and to the rear; however, for vehicles with a length of 6 meters or less, this value can be
reduced to 30 degrees or less.
b) If the vehicle is equipped with side-marker lamps used to conform to Subparagraph 1 Item
'B of Table 6-11, Subparagraph 1 Item B of Table 6-14 and Subparagraph 1 Item 'C of Table
6-17, the visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured not more than 45 degrees towards
the front and the rear and not more than 30º towards the direction of vehicle center.
2) Vertical angle
The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 10 degrees

E. Operation requirements
1) On passenger cars 6m or less in length, and trucks or special purpose vehicles with GVW not

2) The amber side-marker lamp, installed on trucks, special purpose vehicles and trailers

(Category -5) has been additionally installed pursuant to Subparagraph 1 Item A of Table 6-
17.F. Tell-tale
A tell-tale to indicate the operation state of the lamp may be installed. However, its function shall
be carried out by the tell-tale required for the position lamp and rear position lamp.
G. Other requirements
1) When the side-marker lamp is combined with the rear position lamp or reciprocally
incorporated with the rear fog-lamp or stop lamp, the photometric characteristics of the side-
marker lamp may be modified while the rear fog lamp or stop lamp is in operation.
2) Color of the corresponding rear side-marker lamps shall be amber if they flash with the rear
direction indicator lamp.

Installation Requirements of Hazard Warning Lamp (Article 45 Subparagraph 2)

1. Operation requirements
A. The hazard warning lamp shall be operated by means of a separate manual control enabling all
the turn signal lamps to operate in phase.
B. The hazard warning lamp may be activated automatically in the event of a vehicle being
involved in a collision or even after the de-activation of the emergency stop signal. In such cases,
it may be turned "on" or "off" manually.
C. On passenger cars less than 6m in length, and trucks or special purpose vehicles with GVW not
exceeding 3.5 tons less than 6 m in length, the amber side-marker lamps, when mounted, shall
also flash at the same frequency (in phase) with the turn signal lamps of the same side.

2. Tell tale
The flashing tell-tale to indicate the operation state of the lamp shall be installed and it can operate
in conjunction with the tell-tale(s) specified in Subparagraph 1. Item 'E of Table 6-17.

3. Other requirements
A. If a power-driven vehicle is equipped to draw a trailer, the hazard warning lamp control shall
be capable of bringing the turn signal lamps on the trailer into action simultaneously.
B. The hazard warning lamp shall be able to function even if the engine is operated or stopped.


<!-- Page 213 -->

213
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)[Table 6-20]

Installation Requirements for Rear-End Collision Alert Signal
(Article 45-2 Subparagraph 2)

1. Installation requirements
A. All the lamps of the rear-end collision alert signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 +/-
1.0 Hz. However, if any of the lamps of the rear end collision alert signal to the rear of the vehicle
use filament light sources the frequency shall be 4.0 +0.0/-1.0 Hz.
B. The rear-end collision alert signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
C. The rear-end collision alert signal shall be activated and deactivated automatically.
D. The rear-end collision alert signal shall not be activated if the direction indicator lamps, the
hazard warning signal or the emergency stop signal is activated.
E. Activation of rear-end collision alert signal
Activation (sec)Vr > 30km/hTime to collision  1.4Vr  30 km/hTime to collision  1.4 / 30 ×VrRemark)
"Vr (Relative Speed)": means the difference in speed between a vehicle with rear-end collision
alert signal and a following vehicle in the same lane.

F. The activation period of the rear-end collision alert signal shall be not more than 3 seconds.

2. Tell-tale
A tell-tale to indicate the operation state of the lamp may be installed.


|  | Activation (sec |  |

| Vr > 30km/h | Time to collision | 1.4 |
| Vr 30 km/h | Time to collision 1.4 | / 30 ×Vr |

Installation Requirements of Rear Retro-Reflector Etc.
(Article 49 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation
A. In the case that reflectors are reciprocally incorporated with the lighting device situated at the
rear, the additional installation may be allowed.
B. The retro-reflectors shall conform to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB.
C. Additional retro-reflectors are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the
other lighting and light-signaling devices.

2. Installation positionA. In width
1) The outermost point on the reflected surface shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme
outer edge of the vehicle.
2) The distance between the two reflected surfaces in the direction of the reference axis shall be
not less than 600 mm except passenger cars, and trucks and special purpose vehicles with
GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons. This distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall
width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
B. In height
The reflected surface shall be not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm above the ground in
unloaded state. (not more than 1,200mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), 1,500mm or less if
the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900mm or 1200mm respectively)
C. In lengthIt shall be installed at the rear of the vehicle.

3. Observation angleA. Horizontal angle
The visibility of reflected surface of shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 30 degrees
inwards and outwards.B. Vertical angle
The visibility of reflected surface of retro-reflector shall be ensured not more than 10 degrees
above and below horizontal. The vertical angle below the horizontal may be reduced to 5 degrees
or less in the case of the reference axis of a retro-reflector below 750 mm above the ground.

4. Other requirements
The illuminating surface of the retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface
of any other additional lamps situated at the rear.


<!-- Page 224 -->

© KAIDA

KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)[Table 6-24]

Installation Requirements of Triangle Retro-Reflector for Trailers
(Article 49 Paragraph 2 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation
A. The retro-reflectors shall conform to the requirements concerning Class IIIA or IIIB.
B. Additional retro-reflectors are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the
other lighting systems.C. The apex of the triangle shall be directed upwards.

2. Installation positionA. In width
1) The outermost point on the reflected surface shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme
outer edge of the vehicle.
2) The distance between the two reflected surfaces in the direction of the reference axes shall be
not less than 600 mm. This distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of
the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.B. In height
The reflected surface of the trailer shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm
above the ground in unloaded state. (not more than 1,200mm if grouped with any other lamp(s),
1,500mm or less if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900mm or
1200mm respectively)C. In lengthIt shall be installed at the rear of the vehicle.

3. Observation angleA. Horizontal angle
The visibility of reflected surface of shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 30 degrees
inwards and outwards.B. Vertical angle
The visibility of reflected surface of the retro-reflector shall be ensured in any angle of not more
than 15 degrees above and below horizontal. The vertical angle below the horizontal may be
reduced to 5 degrees or less in the case of the reference axis of a retro-reflector for trailers below
750 mm above the ground.

4. Other requirements
The reflected surface of the retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of
any other lamp situated at the rear.

Installation Requirements of Front Retro-Reflector
(Article 49 Paragraph 3 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation
A. The retro-reflectors shall conform to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB.
B. Additional retro-reflectors are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the
other lighting and light-signaling devices.

2. Installation positionA. In width
1) The outermost point on the reflected surface shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme
outer edge of the vehicle.
2) The distance between the two reflected surfaces in the direction of the reference axes shall be
not more than 150mm.
3) The distance between the two reflected surfaces in the direction of the reference axis shall be
not less than 600 mm except passenger cars, and trucks and special purpose vehicles with
GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons. This distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall
width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
B. In height
The reflected surface shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm above the ground
in unloaded state. (not more than 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to
keep within 900 mm)C. In lengthIt shall be installed at the front of the vehicle.

3. Observation angleA. Horizontal angle
1) The visibility of reflected surface of front retro-reflector shall be ensured in any angle of not
more than 30 degrees inwards and outwards. In the case of trailers, the angle inwards may be
reduced to 10°.
2) The visibility shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 10 degrees inwards when the
trailer is connected, if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible, the additional
(supplementary) retro-reflectors shall be fitted to meet the observation angle.
B. Vertical angle
The visibility of reflected surface of front retro-reflector shall be ensured in any angle of not
more than 10 degrees above and below horizontal. The vertical angle below the horizontal may
be reduced to 5 degrees in the case of the reference axis of a side retro-reflector below 750 mm
above the ground.

4. Other requirements
The reflected surface of the retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of
any other lamp situated at the front.


<!-- Page 226 -->

© KAIDA
226
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)[Table 6-26]

Installation Requirements of Side Retro-Reflector
(Article 49 Paragraph 4 Subparagraph 2)

1. Installation
A. The retro-reflectors shall conform to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB.
B. Additional retro-reflectors are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the
other lighting and light-signaling devices.

2. Installation positionA. In height
The reflected surface shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm above the ground
in unloaded state. (not more than 1,200mm if grouped with any lamp(s), 1,500mm or less if the
shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900mm or 1200mm respectively)
B. In length
1) At least one side retro reflector shall be fitted to the middle third of the vehicle and shall not
be fitted 3,000 mm or less from the front.
2) The distance between two adjacent side retro reflectors shall not exceed 3,000 mm. This does
not, however, apply to passenger cars and trucks and special purpose vehicles with GVW not
exceeding 3.5 tons.
3) If the structure, design or the operational use of the vehicle makes it impossible to comply
with such a requirement, this distance may be increased to 4,000 mm or less.
4) The distance between the rearmost side retro-reflector and the rear of the vehicle shall not
exceed 1,000 mm. However, for motor vehicles the length of which does not exceed 6,000
mm, it is sufficient to have one side retro-reflector fitted within the first third and one within
the last third of the vehicle length.

3. Observation angleA. Horizontal angle
The visibility of reflected surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 45 degrees to
the front and to the rear.B. Vertical angle
The visibility of reflected surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 10 degrees
above and below the horizontal. The vertical angle below the horizontal may be reduced to 5
degrees or less in the case of the reference axis of a retro-reflector below 750 mm above the
ground.

4. Other requirements
The reflected surface of the retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface
of any other lamp situated at the side.

Installation and Reflection Requirements of Rear Reflecting Plate (Paper)
(Article 49 Paragraph 6 and Article 112-9 Subparagraph 1)

1. InstallationA. Install 1, 2, or 4 on the rear side
B. Reflection of the rear reflecting plate or paper shall have the meeting the following requirements.
1) Reflection: Amber or red2) Fluorescent: RedC. Arrangement
1) The lower end of each rear reflecting plate should be installed horizontally with the ground.
2) The rear reflecting plate shall be installed at an angle of not more than 5 ° to the median
longitudinal plane of the vertical plane of the vehicle and face rearward.
3) The rear reflecting plate shall be installed symmetrically with respect to the median
longitudinal plane of the vehicle.D. Observation angle1) Horizontal angle: 30° or less inwards and outwards.2) Vertical angle: 15° or less above and below horizontal.
E. The center point of the rear reflecting plate or rear reflect paper shall be not less than 250 mm
and not more than 2,100 mm above the ground in the unloaded state.

Exterior Courtesy Lamp Installation (Article 38-3)

1. Installation
A. Two, however further exterior courtesy lamps to illuminate steps and/or door handles are
permitted. If the vehicle has an entrance in either left or right side, the exterior courtesy lamps
may be installed only on the side with the entrance.
B. Lamp color shall be white
C. The exterior courtesy lamp shall not be activated unless the vehicle is stationary and one or more
of the following conditions is satisfied:
1) The engine is stopped; or2) A driver or passenger door is opened; or3) A load compartment door is opened.
D. Approved lamps emitting white light with the exception of main beam head lamps, day time
running lamps and reversing lamps may be selectively activated as courtesy lamp function.

2. Observation
Perform a visual test to verify that there is no direct visibility of the apparent surface of these lamps,
if viewed by an observer moving on the boundary of a zone on a transverse plane 10 m from the
front of the vehicle, a transverse plane 10 m from the rear of the vehicle, and two longitudinal
planes 10 m from each side of the vehicle; these four planes to extend from 1 m to 3 m above and
parallel to the ground


Boundaries of the zones


<!-- Page 232 -->

© KAIDA
232
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)[Table 6-31]

Maneuvering Lamp Installation and Luminous Intensity (Article 39-2)

1. InstallationA. One or two (one per side)B. Lamp color shall be whiteC. OrientationDownwardsD. Operation requirements
1) Maneuvering lamps shall be so connected that they cannot be activated unless the main-beam
headlamps or the dipped-beam headlamps are switched ON at the same time.
2) The maneuvering lamp(s) shall be activated automatically for slow maneuver up to 10 km/h
provided that one of the following conditions is fulfilled:
(A) Prior to the vehicle being set in motion for the first time after each manual activation of
the propulsion system; or(B) Reverse gear is engaged; or
(C) A camera- or sensor-based system which assists parking maneuver is activated
3) The maneuvering lamps shall be automatically switched off if the forward speed of the vehicle
exceeds 10 km/h and they shall remain switched off until the conditions for activation are met
again.E. Other requirements
Perform a visual test to verify that there is no direct visibility of the apparent surface of these
lamps, if viewed by an observer moving on the boundary of a zone on a transverse plane 10 m
from the front of the vehicle, a transverse plane 10 m from the rear of the vehicle, and two
longitudinal planes 10 m from each side of the vehicle; these four planes to extend from 1 m to
3 m above and parallel to the ground


2. Luminous intensity of maneuvering lamp
A. Emax: 500 Cd or less
B. Emin: Shall not exceed 0.5 Cd within the fields of the vertical minimum and maximum angles.

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)[Table 6-32]

Installation Requirements of Parking Lamp (Article 40-3)

1. Installation
A. Either two lamps at the front and two lamps at the rear, or one lamp on each side.
B. White in front, red at the rear, amber if reciprocally incorporated in the side direction-indicator
lamps or in the side-marker lamps.C. Position1) In width
That point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from
the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer
edge of the vehicle.2) In height
For all other categories of vehicles (except passenger cars, and trucks and special purpose
vehicles with GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons): above the ground, not less than 350 mm nor more
than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within
1,500 mm).D. Observation angle
1) The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 45° outwards
2) The visibility of apparent surface shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 15° above
and below the horizontal. However, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm, the downward
angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
E. Such that the lamps meet the requirements for visibility forwards and rearwards.
F. Operation requirements
1) The connection shall allow the parking lamp(s) on the same side of the vehicle to be lit
independently of any other lamps.
2) The parking lamp(s) and, if applicable, the front and rear position lamps, shall be able to
operate even if the device which starts the engine is in a position which makes it impossible
for the engine to operate.
3) A device which automatically deactivates these lamps as a function of time is prohibited.
G. Tell-tale
Circuit-closed tell-tale optional. If there is one, it shall not be possible to confuse it with the tell-
tale for the front and rear position lamps.
H. Other requirements
The functioning of this lamp may also be performed by simultaneously switching on the front
and rear position lamps on the same side of the vehicle. In this case, they shall meet the luminous
intensity requirements of parking lamps.

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)[Table 6-33]

Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System (AVAS) for Quiet Road Transport Vehicles (QRTV)
(Article 53-3)

1. The AVAS shall operate in the speed range of at least 20 km/h or less from the start.

2. The warning sound pursuant to Subparagraph 1 shall meet the requirements specified in each of
the following Items.
A. The overall sound shall be not less than the overall minimum sound level requirements specified
in Subparagraph 8
B. The alarm has at least two of the one-third octave bands applicable to the minimum sound level
requirements specified in Subparagraph 8. At least one of these bands shall be within the 1,600
Hz or less one-third octave band.

3. The warning sound shall have frequency shift characteristics applicable to the each of the following
items to inform road users about the change in vehicle speed when driving in forward direction.
A. The warning sound emitted by the vehicle shall vary proportionally with speed within each
individual gear ratio by an average of at least 0.8 % per 1 km/h in the speed range from 5 km/h
to 20 km/h.
B. The warning sounds meeting the requirements of the Item A' shall be within the frequency range
in Subparagraph 8, at least one of them shall meet the requirements of the frequency shift
characteristics.

4. The overall sound level shall not exceed 75 dB(A) when driving in forward direction.

5. The function enabling the driver to deactivate the warning sound (warning sound off-switch) shall
not be installed.

6. AVAS equipped with various type of warning sounds, shall meet the requirements specified in
Subparagraph 1 through Subparagraph 5.

7. If the vehicle not equipped with AVAS exceeds the overall sound in Subparagraph 8 by 3 decibels
(A), Subparagraph 2 Item B' and Subparagraph 3 shall not apply.

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)[Table 7]

Brake Performance of the Passenger Cars (Article 90 Subparagraph 1)

1. Brake force distribution between axles (except for vehicles fitted with anti-lock service brake
system)
A. For all braking rates between 0.15 and 0.8, the adhesion utilization curve (meaning curves
showing, for specified load conditions, the adhesion utilized by each axle plotted against the
braking rate of the vehicle) of the front axle shall be situated above that for the rear axle in a full
load state and a light load state (a state with a driver and test equipment).
B. For K (theoretical coefficient of adhesion between tire and road) values between 0.2 and 0.8:
Z=>0.1+0.7(K-0.2)

K: theoretical coefficient of adhesion between tire and road
Z: braking rate of vehicle = J/g (deceleration of the vehicle/acceleration due to gravity)

2. When tested to the wheel-lock sequence test procedure (except for vehicles fitted with anti-lock
service brake system), and at vehicle braking rates between 0.15 and 0.8m/s2, both rear wheels
shall not reach a locked condition prior to both front wheels being locked. However, if the vehicle
meets one of the following criteria, then it passes this wheel lockup sequence requirement:
A. no wheels lock
B. both wheels on the front axle and one or no wheels on the rear axle lock
C. both axles simultaneously lock (the condition when the time interval between the lockup of the
last (second) wheel on the front axle is <0.1 seconds for vehicle speeds >30km/h)

3. Torque wheel test (except for vehicles fitted with anti-lock service brake system)
The requirement of Subparagraph 1.A. shall be met. However, the test may be omitted if the
requirement of Subparagraph 2 is met.

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)[Table 7-2]

Brake Performance of Bus, Truck (Except Trailer), and Special Purpose Vehicle
(Article 90 Subparagraph 2)

1. Structure requirement of brake system and brake force distribution
A. Structural requirement
(1) The variable brake device shall be operated automatically even in case of a manual variable
brake system , this requirement shall be met in the entire variable range
(2) The braking power of a towing vehicle for a semi-trailer continuously shall be variable from
the state without a trailer to the state with an unladen trailer
(3) In the case of a towing vehicle with GVW over 3.5 tons (in case of semi-trailer or central
axle trailer, it means the total of rear axle weights in loaded state) which tows a trailer, the air
pressure supplied from the towing vehicle to the brake system of a trailer shall comply with
the following requirements
(a) If the control device of the braking system is operated at maximum, the air pressure
supplied to the pneumatic control line and air supply line of the trailer shall be 6.5 - 8.5 bar.
(b) When the pressure of the energy storage device is "P5", the air pressure supplied to the air
supply line of the trailer shall be 7.0 bar or more before the control device of service braking
system of a trailer is operated. In this case, "P5" refers to the lower limit pressure (input
limit pressure) of the pressure governor of the energy storage device, and if no pressure
governor is provided, it refers to the pressure from the energy source (maximum pressure
× 0.9).
(c) Even if the variable brake device is in failure, the requirements of (a) and (b) shall be met.
B. Brake force distribution (3xcept the vehicle installed with anti-lock braking system)
(1) Two-axle vehicles
(a) If the coefficient of adhesion (K) is 0.20 or more and 0.80 or less, the adhesion utilization
curve of front and rear axles are situated below the line A in FIG. 1A through 1C
(b) The adhesion utilization curve of the front axle shall be situated above the adhesion
utilization curve of the rear axle, however, except the cases specified in 1) through 3) below.
1) For truck and special purpose vehicles with either GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons and its
loaded/unladen rear axle loading ratio not exceeding 1.5 or GVW less than 2 tons, if Z is
more than 0.15 and less than 0.3 (0.15-0.3) and more than 0.45 and not more than 0.8
(0.45-0.8), the adhesion utilization curves of front axle shall be situated above the
adhesion utilization curves of rear axle, and if Z is not less than 0.3 and not more than
0.45 (0.3-0.45), the adhesion utilization curves of rear axle shall be situated below B line
of Figure 1A.
2) Truck and special purpose vehicles with GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons, not applicable to
1), shall comply with the requirements specified in a) or b) below.
a) If Z is 0.15 or more and 0.50 or less (0.15-0.50), the adhesion utilization curves of
front axle shall be situated over the adhesion utilization curves of rear axle.
b) If Z is more than 0.15 and less than 0.30 (0.15-0.30), the adhesion utilization curves
of front axle shall be situated between the line of C-1 and C-2 in FIG 1C, and if Z is
more than 0.15 and less than 0.50 (0.15-0.50), the adhesion utilization curves of rear
axle shall be situated below line of C-1 of FIG 1C. If Z is not less than 0.50 and not
more than 0.61, the adhesion utilization curves of rear axle shall be situated below the
line of D of Figure 1C.
3) Bus and Truck and special purpose vehicles with GVW exceeding 3.5 tons shall meet

8. Warning signal requirements in the event of the leakage of brake fluid
Requirements
When the ignition switch is "ON", the warning signal meeting the following requirements shall be
operated.
. The warning signal shall be red so that the driver can easily check it.
. The warning signal shall be easily distinguishable from others. However, in this case, this
warning signal may be combined with the warning signal of other brake system.
Measuringconditions
Measure when the brake fluid drops below the lowest part of the partition of storage device or
decreases to one-fourth of the maximum normal level, or when the difference in pressures between
the normal system and the failing system reaches 15 bar at the outlet of the master cylinder.
Test vehicle state Loaded and lightly-loaded state

9. Braking performance of service brake system in the event of the failure of anti-lock service
braking systemRequirements
When the ignition switch is "ON", the warning signal meeting the following requirements shall be
operated.
. The warning signal shall be yellow so that the driver can easily check it.
. The warning signal shall be easily distinguishable from others. However, in this case, this warning
signal may be combined with the warning signal of other brake system.
Measuringconditions
Cut off the power supply cable of vehicle from the power cable of anti-lock brake service brake
system or from the input(output) cable to modulator which controls the braking force of anti-lock
brake service brake system and measure it.
Test vehicle state Loaded and lightly-loaded state

16. Requirements for structure and braking performance for spring brake
A. Structure requirements
(1) A spring braking system shall not be used as a service braking system.
(2) The feed circuit to the spring compression chamber shall either include an own energy
reserve or shall be fed from at least two independent energy reserves.
(3) During re-charging of the braking system from zero pressure, the spring brakes shall not be
released, until the pressure in the service braking system meets the requirements in "(4)
Insurance test of operation of service brake system" under Item b "Brake performance
requirements the loaded-state vehicle, using the service braking system control.
(4) Once applied, the spring brakes shall not release unless there is sufficient pressure in the
service braking system to at least provide the braking performance of the loaded vehicle by
application of the service braking control, as meeting "Requirements (2)" under
"Requirements applied per vehicle type" in Item b' Subparagraph 5 of this Table.
(5) It shall be so designed that it is possible to release the spring braking system even if a failure
occurs in the spring braking system.
(6) In the case that the energy required for the external device is supplied from the energy
storage device of the spring brake, if the failure occurs in the energy source and if the system
to the external device is open to the standby state, it shall be structured to be possible that the
control device of the spring brake could be released once or more.
Remark)1. Pressure unit: bar
2. Spring braking systems: are braking systems in which the energy required for braking is
supplied by one or more springs acting as an energy storage device (energy accumulator).
3. Spring compression chamber: means the chamber where the pressure variation that induces
the compression of the spring is actually produced.
4. External device: other energy storage devices than energy storage device for braking device.

B. Braking performance requirements(1) Warning pressure verification testRequirements
(1) The warning pressure of the spring braking system shall not be less than the initial pressure
for actuating the spring braking system
(2) When the warning pressure of the spring brake system is activated in the position of "ON"
switch, warning signal shall be operated as follows.
- warning signal shall be red so that the driver can easily check it
- warning signal shall be easily distinguishable from other warning signal, however, this
warning signal may be combined with the warning signal of other brake system.
MeasuringConditions
The spring brake system is released and the air pressure of the energy storage device for the
spring brake system is gradually decreased to set the warning pressure and the initial pressure
for actuating the spring brake system shall be measured.
Test vehicle stateLoaded and lightly-loaded state

(2) Operation and release testRequirements
The system shall be so designed that it is possible to apply and release the brakes at least three
times if the initial pressure for actuating the spring compression chamber is equal to the
maximum design pressure.Measuringconditions
(1) With the spring braking device released, the air pressure of the energy storage device for
the spring braking device is charged to the "P3" state, and the pipe is cut-off from the energy

Braking Performance for Trailers (Article 90 Subparagraph 3)

1. Brake force distribution (except for cars fitted with wheel locks)
A. Two axles full trailers
For full trailers with a wheelbase of 2 m or more, the adhesion utilization curves in unladen or
loaded state as shown in Fig. 1 shall meet the following criteria
(1) If Z is 0.15 or more and less than 0.30, the adhesion utilization curves of the front axle shall
be situated on the C line, and the adhesion utilization curves of the rear axle situated below
line A
(2) If Z is 0.30 or more 0.61 or less, the adhesion utilization curve of rear axle shall be situated
below line B.B. 3-or-more axles full trailers
For 3-or-more axle full trailers are subjected to the requirements for two axles full trailers.
However, if Z is 0.15 or more and less than 0.30, the adhesion utilization curves of at least one
front axle shall be situated above the adhesion utilization curves of at least one rear axle.
C. Trailers connected to towing vehicle
In the case of the trailers with compressed-air service brake system, the braking force distribution
curve shall meet the following requirements at a pressure of 7.5 bar or less (Pm), when the
trailers are connected and towed in a unladen or loaded state.
(1) The braking force distribution curve shall be within the range shown in Figure 2, if the full
trailer is towed
(2) When the center axle trailer is towed, the braking force distribution curve shall be within the
range obtained by multiplying the value read from the vertical axis of Figure 2 by 0.95
(3) When the semi-trailer is towed, the braking force distribution curve shall be within the range
obtained by multiplying the value read from the vertical axis of Figure 3 by the correction
factor (K) obtained by the following formula

K: Theoretical coefficient of adhesion between tire and road
g: Acceleration of gravity (10m/s2)P: Total weight of the trailer (N)
PR: Total weight on all wheels of a semi trailer or center axle trailer (N)
PR: Maximum of total mass on all wheels of a semi trailer or center axle trailer (N)
ER: Distance between king-pin and center of axle or axles of semi-trailer (m)
hR: Height of center of gravity of semi-trailer (m)
TR: Sum of braking forces at periphery of all wheels of the trailer or semi-trailer (m)

7. Warning signal in the event of the failure of anti-lock service brake system
Requirements
When the ignition switch is "ON", the yellow warning signal shall be installed in a towing vehicle
so that the driver can easily check it.
The yellow warning signal shall be easily distinguishable from others. However, in this case, this
yellow warning signal may be combined with the warning signal of other brake system.
Measuringconditions
Cut off the power supply cable of vehicle from the power cable of anti-lock service brake system
or from the input(output) cable to modulator which controls the braking force of anti-lock service
brake system and measure it.

8. Structure and braking performance for spring brake
A. Structure requirement
(1) A spring brake system shall not be used as a service braking system.
(2) It shall be able to release the spring brake system even if a failure occurs in the spring brake
system.
(3) It shall be structed such that the parking brake system of the trailers can be operated and
deactivated even after the trailer is connected to towing vehicle.
B. Brake performance requirement(1) Energy storage capacity testRequirements
The air pressure of spring compression chamber of trailers, when the control device of service
brake system of towing vehicle fully applied at 4th time, shall be not less than initial operated
pressure of spring brake system.MeasuringConditions
(1) Measure the air pressure in spring compression chamber of trailer with spring brake
activated, when the control device of service brake system of towing vehicle fully is applied 4
times repeatedly as setting the pressure in the energy storage devices of spring brake to 7.0 bar
(the pressure of the pneumatic control line at 7.5 bar for each braking application) and as
stopping the supply line.
(2) Measure the initial operating pressure of spring brake by reducing the air pressure in spring
compression chamberTest vehicle stateLaden and loaded state as connecting to a simulatorRemark) pressure unit = bar

(2) Release timeRequirements
The spring brake of trailers shall be able to release 3 times at least.
MeasuringConditions
(1) Separate air supply line and pneumatic control line in a condition of emergency brake
release, as setting air supply line pressure to 7.5 bar before disconnection from the towing
vehicle with spring brake activated.
(2) Measure the release time of spring brake by repeating the shift from release and operation
of the control of the spring brake for trailer
Test vehicle stateTrailer only (Unladen or loaded state)Remark) pressure unit = bar

Brake Performance Criteria for a Vehicle Equipped with an Anti-Lock Service Brake (Except
Trailers) (Article 90 Paragraph 4)

1. Energy Consumption Test ProcedureLow adhesion surfaceBraking time(sec)Vmax/7 (shall be not less than 15 seconds)Initial braking
speed (km/h)Not less than 50Vehicle state atthe start of
Engine is disconnected, or the energy storage device is disconnected. The anti-lock service
brake system is operative.Test Vehicle
(In case of a tow vehicle hauling a trailer equipped with a compressed-air brake system, the
compressed-air reservoir of 0.5 liter capacity shall stay connected.)
The anti-lock service brake shall remain operative for a period of maximum braking time
(sec), and all wheels with anti-lock service brake shall be controlled.
In case of a tow vehicle hauling a trailer equipped with a compressed-air brake system, when
its brake control is fully applied 5 times, the pressure of the reservoir shall not fall below a
level equivalent to 50 % of the figure obtained at the first brake application.

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)[Table 7-7]

Electronic Stability Control System (Article 90-2)

1. Performance requirements (Only applicable to the vehicle with a GVW of 4.5 tons or less)
A. The yaw rate measured one second after and 1.75 seconds after completion of the Sine with
Dwell steering input shall meet the following requirements:
1) 1.0 second: not to exceed 35% of the first peak value of yaw rate recorded after the steering
wheel angle changes sign (between first and second peaks) during the same test run; and
2) 1.75 seconds: not to exceed 20% of the first peak value of yaw rate recorded after the steering
wheel angle changes sign (between first and second peaks) during the same test run.
B. The lateral displacement of the vehicle center of gravity with respect to its initial straight path
shall meet the following requirements when computed 1.07 seconds after the Beginning of Steer
(BOS), when the Sine with Dwell maneuver of 0.7 Hz is performed with normalized steering
angles greater than 5.0.
1) vehicles with a GVW of 3.5 tons or less: At least 1.83 m,
2) vehicles with a GVW greater than 3.5 tons: At least 1.52 m.

Remark:
1. "Electronic Stability Control System" or "ESC System" means a system that has all of the
following attributes:
A. That improves vehicle directional stability by at least having the ability to automatically
control individually the braking torques of the left and right wheels on each axle or an axle
of each axle group (An axle group shall be treated as a single axle and dual wheels shall be
treated as a single wheel.) to induce a correcting yaw moment based on the evaluation of
actual vehicle behavior in comparison with a determination of vehicle behavior demanded
by the driver;
B. That is computer-controlled with the computer using a closed-loop algorithm to limit
vehicle oversteer and to limit vehicle understeer based on the evaluation of actual vehicle
behavior in comparison with a determination of vehicle behavior demanded by the driver;
C. That has a means to determine directly the value of vehicle's yaw rate and to estimate its
side slip or side slip derivative with respect to time;
D. That has a means to monitor driver steering inputs; and
E. That has an algorithm to determine the need, and a means to modify propulsion torque, as
necessary, to assist the driver in maintaining control of the vehicle.
2. "Yaw rate" means the rate of change of the vehicle's heading angle measured in
degrees/second of rotation about a vertical axis through the vehicle's center of gravity.
3. "Sideslip or side slip angle" means the arctangent of the ratio of the lateral velocity to the
longitudinal velocity of the center of gravity of the vehicle.
4. "Oversteer" means a condition in which the vehicle's yaw rate is greater than the yaw rate that
would occur at the vehicle's speed as result of the Ackerman Steer Angle.
5. "Understeer" means a condition in which the vehicle's yaw rate is less than the yaw rate that
would occur at the vehicle's speed as result of the Ackerman Steer Angle.
6. "Ackerman Steer Angle" means the angle whose tangent is the wheelbase divided by the
radius of the turn at a very low speed.
7. "Lateral acceleration" means the component of the vector acceleration of a point in the vehicle
perpendicular to the vehicle x axis (longitudinal) and parallel to the road plane.

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)2. ESC malfunction telltale
A. The vehicle shall be equipped with a telltale that provides a warning to the driver of the
occurrence of any malfunction that affects the generation or transmission of control or response
signals in the vehicle's electronic stability control system. The ESC malfunction telltale shall
meet the requirements specified in Item b' through Item d' below.
B. The ESC malfunction telltale shall meet each of the following requirements:
1) It shall be displayed in direct and clear view of the driver while in the driver's designated
seating position with the driver's seat belt fastened;
2) It shall appear perceptually upright to the driver while driving;
3) When illuminated, it shall be sufficiently bright to be visible to the driver under both daylight
and night time driving conditions, when the driver has adapted to the ambient roadway light
conditions;
4) Each ESC telltale shall be activated as a check of lamp function when the ignition locking
system is turned to the "On" ("Run") position when the engine is not running, and shall
extinguish. However, it need not be activated when a starter interlock is in operation, and it
does not apply to telltales shown in a common space.
5) It shall illuminate when a malfunction exists and shall remain continuously illuminated upon
occurrence of any malfunction that affects the generation or transmission of control or
response signals in the vehicle's ESC system
6) It shall extinguish at the next ignition cycle after the malfunction has been corrected;
7) It may also be used to indicate the malfunction of related systems/functions, including traction
control, trailer stability assist, corner brake control, and other similar functions that use throttle
and/or individual torque control to operate and share common components with ESC.
C. The manufacturer may use the ESC malfunction telltale in a flashing mode to indicate ESC
operation.
D. If the ESC malfunction telltale is not activated when the ESC is malfunctioning and when the
ignition locking system is in the "On" ("Run") position, drive the vehicle forward to obtain a
vehicle speed of 48+/-8km/h at the latest 30 seconds after the engine has been started and within
the next two minutes at this speed, conduct at least one left and one right smooth turning
maneuver without losing directional stability and one brake application. Verify that the ESC
malfunction indicator illuminates by the end of this maneuvers.

Remark:
"Common space" means an area on which more than one telltale, indicator, identification symbol,
or other message may be displayed but not simultaneously.

3. ESC Off and Other System Controls
A. The manufacturer may include an "ESC Off" control which shall be illuminated when the
vehicle's headlamps are activated and which has a purpose to place the ESC system in a mode
in which it may no longer satisfy the performance requirements of paragraph 1. Manufacturers
may also provide controls for other systems that have an ancillary effect upon ESC operation.
The "ESC Off" control and "the controls for other systems" shall meet the following
requirements specified in Item b' through Item e':
B. The vehicle's ESC system shall always return to the fully functional default mode that satisfies
the requirements of Article 15-2 Paragraph 2 Subparagraph 1 through Subparagraph 3 at the
initiation of each new ignition cycle, regardless of what mode the driver has previously selected.
However, the vehicle's ESC system need not return to a mode that satisfies the requirements of
paragraph 1 above at the initiation of each new ignition cycle if:

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
1) The vehicle is in a four-wheel drive configuration which has the effect of locking the drive
gears at the front and rear axles together and providing an additional gear reduction between
the engine speed and vehicle speed of at least 1.6, selected by the driver for low-speed, off-
road driving; or
2) The vehicle is in a four-wheel drive configuration selected by the driver that is designed for
operation at higher speeds on snow-, sand-, or dirt-packed roads and that has the effect of
locking the driver gears at the front and rear axles together, provided that in this mode the
vehicle meets the stability performance requirements of paragraph 1 Item a. However, if the
system has more than one ESC mode that satisfies the requirements of paragraph 1 Item a
within the drive configuration selected for the previous ignition cycle, the ESC shall return to
the manufacturer's original default ESC mode for that drive configuration at the initiation of
each new ignition cycle.
C. A control whose only purpose is to place the ESC system in a mode in which it can stop functions
shall be identified by the symbol or the text shown in Table 2. However, the vehicle with a GVW
exceeding 4.5 tons shall be identified by the symbol or the text defined by manufacturer.
D. A control for an ESC system whose purpose is to place the ESC system in different modes, at
least one of which may no longer satisfy the fully functional default mode of manufacturer shall
be identified by the symbol below with the text "OFF" adjacent to the control position for this
mode. Alternatively, in the case where the ESC system mode is controlled by a multi-functional
control, the driver display shall identify clearly to the driver the control position for this mode
using either the symbol in Table 2.or the text "ESC OFF". However, the vehicle with a GVW
exceeding 4.5 tons shall be identified by the symbol or the text defined by manufacturer.

E. A control for another system that has the ancillary effect of placing the ESC system in a mode
in which it no longer satisfies the performance requirements of paragraph 1 need not be identified
by the symbol or the text shown in Table 2.

Note) However, the proviso of Item b' shall be not applied for the vehicle with a GVW exceeding
4.5 tons.

4. "ESC Off" Telltale
A. If the manufacturer elects to install a control to turn off or reduce the performance of the ESC
system under paragraph 3, the telltale requirements of Item b' through Item d' below shall be met
in order to alert the driver to the lessened state of ESC system functionality. The requirement
does not apply for the driver-selected mode referred to in paragraph 3 Item b' 2).
B. The vehicle manufacturer shall provide a telltale indicating that the vehicle has been put into a
mode that can stop functions.
C. The "ESC Off" telltale shall meet each of the following requirements:
1) It shall be displayed in direct and clear view of the driver while in the driver's designated
seating position with the driver's seat belt fastened;
2) It shall appear perpendicularly upright to the driver while driving;
3) It shall be identified by the symbol or the text shown in Table 2, or shall be identified with
the English word "OFF" on or adjacent to either the control referred to in paragraph 3 Item c
and Item d. or the illuminated malfunction telltale shown in Table 2. However, the vehicle
with a GVW exceeding 4.5 tons shall be identified by the symbol or the text defined by

5) When illuminated, it shall be sufficiently bright to be visible to the driver under both daylight
and night time driving conditions, when the driver has adapted to the ambient roadway light

6) It shall remain continuously illuminated for as long as the ESC is in a mode that renders it
unable to satisfy the requirements of paragraph 1.
7) It shall be activated as a check of lamp function either when the ignition locking system is
turned to the "On" ("Run") position when the engine is not running, or when the ignition

8) It shall extinguish after the ESC system has been returned to its manufacturer's original default

D. The vehicle manufacturer may use the "ESC Off" telltale to indicate an ESC level of function
other than the fully functional default mode, even if the vehicle would operate normally, of ESC
function.

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)[Table 7-8]

Criteria for Structure and Performance Requirements of AEBS Installed in Buses and
Trucks/Special Purpose Vehicles with GVW Exceeding 3.5 Tons
(Article 90-3 Subparagraph 1)

1. Structure Requirements
A. AEBS shall be classified as "Collision warning phase1)" that automatically detects a potential
forward collision, provide the driver with a warning and "Emergency braking phase2)" that
activates the vehicle braking system to decelerate the vehicle.
B. The collision warning phase shall be provided by at least two modes selected from acoustic,
haptic or optical. However, if an optical means is used among at least two modes, the warning
indication confirming to Item j' shall be provided and the optical signal may be the flashing of
the failure warning signal specified in Table 2.
C. (Deleted)
D. The emergency braking phase shall not start before a TTC3) equal to or less than 3.0 seconds.
E. The driver can control with a high priority than AEBS if there is a driving behavior by a driver
such as kickdown (in an automatic transmission vehicle, pressing the accelerator pedal hard for
rapid acceleration to lower the gear), turn signal lamp operation, etc. when "Collision warning
phase" or "Emergency braking phase" in AEBS.
F. AEBS deactivation control system shall be installed to deactivate the AEBS, and it shall meet
the requirements specified in 1) to 3) below.
1) The AEBS function that has stopped working by AEBS deactivation control system shall be
automatically reinstated at the initiation of each new ignition "on" (run) cycle.
2) A constant warning indication confirming to Item j' shall inform the driver that the AEBS
function has been stopped if a driver operates AEBS deactivation control system, the failure
warning signal specified in Table 2 may be used for this purpose.
3) The warning indication specified in 2) or the failure warning signal shall be automatically
turned off, if AEBS is reinstated normally.
G. The failure warning signal in Table 2 as conforming to Item j' shall be constantly turned on,
unless AEBS meets the requirements specified in Subparagraph 2) due to the failure of control
signal or sensor.
H. When the driver is provided with an optical warning signal to indicate that the AEBS is
temporarily not available, for example due to inclement weather conditions, the signal shall be
constant and yellow in color. The failure warning specified in Item g' above may be used for this
purpose.
I. AEBS shall meet the requirements specified in Table 24 (Electromagnetic Compatibility).
J. The warning indication used to AEBS shall meet the requirements below.
1) The signal shall be directly and clearly verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.
2) The warning indication, if illuminated, shall have the sufficient brightness so that a driver
could recognize the indication in day-or-night time driving after adapting to the lighting
condition around the road.
3) Each AEBS optical warning signal shall be activated either when the ignition (start) switch is
turned to the "on" (run) position or when the ignition (start) switch is in a position between
the "on" (run) and "start" that is designated by the manufacturer as a check position. This
requirement does not apply to warning signals shown in a common space or the case that
engine-start lock is activated.

exceeding 8 tons. However, Std. 1 applies to the vehicles equipped with air
brake.

1) "Stationary target vehicle" means a target at standstill facing the same direction and positioned
on the center of the same test lane of travel as the subject vehicle.
2) "Moving target vehicle" means a target travelling at a constant speed in the same direction and
in the center of the same lane of travel as the subject vehicle.

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)[Table 7-9]

Criteria for Structure and Performance of Advanced Emergency Braking Systems Installed in
Passenger Cars and Trucks/Special Purpose Vehicles with GVW of 3.5 Tons or Less (Article
90-3 Subparagraph 2)

1. Structural requirements
A. AEBS shall be divided into a "collision warning phase" that warns the driver of the risk of
collision when a collision with pedestrians, bicycles, or vehicles in front of the driving lane is
expected, and an "advanced emergency braking phase" that automatically activates the brake
system. However, the operation of the "collision warning phase" and the "advanced emergency
braking phase" may be suspended if a condition where a collision is expected no longer exists.
B. For the collision risk warning that is provided to a driver in the "collision warning phase," two
or more warning methods shall be simultaneously used out of auditory, tactile, or visual
warnings.
C. The "collision warning phase" shall satisfy the following criteria according to the detection
target.
1) AEBS that detects a motor vehicle ahead in the lane of travel
In the case where a collision with a passenger car ahead in the lane of travel in a state of
driving at a relative speed greater than or equal to the speed at which the collision can be
avoided or a standstill state is imminent, a collision warning shall be provided at the latest 0.8
seconds before the start of the "advanced emergency braking phase." However, if a collision
with a vehicle cannot be predicted by the deadline for providing a collision warning signal, a
collision warning shall be provided until the start of the "advanced emergency braking phase."
2) AEBS that detects a pedestrian
In case of detecting a potential collision with a pedestrian crossing the road at a constant speed
of 5 km/h, a collision warning shall be provided until the "advanced emergency braking
phase" is initiated, at the latest.3) AEBS that detects a bicycle
In case of detecting a potential collision with a bicycle crossing the road at a constant speed
of 15 km/h, a collision warning shall be provided until the "advanced emergency braking
phase" is initiated, at the latest.
D. In case of detecting a possibility of an imminent collision in the "advanced emergency braking
phase", a deceleration control signal of 5 m/s2 or more shall be generated in order to activate the
service braking system of a motor vehicle.
E. In the case where the AEBS is not deactivated, it shall operate normally under all load conditions,
at least to the extent of the following scope of vehicle speed.
1) AEBS that detects a motor vehicle ahead in the lane of travel: 10 km/h - 60 km/h
2) AEBS that detects a pedestrian: 20 km/h - 60 km/h
3) AEBS that detects a bicycle: 20 km/h - 60 km/h
F. In the case where the driver does a clear driving action, such as kick-down (In an automatic
transmission vehicle, pressing the accelerator pedal hard for rapid acceleration to lower the gear)
or turn signal lamp operation, in the "collision warning phase" and "advanced emergency
braking phase" of the advanced emergency braking system, it shall be possible for the driver to
control the vehicle in preference to the operation of the advanced emergency braking system.
G. In the case where the deactivation control system, which stops the operation of the AEBS, is
installed, the following criteria shall be met.
1) The function of the AEBS, which has been stopped by the "deactivation control system," shall


<!-- Page 283 -->

© KAIDA
283
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
return to the state of normal operation with each new start cycle ("On" or "Run").
2) The operation of the AEBS shall not be deactivated manually by intentional operation of less
than 2 times.
3) If the speed of a motor vehicle exceeds 10 km/h, the AEBS shall not be deactivated manually.
H. In the case where a device that can stop the operation of the AEBS automatically is installed,
the following criteria shall be met.
1) The function of an AEBS may be stopped automatically under conditions such as an unpaved
road, towing, dynamometer, automatic car wash, etc., and the AEBS shall return to the state
of normal operation immediately in the case where the conditions for automatic knockoff no
longer exist.
2) In the case where the function of the advanced emergency braking system is automatically
stopped by manually stopping the function of the ESC (electronic stability control), the
operation of the advanced emergency braking system shall not be stopped by less than two
intentional operations.
I. While the autonomous driving function, which provides the same level of a collision avoidance
function as the advanced emergency braking system or a higher level than it, the function of the
advanced emergency braking system may be temporarily stopped or the advanced emergency
braking control strategy such as warning timing and braking deceleration may be adjusted
without separately notifying the driver.
J. The AEBS shall meet the criteria of Table 24 Electromagnetic Compatibility.
K. A "display device" used for an AEBS shall meet the following criteria.
1) It shall be clearly displayed so that the driver does not confuse it with other devices.
2) The driver shall be able to check the display device directly from the driver's seat without
operating any additional device.
3) It shall be possible to check without departing from the driver's seat vision range due to an
action of nodding while wearing a seat belt.
4) When the device is turned on, it shall provide sufficient brightness for clear recognition under
conditions of day/night driving after the driver adapts to the lighting around the road.
5) The device shall be activated either when the ignition (Start) switch is turned to the "On"
(Run) position or when the ignition (Start) switch is in a position between the "On" (Run) and
"Start" that is designated by the manufacturer as a check position before the motor starts.
However, this shall not apply to the warning lamp of the AEBS that is displayed in a shared
area or when the ignition lock is in operation.
6) The switching on/off of a "display device" shall meet the following criteria.

L. The AEBS shall be designed to minimize the activation in situations where there is no imminent
risk of a collision with a motor vehicle, a pedestrian, a bicycle, etc. ahead in the lane of travel.
M. The AEBS shall meet the following criteria for failure detection.
1) In case of any electrical failure relating to the control signal or sensor of the AEBS, the
"warning signal for AEBS failure" that satisfies the criteria under Item K shall be turned on
at least within 10 seconds after the vehicle speed exceeds 10 km/h.
2) In the case where the motor is stopped and the motor is driven again while the electrical failure
condition under 1) continues, the "warning signal for AEBS failure" that meets the criteria
under Item K shall be turned on immediately.

from the storage system occurs.3) The hydrogen storage container(s) shall remain attachedto the vehicle at a minimum of one attachment point.B. When a motor vehicle is caused to crash into a movingbarrier with its side at 50 km/hC. When a motor vehicle is caused to crash into a moving

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)2. Buses with a GVW of 4.5 tons or lessTest conditionsA. When a motor vehicle is caused to crashinto a fixed barrier with its width front at48-53 km/h (in the case of a low-speed
electric vehicle, it refers to the time when it
is caused to crash at 40 km/h)1) It shall not cause fire or explosion.
2) Not more than 7 percent of total capacity of electrolyte from traction
batteries shall spill outside the passenger compartment from the time
the vehicle ceases motion after a barrier impact test until 30 minutes
thereafter,
3) and no visible trace of electrolyte shall spill into the passenger
compartment.
4) No part of any battery system component shall enter the passenger
compartment.
5) Insulation resistance of high voltage live parts and exposed
conductive parts (electrical chassis) shall meet at least one of the
followings.
a) The voltage of Vb, V1, V2 shall be equal or less than 60 volts
(DC) and 30 volts(AC) within 60 seconds after the impact.
b) If consisting of separate AC and DC buses, each insulation
resistance shall be 100Ω/V[DC] or more and 500Ω/V[AC] or
more.
c) If consisting of electrically-combined AC and DC buses, at least
one of the followings shall be met.
(1) Insulation resistance between the high voltage live parts and
the electrical chassis shall be 500Ω/V or more
(2) If the test result of protection degree IPXXB is satisfied after
crash or voltages of Vb, V1, V2 are below 30V [AC], the
insulation resistance between high voltage live parts and
electrical chassis shall be 100Ω/V or more
d) The direct contact of live parts in passenger compartment or
luggage compartment shall not occur upon IPXXB approach and
when there is current flow of at least 0.2 amperes the isolated
resistance between all exposed conductive parts and the electrical
chassis shall be equal to or less than 0.1Ω.
e) The total energy (TE) shall be less than 2.0 joules (J) from 5 to 60
seconds after the crash.B. When a motor vehicle is caused to crashinto a moving barrier with its side at 50km/h (excluding low-speed EVs)C. When a motor vehicle is caused to crashinto a moving barrier with its rear at 48
km/h (excluding low-speed EVs)

1. Vb: Voltage of traction batteries
2. V1: Voltage between the negative pole (-) of a traction battery and the electrical chassis
(frame)
3. V2: Voltage between the positive pole (+) of a traction battery and the electrical chassis
(frame)

Frontal impactCorner impactconditionImpactor speed4 km/h2.5 km/h

Test Load and Installation Strength of Rear Underrun Protection Bar (Article 96)

1. Test Load
A The test load applied to the point P1 and P3 shall be 25% of the gross vehicle weight or 50 kN,
whichever is less, and the test load applied to the point P2 shall be 50% of the gross vehicle
weight or 100 kN, whichever is less.
B The application point of the test load shall be as follows:


(A) Between 700 mm and 1,000 mm(B) Within 300 +/- 25mm.
(C) Width of outer wheel of the rear axle (Outermost with the tire contact into the ground at the
standard inflation pressure)
(D) Not exceeding 600 mm: previously, the load is applied in the center

2. Installation Strength
When the load as specified in Subparagraph 1 is applied, the clearance between the rear underrun
protection bar and the rearmost area of the body which is not more than 2m above ground shall not
exceed 400mm.

Body Structure In the Crash Test (Article 102 Paragraph 3)

Test ConditionBody Structure Criteria1. When the vehicle isimpacted perpendicularlyinto a fixed collisionbarrier at 48.3 km/h – 53.1
km/h
A. For a horizontal range between 150 mm to the right and left from the center of the
seat, the distance between the vertical transverse plane passing the seating reference
point of the front seat and the vertical transverse plane passing the rearmost part of the
instrument panel shall be not less than 450 mm.
B. The distance between the vertical transverse plane passing the seating reference point
of the front seat and the front interior compartment door shall be not less than 650 mm
at the height of the center of the brake pedal.
C. The distance between the legroom of the front seat and the side wall shall be not less
than 250 mm at the height of the center of the brake pedal.
D. The vertical distance between the ceiling and floor passing the seating reference point
of the front seat shall not constrict 10% or more.
E. The side door shall not open at the moment of impact, and the occupants shall be able
to open the sufficient number of doors to exit without the use of tools.
2. When the vehicle isimpacted perpendicularlyon the rear by a barriermoving at 35 km/h – 38km/h
A. The deformation of the seating reference point of the rearmost seat shall not exceed
75 mm to the direction of the vehicle's longitudinal center line.
B. The side door shall not open at the moment of impact, and the occupants shall be able
to open the sufficient number of doors to exit without the use of tools.

Airbag Warning Label (Article 102 Paragraph 4)

1. The airbag warning of vehicle shall meet the requirements as follows.
A. The warning label shall be affixed to the outer and inner faces of the passenger front sun visor.

it is difficult to affix it on the inner face.

Injury Criteria of Test Dummy In the Pedestrian Headform and Legform Impact
(Article 102-2 Subparagraph 2 Item B)

Injury Criteria1. Headform
The injury criteria of the headform, or HIC, when calculated in accordance with
the following formula, shall meet each of the following requirements:
a. The HIC shall not exceed 1,000 over a minimum of one half of the child headform test area
and 1,000 over two thirds of the combined child and adult headform test area.
b. The HIC for the remaining areas shall not exceed 1,700 for both headforms.
c. In case there is only a child headform test area, the HIC shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds
of the test area. For the remaining area the HIC shall not exceed, 1,700.

where;
a: the resultant acceleration expressed as a multiple of g(the acceleration of gravity),
t1 and t2: any two points in time during the impact which are separated by not more than a 15
millisecond time interval.2. Legform
The injury criteria of the flexible low legform shall meet the following requirements.
a. the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament elongation
shall not exceed 13 mm.
b. the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22
c. the dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm. In addition, the
manufacturer may nominate bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total where
the absolute value of the tibia bending moment shall not exceed 380 Nm.
The injury criteria of the upper legform to bumper shall meet each of the following requirements:
a. The instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5kN.
b. The bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510Nm.
3. Splitting ofheadform test zoneand legform test
The manufacturer shall identify the zones of the headform test zone and the legform test zone
(where the HIC shall not exceed 1,000 (HIC1000 Zone) or 1,700 (HIC1700 Zone), for flexible low
legform, the dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 380 Nm), and shall be able to
submit the data when the requirements are met.

Performance Standards for Seat Belt (Article 103 Paragraph 1 and Article 112-3)

1. The seatbelt shall have neither sharp protrusion nor edge that can injure passengers.

2. Each part of the seatbelt shall be connected firmly, without crack or corrosion that can
damage its strength.

3. Performance standardsA. Standards for load under static conditionSubparagraphPerformance RequirementsTensile Strength

hereinafter the same shall apply in this table) of two strap samples shall be
not less than 14,700N after adjusting the environmental conditions, and the
braking loads of the two samples shall not exceed 10% of the greater of the
breaking load measured.
2) The breaking strength (the strength that is broken and separated) after
abrasion test shall be not less than 75% of the average value of normal state

Automaticallylocking retractors
1) The strap of seatbelt shall not move more than 30mm between locking

2) In case of the restraint of pelvic, the retracting force of the strap shall be not
less than 7N, in case of restraint of chest the retracting force of the strap
shall be not less than 1N and not more than 7N.

Emergency lockingretractors
1) It shall lock when the deceleration of the vehicle is 0.45 times of gravity
acceleration (0.85 times of gravity acceleration for the retractors with higher
response) or less.
2) It shall not lock for values of acceleration of the strap measured 0.8 times of
gravity acceleration (gravity acceleration for the retractors with higher
response) or less.
3) The amount of strap movement which may occur before the retractor locks
under the condition where the retractor locks shall not exceed 50mm.
4) It shall not lock be locked when its sensing device is tilted 12o or less in any
direction from the installation position.
5) It shall lock when its sensing device is tilted by 27o or more from the
installation position (40o for the retractor with higher response).

correctly after 45,000 cycles of withdrawal and retraction.

Seat beltdisplacement of
The seat belt shall meet any one of the following requirements.
1) Requirements for parts of seat belt
a) The pelvic displacement of 2-point and 3-point seat belts shall be between 80 and 200mm and
the thorax displacement of the 3-point seat belt shall be between 100 and 300mm.
b) In the case of a safety-belt of front seat with an airbag, the maximum displacement of the
chest may exceed 300mm if its speed at this value shall not exceed 24 km/h. In this case, the
seat belt shall be considered to meet the requirements.
2) Requirements for a seat belt when the manikin is seated in the vehicle
a) The seat belt installed in driver's seat shall meet the requirements pursuant to Article 89
Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 1 and shall be subject to any one of the following requirements.
(1) no contact of the head or of the chest with any part of the vehicle in front of the manikin
(2) if contacting the chest with the steering system, the speed of the chest shall not exceed 24
km/h
b) For the manikin with seat belt which is seated in other seats than driver's seat, a contact of the
head or of the chest with any part of the vehicle in front of the manikin would not be allowed.
Additionally, contact of the manikins head with its knees is not allowed.
