2) After the test, the deformation or crack which may damage the seat belt and deteriorate its
performance shall not be present.Note: The terms used in this table are defined as followed:
1. "Seatbelt adjuster" means the solid part designed to enable the belt to be adjusted according
to the requirements of the individual wearer and it consists of buckle, attachments and
retractor, etc.
2. "Micro slip test" means a test to measure the amount of slip minutely.
3. "Buckle" means the connecting part of the seatbelt and a quick-release (disconnected and
separated) device enabling the wearer to be held by the belt.
4. "Release force" means the force used to unfasten the buckle.
5. "Retractor" means the device to accommodate part or the whole of the strap of a safety-belt.
A. "Manually unlocking retractor" means a retractor requiring the manual operation of a
device by the user to unlock the retractor in order to obtain the desired strap extraction and
which locks automatically when this operation ceases.
B. "Automatically locking retractor" means a retractor allowing extraction of the strap to the
desired length and which, when the buckle is fastened, automatically adjusts the strap to
the wearer. Further extraction of the strap is prevented without voluntary intervention by
the wearer.
C. "Emergency locking retractor" means a retractor which during normal driving conditions
does not restrict the freedom of movement by the wearer of the safety-belt.
Ex.) Retractor that is locked by a locking device operated by sensing the deceleration of the
vehicle (single sensing function) or a combination of deceleration of the vehicle,
movement of webbing or any other automatic means (multiple sensing function) caused
by a vehicle emergency such as crash, collision, and rollover
6. "Attachment" means the part of the seatbelt made of metal or solid plastic and designed to
connect the seatbelt to the connecting device firmly.
7. "Seatbelt adjustment device for height" means a device enabling the position in height of the
upper pillar loop of a belt to be adjusted according to the requirements of the wearer.
8. "Pretensioner" means an additional or integrated device which tightens the seat-belt webbing
in order to reduce the slack of the belt during a crash sequence.
9. "Seatbelt dummy" means the test dummy with characteristics of human body used for seatbelt
parts test.
10. "Environmental condition adjustment" means the adjustment to lights (resistance to light),
the adjustment to low-temperature (resistance to cold temperature), the adjustment to high-
temperature (resistance to high temperature), and the exposure to water (water-resistance).
11. "Abrasion test" means the test to check if the performance of the product is deteriorated by
applying friction to the seatbelt.
12. "Dust test" means the test to determine if a malfunction is caused by the exposure to
environmental factors such as dust.
13. "Corrosion test" means the test to determine if the parts are damaged by the exposure to
environmental factors such as salt water.

Windshield Protected Zone (Article 105 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 3)

1. The protected zone is the space enclosed by the following surfaces:
A. The outer surface of the windshield.
B. The locus of points 76 mm outward along perpendiculars drawn to each point on the outer
surface of the windshield.
C. The locus of lines forming a 45 ° angle with the outer surface of the windshield at each point
along the top and side edges of the outer surface of the windshield and the lower edge of the
protected zone.

2. The lower edge of the protected zone is determined by the following procedure:
Place a 165 mm diameter rigid sphere, weighing 6.8 kg, in a position such that it simultaneously
contacts the inner surface of the windshield glazing and the surface of the instrument panel.
Draw the locus of points on the inner surface of the windshield contactable by the sphere across
the width of the instrument panel. From the outermost contactable points, extend the locus line
horizontally to the edges of the glazing material.
Draw a line on the inner surface of the windshield below and 12.7 mm distant from the locus line.
The lower edge of the protected zone is the longitudinal projection onto the outer surface of the
windshield of the line.

1. Vision area A is the area on the outer surface of the windshield bounded by the following four
planes extending forward from the V Point:

2) a vertical plane passing through V1 and V2 and at an angle of 20o to the right of the X axis
3) a plane parallel to the Y axis, passing through V1 and at an upward angle of 3o from the X axis
4) a plane parallel to the Y axis, passing through V2 and at a downward angle of 1o from the X axis

Structure and Performance Requirements of Speed Limit Device (SLD) (Article 110-2)

1. Structure requirementsA. General requirements
1) SLD shall be able to withstand the vibration of a vehicle running normally.
2) SLD shall not be affected under external electromagnetic environment.
3) SLD shall be designed so that it is difficult to arbitrarily modify its structures.
4) The control, operating and connection system shall be protected by the attachment of seal,
except that the function cannot be changed without using the diagnostic tool for engine control
unit.
5) SLD shall be designed so that the service brake system may not be used, except PC, trucks
with a GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons and special purpose vehicles with a GVW not exceeding
3.5 tons.
6) SLD shall be designed so that it may not affect the operation of transmission.
B. Fixed SLD: SLD in which the driver cannot arbitrarily change the Vmax
1) Fixed SLD shall be designed so that it can be operated when the engine key is positioned at
engine-on.
2) Fixed SLD shall be designed so that the max speed set (Vset) cannot be changed or deactivated
while vehicle running.
C. Adjustable SLD (ASLD): Adjustable speed limit device in which the driver can arbitrarily
change the Vmax.
1) ASLD shall be designed so that the Vadj can be checked continuously from the driver's seat.
2) It shall be possible to change or release Vadj.
3) At engine stop, Vadj shall be released.
4) If the accelerating is required, ASLD shall be designed so that it may exceed Vadj. In this
case, the warning signal or warning sound shall be continuously activated for warning the
driver.
5) It shall be possible to set Vadj value by steps no greater than 10 km/h between 30 km/h.
6) The initial setting of the Vadj shall be able to set at a speed higher than running speed.

2. Performance requirementsA. Fixed SLD1) Requirements at acceleration
a) The stabilized speed (Vstab) shall not exceed a tolerance of 5 % of the Vset value, or 5 km/h,
whichever is the greater.


<!-- Page 328 -->

328
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)

<Speed response curve>

b) After the Vstab is reached for the first time, the following requirements shall be met.
(1) Vmax shall be less than 105% of the Vstab.
(2) The rate of change of speed shall not exceed ±0.5 m/s2 when measured on a period of
0.1 second or more.
c) The following requirements shall be met within 10 seconds after the Vstab is reached for
the first time.
(1) The vehicle speed shall not vary by more than 4% of Vstab or 2 km/h, whichever is
greater.
(2) The rate of change of speed shall not exceed ±0.2 m/s2 when measured on a period 0.1
second or more.

d) The test shall be carried out for each gear ratio exceeding the Vset and the requirements in
a) through c) shall be met.2) Requirements at steady speed
a) The Vstab shall not exceed a tolerance of 5% of Vset or 5 km/h, whichever is greater.
b) The difference between the stabilization speeds obtained during each test run shall be equal
to or less than 3 km/h;.
c) The test shall be carried out for each gear ratio exceeding the Vset and the requirements in
a) through b) shall be met.

B. Adjustable SLD (ASLD)1) Requirements at accelerationa) The Vstab shall not exceed 3 km / h more than Vadj
b) After the Vstab is reached for the first time, the following requirements shall be met.
(1) Vmax shall not be more than 105% of the Vstab.
(2) The rate of change of speed shall not exceed ±0.5 m/s2 when measured on a period of
0.1 second or more.
c) The following requirements shall be met within 10 seconds after the Vstab is reached for
the first time.(1) The vehicle speed shall not vary by more than 3 km/h.
(2) The rate of change of speed shall not exceed ±0.2 m/s2 when measured on a period 0.1
second or more.
d) The test shall be carried out for each gear ratio exceeding the Vadj and the requirements in
a) through c) shall be met.2) Requirements for warning signal
The driver shall be informed continuously by a warning signal when the actual speed of the
vehicle is exceeding Vadj by more than 3 km/h.

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)※ Remarks
1. Vehicles specified in each Subparagraph of Article 54 Paragraph 2 shall be equipped with a fixed
SLD. However, other vehicles may be equipped with either a fixed SLD or ASLD.
2. "Vset" refers to the vehicle speed when the limitation speed is set by the manufacturer as the
target so that the vehicle be operated in a stabilized condition.
3. "Vstab" refers to the actual mean vehicle speed that is aimed at the Vset and refers to the mean
vehicle sped measured when the speed becomes stable after full acceleration.
4. "Vmax" refers to the maximum speed reached by the vehicle in the first half period of the
response curve after the acceleration is initiated with SLD operative.
5. " Vadj" refers to the vehicle speed that the driver has set arbitrarily to limit the speed of the
vehicle.

Safety Standard for the Partially Automated Driving System (Article 111-3)

1. Performance requirements of automated lane keeping function
A. General requirements for activation/deactivation of the automated lane keeping system
1) The vehicle shall be equipped with means for the driver to activate (active mode) and
deactivate (off mode) the automated lane keeping system. In these cases, the means of starting
(active mode) and turning off (off mode) the automated lane keeping system (ALKS) shall be
the same.
2) The means of turning off the ALKS (off mode) shall meet the following criteria:
a) The system should be turned off (off mode) if the driver engages one input device once for
over a certain amount of time, engages such device twice consecutively, or engages in two
input devices simultaneously.
b) The system should be operated in a manner that allows the driver to assume horizontal
control of the motor vehicle immediately upon turning off the ALKS (off mode), e.g., the
input device is on the steering control system, allowing the ALKS to be turned off only
when the driver is in control of the steering control system, etc.
3) The default status of the ALKS shall be deactivated (off mode) at the initiation of each new
engine (including internal combustion engine, traction motor, and fuel cell; hereinafter the
same shall apply) start/run cycle. However, this requirement does not apply when the engine
start/run cycle is performed automatically by the operation of a stop/start function by a
traveling vehicle.
4) The ALKS shall become operational only when all of the following conditions are met, and
if any of the conditions from B) to F) is not met during operation, the system shall immediately
request a transition to manual driving.
a) The ALKS shall become active only upon a deliberate action by the driver
b) the driver is in the driver seat and the driver's safety belt is fastened
c) the scanning of drivability under Subparagraph 2 Item C should reveal that the driver is
able to engage in direct driving
d) all functions comprising the ALKS and related functions and devices that are necessary for
the operation of the motor vehicle using the ALKS, including the following items, shall be
normally functioning.(1) Self-diagnosis function(2) Driver monitoring system(3) Data storage system for automated driving (DSSAD)
e) activates only when the road on which vehicle travels shall meet all of the following
conditions(1) Road where pedestrians and cyclists are prohibited
(2) Road equipped with a physical separation (e.g. median strip, etc.) that divides the traffic
moving in opposite directions of the traveling vehicle
f) When the vehicle is within the operational design domain (ODD)
5) Input value criterion, which allows the partially automated driving system to determine
whether control of the steering control system, braking device and or acceleration control
system exerted by the driver during the operation of the ALKS is in fact intended by the driver,
(hereinafter "control input criterion") shall be set on each device. In such cases, the control
input criterion of the steering control system shall be set as follows:
a) Values pertaining to the forces and time of control exerted on the steering control system


<!-- Page 332 -->

© KAIDA
332
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)shall be included;
b) Adjusted based on a variable that includes a criterion to confirm if the driver is in a state of
attention under Subparagraph 2 Item D;
6) If the driver engages the steering control system, braking device or acceleration control system
while the ALKS is in operation, the system shall operate as follows: Provided, however, in
case where the partially automated driving system has perceived that operation in accordance
with the following may realize an imminent risk of collision, the system may ignore the
driver's control input or appropriately adjust the steering, braking and acceleration of the
motor vehicle arising from the driver's control input.
a) If the driver's control input does not exceed the control input criterion, such control input
shall be ignored.
b) Where the driver is operating the steering control system, if the steering input value due to
the driver's engagement of the steering control system exceeds the control input criterion,
the ALKS shall be immediately deactivated.
c) The driver operates the braking device.
(1) In cases where the braking control input arising from the driver's operation of the
braking device exceeds the control input criterion, the system shall immediately request
a transition to manual driving.
(2) In cases where deceleration power arising from the driver's operation of the braking
device is higher than the deceleration power arising from the operation of the ALKS
(including where deceleration is 0) or where the motor vehicle is maintained in a
stationary state due to the driver's engagement of the braking device, brake power shall
be generated in accordance with the driver's engagement of the braking device.
(3) In cases where the driver operates the braking device while holding the steering control
system and the partially automated driving system controls the speed of the motor vehicle
as the driver engages it, the ALKS shall be deactivated.
d) Where the driver operates the acceleration control system.
(1) In cases where the acceleration input from the driver's operation of the acceleration
control system exceeds the control input criterion, a request for transition to manual
driving shall be immediately made.
(2) In cases where the driver may control the speed of the motor vehicle in a manner
consistent with his or her operation of the acceleration control system, acceleration power
shall be generated in accordance with the operation exerted by the driver. Provided,
however, that if it is anticipated that such operation renders the motor vehicle unable to
maintain the critical distance to the front under Item B 5) a), causes the speed of the
motor vehicle to exceed the designated maximum speed, or otherwise renders the
operation of the motor vehicle incompliant with the standards set forth in this table, the
speed of the motor vehicle shall be maintained through the ALKS.
(3) Where the driver operates the acceleration control system while holding the steering
control system and the partially automated driving system controls the speed of the motor
vehicle in accordance with the operation exerted by the driver, the ALKS shall be
deactivated.
e) In cases where the ALKS is deactivated in accordance with the provisions in Items B)
through D) above, or where the partially automated driving system requests a transition to
manual driving, the driver shall be notified in accordance with the standards for interaction
between the driver and the motor vehicle set forth in Item E).
f) Where a serious failure has occurred in the partially automated driving system or the motor
vehicle, the partially automated driving system may operate in a manner not consistent with


<!-- Page 333 -->

© KAIDA
333
KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
the standards prescribed in Items B) through D) above even if the driver operates the
steering control system, braking device or the acceleration control system. However, even
in such cases, the change of driving mode shall be conducted safely.
7) Where the driving mode change request function or the minimum risk maneuver function is
active, the ALKS shall be deactivated only in the following cases:
a) Where the automated lane keeping system is deactivated in accordance with 2) or 6) above.
b) Where it is perceived that the driver is holding the steering control system and is in attention
as defined in Subparagraph 2 Item D.
8) In cases where the ALKS is deactivated, the related functions of the motor vehicle shall be
activated as follows:
a) Even if the ALKS is deactivated, the motor vehicle shall not automatically shift to a mode
that continuously controls the vertical and horizontal movement of the motor vehicle
simultaneously or separately. Provided, however, a steering revision function comprising
an advanced steering assistance device installed additionally on the main steering control
system of the motor vehicle may be automatically activated.
b) In cases where the steering revision function is automatically activated in accordance with
the front-end section of Proviso A) above, the system shall operate in such a way that the
steering power assistance generated as a result of the activation of the steering revision
function is gradually reduced.
c) The safety devices and functions of the motor vehicle that support the vehicle's vertical and
horizontal directional control whose function was limited or deactivated as a result of the
activation of the ALKS, including the advanced emergency braking system, motor vehicle
stability control device, brake assist system, emergency steering function, etc., shall be
restored to their original function and operate accordingly.
B. Cope with driving conditions and headway control of the ALKS
1) The activated ALKS shall be able to cope with the ODD specified by the manufacturer, or
otherwise provide sufficient time for the driver to cope with a transition demand signal of
ALKS.
2) The ALKS shall be operated in such a way that the outer surface edge of the motor vehicle's
front wheel tire does not go beyond the outer boundary of the lane being traveled, and a stable
horizontal direction is maintained in the lane so that confusion is not caused to other drivers
on the road. Provided, however, that in cases where the lane change function is activated as a
result of minimum risk operation, the outer boundary of the lane being traveled may be
crossed.
3) In its operation, the ALKS shall be able to detect other vehicle traveling the lanes adjacent to
the lane the motor vehicle is currently traveling and appropriately adjust the speed and
horizontal location of the motor vehicle in the lane currently being traveled as necessary.
4) The activated ALKS shall be able to automatically control the speed of the vehicle as the
following.a) The maximum operational speed shall not exceed 110 km/h.
b) The speed limit of the road being traveled (refers to the speed limit under Article 17
Paragraph 1 or 2 of the Road Traffic Act) shall not be exceeded.
c) The activated ALKS shall automatically adapt the speed according to the traveling road
conditions and environmental conditions (for example, change of road curvature, heavy
rain, snow, etc.).
5) In its operation, the ALKS shall be able to adjust the distance to the vehicle ahead in the lane
being traveled as follows:
a) If the motor vehicle is not in a stationary state, the distance between the motor vehicle in

B) Despite Item A) above, in cases where the critical distance to the front under Item A) above
is temporarily unable to be maintained as a result of other road users such as a motor vehicle
cutting into the front from an adjacent lane, or as a result of a motor vehicle in front reducing
speed, but emergency maneuver is not necessary, the critical distance to the front should be
maintained without sudden braking.
6) The ALKS in operation shall, in cases where another motor vehicle or a pedestrian in front is
at a standstill or the road is blocked, be able to completely stop the motor vehicle at a point
behind such other motor vehicle, pedestrian or roadblock.
7) The ALKS in operation shall be able to perceive imminent risk of collision and automatically
engage in maneuver to minimize the risk to the safety of the driver and passengers of the
motor vehicle, and other road users in the event of an unforeseen situation, such as a motor
vehicle in front reducing speed, cutting-in, an obstacle suddenly appearing after a motor
vehicle in front changing lanes, etc. In such cases, the ALKS shall not be deactivated, and the
motor vehicle shall not be controlled in an unreasonable manner.
8) In cases where a situation set forth in the former parts of Paragraph 7) occurs and falls under
one of the following circumstances, the ALKS in operation shall ensure that the motor vehicle
in motion does not collide with a motor vehicle or an obstacle in front, etc.
a) A motor vehicle in motion at a distance equal or greater than the critical distance to the
front reduces its speed within its maximum braking capacity.
b) Where a motor vehicle cuts into the front of the motor vehicle in motion from an adjacent
lane, falling under all of the below:
(1) The motor vehicle from the adjacent lane cuts in while maintaining a vertical speed
lower than the vertical speed of the motor vehicle in motion.
(2) Where another motor vehicle is cutting in, the partially automated driving system
detects the horizontal movement of such other vehicle 0.72 seconds before the outer
surface edge of the vehicle's front wheel tire reaches a point 0.3m over the outer boundary
of the lane (hereinafter the "reference location of anticipated collision time") that is

9) The ALKS in operation shall immediately engage in a maneuver designed to reduce the risk
of collision in the event where a pedestrian is perceived crossing the road in front when the
motor vehicle is traveling at a speed exceeding 60 km/h.
C. Requirements for the detection range of the partially automated driving system
1) The partially automated driving system shall be equipped with detection capabilities enabling
it to perceive the driving environment and traffic situation, including the structure of the road,
lanes, other motor vehicles in motion, etc., of the scope including the shadowed parts in the
figure below.

[Detection range of the partially automated driving system]

vehicles, pedestrians, etc. in front are detected) and side detection distance (distance within
which motor vehicles on the side are detected) shall meet the standards under the following
categorization:
a) Front detection distance measured from the front end of the motor vehicle shall be at least
the minimum front detection distance set forth in the table below for each specified
maximum speed level. In such cases, the minimum front detection distance of the specified

b) Side detection distance shall be at least the width of the right and left adjacent lanes of the
lane currently being traveled.
3) The system shall be equipped with capabilities enabling it to detect environmental conditions
that reduce the range of detection and to respond to such reduction of detection range [refers
to functions such as terminating the initiation of activation of the automated lane keeping
system, deactivation of the automated lane keeping system, making requests for transition to
manual driving, and limiting the speed of the motor vehicle in cases where visibility is
extremely poor].
4) During the useful life of the partially automated driving system (refers to the period designated
by the manufacturer of the partially automated driving system), the detection capabilities of
the partially automated driving system shall not be reduced to below the standards set forth in
this table even if parts or devices comprising the system are worn or aged.
5) Even if temporary failure occur in one perception capability, the system shall not cause risk
situations impeding the safe operation of the motor vehicle unless such failure constitutes a
breakdown.
D. Requirements for transition demand of partially automated driving system
1) The activated system shall recognize situations in which it needs to transition the control back
to the driver and sufficient time for transition shall be provided to ensure safe transition to
manual driving
2) The transition demand shall meet the following requirements
a) In the case of detecting the occurrence of an expected situation, a request for transition to
manual driving shall be made sufficiently in advance so that the motor vehicle may be
safely stopped through minimum risk maneuver even if the driver does not respond to the
partially automated driving system's request for transition to manual driving.
b) In case of an unplanned event is detected, a transition demand shall be given upon detection.
c) In case of any failure that hinders with the operation of system, the system shall
immediately initiate a transition demand upon detection. Provided, however, that in cases
where a serious failure has occurred in the partially automated driving system or the motor
vehicle (including where a serious failure has occurred while a request for transition to
manual driving is being made), minimum risk maneuver may be immediately initiated
without making a request for transition to manual driving.
d) In cases where minimum risk maneuver is conducted in accordance with the Proviso of
Item C) above, the partially automated driving system may operate in a manner not
consistent with the standards set forth in this table, but even in such cases, the system shall
ensure that the transition to manual driving is made as safely as possible.
3) The following requirements shall be met during the transition demand phase.
a) The ALKS shall be in continuous operation even when a request for transition to manual
driving is being made.
b) During the transition demand, the system may reduce the speed of the traveling vehicle but

(1) Where the motor vehicle cannot continue to be driven, including where there is a

(2) Where the motor vehicle is traveling at a speed of less than 20 km/h and the partially
automated driving system has transmitted a signal requesting transition to manual driving,
including by a sensory signal, or has amplified a signal requesting transition to manual
driving in accordance with Item 4) below.
c) The system shall activate the hazard warning lamp within 5 seconds after the vehicle was
brought to standstill due to a situation in Item b) above.
d) If the driver does not respond in a manner prescribed in Item A 2) A), 6) B) of the same
Item, the same 6) C) (3), the same 6) D) (3) or the same Item 7) B) within 10 seconds of a
request for transition to manual driving is first made, minimum risk maneuver shall be

4) The signal requesting transition to manual driving shall be amplified within 4 seconds of

5) A transition demand shall be deactivated only for the following cases.
a) If the driver deactivates the automated lane keeping system
b) If a minimum risk manoeuvre has started
E. Requirements related to the human machine interface
1) The partially automated driving system shall send signals to the driver in accordance with the
following categorization. In such cases, visual signals shall be of appropriate size and
brightness to allow the driver to easily perceive them, and audio signals shall be loud and
clear.a) Signal indicating the state of operation of the ALKS.
(1) Cases where the driver has intentionally activated the ALKS but the system cannot be
activated: At least a minimally sufficient visual signal shall be generated.
(2) In cases where the ALKS is in operation (active mode): A visual signal shall be
generated as follows:
(A) An exclusively designated visual signal shall be generated using all of the following
methods:
(a) A warning signal combining either the letter "A" or the word "AUTO" and a figure
representing the steering control system or the exterior of the motor vehicle is turned
on.
(b) A warning signal other than the one specified in Item (a) above is turned on. In
such cases, the location of the signal shall be within the sight of the driver toward
the front of the motor vehicle from the driver's seat, such as the dashboard, the edge
of the steering control system facing the driver, etc.
(B) The visual signal shall be indicated until the ALKS is deactivated (off mode).
Provided, however, that when a request for transition to manual driving or minimum
risk maneuver has been initiated, the warning signal under Item (A)(a) above may be
substituted with a warning signal under Item C) or D) below.
(C) In cases where a request for transition to manual driving is initiated while the ALKS
is in operation, the warning signal under Item (A)(b) above shall flash repeatedly or
shall be shown in a different color, etc. distinguishing the request for transition to
manual driving from the signal generated therebefore. If the prior signal is indicated
by being flashed repeatedly, the signal shall flash at a low frequency that does not
interfere with the driver's perceiving that a request for transition to manual driving has

(3) Where the ALKS has been deactivated (off mode): The signal shall be generated in

(A) The ALKS activation (active mode) signal and the signal requesting transition to

(B) Where the driver has deactivated the ALKS in response to a request for transition to

b) Signal indicating failure of the partially automated driving system: At least a minimally
sufficient visual signal indicating the failure of the partially automated driving system shall
be generated. In such cases, a signal may not be generated if the ALKS has been deactivated
(off mode).
c) Signal requesting transition to manual driving: The signal shall meet the following criteria:
(1) The signal requesting transition to manual driving shall comprise a visual signal and an
audio signal, a visual signal and a sensory signal, or a visual signal, audio signal and a
sensory signal. Here, the visual signal shall consist of a figure representing two hands
and a steering control system, and may be accompanied by additional explanatory
phrases or warning symbols.


[Example of Optical Signal for Transition to Manual Driving]

(2) Where the signal requesting transition to manual driving is being amplified in
accordance with Item D 4) while the motor vehicle is not in a stationary state, a sensory
signal shall be generated either continuously or intermittently in addition to the signal
under (1) above.
d) Signal indicating minimum risk maneuver: The signal shall consist of a visual signal and
an audio signal, a visual signal and a sensory signal or a visual signal, audio signal and a
sensory signal. In such cases, the visual signal shall indicate the urgency of the need to
transition to manual driving, by using the following visual expression or expressions of
equivalent visual effect: The figure representing the steering control system flashes in red,
while the figure representing two hands are repeatedly shown gripping the steering control
system.
e) The signal in D) above shall be indicated in such a way that it is distinguished from the
signal requesting transition to manual driving.
f) Signal indicating emergency maneuver: Only a visual signal shall be used.
2) In cases where a request for transition to manual driving or minimum risk maneuver has been
initiated or the ALKS has been deactivated, the functions of the display devices embedded in
the motor vehicle (functions that are only activated while the ALKS is in operation and are
unrelated to driving) shall be automatically deactivated.
F. Standards for minimum risk maneuver of the partially automated driving system.
1) Once minimum risk maneuver has been initiated, the speed of the motor vehicle shall be
reduced at a deceleration rate not exceeding 4㎨ in the lane being traveled (if lane markings
are not clear, in an appropriate route considering the surrounding traffic and road

following circumstances:
a) Serious failure has occurred to the partially automated driving system or the motor vehicle.
b) Speed is reduced within a short time to induce a sensory warning to the driver.
2) The emergency light shall start flashing simultaneously with the activation of the minimum
risk maneuver function.
3) If the driver does not deactivate the ALKS after minimum risk maneuver has been initiated,
the motor vehicle shall be automatically and safely stopped in the lane being traveled.
4) The minimum risk maneuver (MRM) shall be terminated only when one of the following
cases are applicable:
a) If the automated lane keeping system is deactivated by the driver
b) Where the motor vehicle has been stopped in accordance with 3) above.
5) If the partially automated driving system has been designed in a manner permitting lane
changes during minimum risk maneuver, the motor vehicle shall change its lane to a side lane
or a lane with reduced risk of accident and engage in minimum risk maneuver in accordance
with the standards set forth in 1) through 3) above. In such cases, lane change shall be

designated based on the safety distance calculated according to the following formula:

6) The ALKS shall be automatically deactivated (off mode) at the end of the minimum risk
manoeuvre function and shall be activated (active mode) after a new engine start/run cycle is
performed.
7) Even after minimum risk maneuver has been terminated in accordance with 4) B) above, if
the driver does not engage in driving, the vehicle shall remain stopped and the emergency
lights shall continue to flash until the driver deactivates them.
G. Standards for emergency maneuver of the partially automated driving system.
1) If an imminent risk of collision or a situation requiring vertical deceleration at a rate exceeding
5 ㎨ has been detected while the ALKS is in operation, emergency maneuver shall be
initiated.
2) Once emergency maneuver has been initiated, the motor vehicle shall decelerate at a rate
suitable in light of the vehicle's maximum braking capacity. Provided, however, that when
necessary given the road and traffic condition, the motor vehicle may decelerate while evading
other motor vehicles and obstacles or may evade such other vehicles and obstacles without
decelerating.
3) In case where the motor vehicle evades other motor vehicles and obstacles in accordance with
the Proviso of 2) above, the outer surface edge of the front wheel tire of the motor vehicle
shall not cross the outer boundary of the lane being traveled, and once the evasive maneuver
has been completed, the motor vehicle shall be restored to a stable position as soon as possible.
4) Emergency maneuver shall be deactivated only when the imminent risk of collision has been
eliminated or the driver has deactivated the ALKS, and once emergency maneuver has been
deactivated, measures shall be taken in accordance with the following: Provided, however,
that where the driver has deactivated the ALKS and an imminent risk of collision exists,
emergency maneuver may be deactivated in a manner whereby the partially automated driving
system delays the deactivation of the ALKS until the imminent risk of collision has been
eliminated.
a) Even when emergency maneuver has been deactivated because the imminent risk of
collision has been eliminated, the ALKS shall remain operational.
b) In case where the motor vehicle has come to a complete stop as a result of emergency
maneuver, the emergency lights shall flash, and shall be deactivated once the motor vehicle
resumes movement with the guidance of the ALKS.
5) Where the motor vehicle reduces speed in accordance with 2) above, the emergency braking
signal shall be generated in accordance with the emergency braking signal generation
standards set forth in Attached Table 5-2 Subparagraph 1.

H. Failure-preventive design standards for the partially automated driving system
1) The partially automated driving system shall be designed based on consideration of system
redundancy, etc. so that the system will continue operation without causing significant risks
to the safe operation of the motor vehicle even in the event of error in the electronic control
system, disconnection of the sensor, electronic signal cut-off and other failures.
2) The system shall be designed in a such a way that self-diagnostics will be regularly carried
out in accordance with the following methods:
a) Method whereby the partially automated driving system and the partially automated system
are activated to detect errors in functions and devices needed for the operation of the motor
vehicle.
b) Method that examines the sensory capability of the senor, by means such as causing the
system to detect objects, etc. at least once at a distance exceeding the detection distance.

2. Performance criteria of the driver monitoring system
A. General criteria
The partially automated driving system shall be equipped with a driver monitoring system that
always detects whether the driver is properly seated in the driver's seat, wearing the seatbelt,
capable of driving operation, etc.
B. Criteria for warning signals on the driver's seating, etc. and operation of the driver monitoring
system:
If the driver is not wearing the seatbelt while the ALKS is in operation or is absent from the
driver's seat for more than 1 second, a request for transition to manual driving shall be initiated.
In such cases, where an audio signal is generated to make the request for transition to manual
driving, the audio signal may be substituted by the two-phase warning under the seatbelt
reminder operation standards set forth in Separate Table 5-24 Subparagraph 2 Item B.
C. Criteria for detecting, etc. whether the driver is capable of driving operation
1) In the event where the driver wearing the seatbelt and seated in the driver's seat does not
engage in two or more of the following activities for 30 seconds, the partially automated
driving system shall continuously generate a warning signal distinct from other signals that
the motor vehicle is able to generate until the driver's activities are detected.
A) Operation of the motor vehicle control system designated exclusively for the driver.
B) Intentional movement of the head or the body.
C) Keeping the eye open.D) Blinking of the eyes.
2) Despite the provisions of 1) A) through D) above, the manufacturer may enable the system to
detect the activities of the driver in accordance with an activity indicator other than, but of
equivalent detection capacity to, the activity indicator set forth in aforesaid provisions.
3) If the driver's activity does not satisfy the driving capability detection criteria even after the
warning sign is generated in accordance with 1) above, a request for transition to manual
driving under Subparagraph 1 Item D shall be generated within 15 seconds after the initiation
of the warning signal.
D. Standards for detecting whether the driver is in an alert state
1) The partially automated driving system shall be able to detect whether the driver is in attention.
2) The detection of attention status in accordance with 1) above shall be made by ascertaining
whether the driver is in the following conditions: In such cases, the driver shall be deemed to
be in a state of attention if one of the following is true:
A) The driver is mainly looking toward to the road in front;
B) The driver is looking toward the direction of the rear-reflection devices.

3. Performance criteria of the automated driving recording device.
A. Record target
The automated driving data recording device shall record the following events:
1) Activation of the ALKS2) Deactivation of the ALKS due to the following:
A) The driver operates the deactivation control (off mode) of the ALKS
B) Deactivation in accordance with Subparagraph 1 Item A 6) B), the same 6) C) (3) or the
same 6) D) (3).
3) The automated driving system requests transition to manual driving in response to the
following:A) Planned eventB) Unplanned event
C) A circumstance set forth in the former parts of Subparagraph 2 Item B (that is, the driver
is not wearing the seatbelt while the ALKS is in operation or is absent from the driver's seat
for more than 1 second).
D) A circumstance set forth in Subparagraph 2 Item C 1) [where the driver is not detected
engaged in two or more of the activities set forth in 1] A) through D) for 30 seconds
(including as determined by another activity indicator applied by the manufacturer in
accordance with 2) of the same Item)].E) Failure of the partially automated driving system
F) Request for transition to manual driving in accordance with Subparagraph 1 Item A 6) C)
(1) and 6) D) (1).
4) Ignoring of control input and adjustment in accordance with partial Proviso other than
Subparagraph 1 Item A 6) A) through F).5) Initiation and termination of emergency maneuver6) Operation of the event data recorder (EDR)7) Collision recognition8) Start of minimum risk manoeuvre (MRM)
9) Serious failure of the partially automated driving system
10) Serious failure of the motor vehicle
B. Record contents
1) The automated driving data recording device shall record the events set forth in Item A with
the following items in a clear and recognizable manner.
A) Type of event that occurredB) Reason for event occurrenceC) The date of the event (in "0000-00-00" format)
D) The time of the event [to be recorded in "00:00:00" format in Korean Standard Time (KST),
with a recording accuracy of ±1 second]
2) When recording the events set forth in Item A, the identification number or version of the
ALKS software at the time of the event shall be clearly distinguishable.
3) In cases where multiple events have occurred within the minimum unit of time for recording
of events under 1) D) above (1 second), the time of occurrence of each event may be recorded

as the same point of time. In such event, the events shall be recorded by the order of their
occurrence.C. Storage and extraction of recorded data
1) The automated driving data recording device shall be able to store the data of events occurring
over a period of 6 months or more, or at least 2,500 separate events regardless of the time
period over which they occur.
2) Once the automated driving data storage device has reached the end of its storage capacity,
pre-existing data may be written over in the order of their recording.
3) Data stored in the automated driving data storage device shall be extractable even in the event
of a collision of an impact level consistent with each testing condition set forth in Separate
Tables 14, 14-2, 14-7 and 14-8, and all recorded data shall be extractable even when the power
supplier embedded in the motor vehicle is not available for use.
4) Recorded data shall be able to be read through standardized communication interface, such
as OBD terminals.
5) Data recorded in the automated driving data recording device shall be viewable in a manner
not hindering a statutorily authorized viewer from ascertaining the contents thereof, or through
provision of a viewing method by the manufacturer.
D. Prohibition against manipulation of recorded data
Manipulation of recorded data shall be prevented through appropriate designs preventing forgery,
tempering, etc. of data and or other technical means.
E. Confirmation of operation status
The automated driving system shall be able to ascertain whether the automated driving data
recording device is properly operated through communication with the device.

1. "ALKS" refers to the function of the motor vehicle that, once activated/operated by the driver,
affects the horizontal and vertical movement of the motor vehicle without additional intervention
of the driver for a long period of time, ensuring that the vehicle maintains its current lane.
2. "Request for transition to manual driving" refers to a request made by the partially automated
driving system to the driver to operate manual driving to affect transition from partially automated
driving to manual driving.
3. "Planned event" is a situation which is known in advance, e.g. at the time of activation such as a
journey point (e.g. exit of a highway) etc. and which requires a transition demand.
4. "Unplanned event" is a situation which is unknown in advance, but assumed as very likely in
happening, (e.g. road construction, inclement weather, approaching emergency vehicle, missing
lane marking, load falling from truck) and which requires a transition demand.
5. "Imminent risk of collision" refers to a situation where the motor vehicle cannot avoid a collision
with other users of the road or obstacles with a rate of deceleration lower than 5 ㎨.
6. "Minimum risk manoeuvre" refers to the function of the partially automated driving system that is
automatically activated to minimize risk in the event where the driver does not respond to a request
for transition to manual driving or a serious failure has occurred in the partially automated driving
system or the motor vehicle.
7. "Emergency manoeuvre" refers to the function of the partially automated driving system that is
automatically engaged in the event of an imminent collision to avoid the collision or to minimize
the damage from the collision.
8. "Designated maximum speed", which is designated by the motor vehicle manufacturer, refers to
the highest speed at which the functions of the ALKS may be normally operated under optimal
conditions permitting the operation of the ALKS.

KMVSS (Korea Motor Vehicle SafetyStandards)MOLIT Ordinance No. 1520 (2025.08.14)

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
9. "Detection distance" refers to the distance at which the partially automated driving system may
definitely detect objects and generate appropriate control signals during the useful life of the motor
vehicle (as designated by the manufacturer), based on consideration of the use and aging of the
related parts and devices and resulting reduction of performance.
10. "Serious failure" of the partially automated driving system refers to each of the following:
A. Failure of a critical part or a device, such as the electronic control unit (ECU) that may affect
the safe operation of the partially automated driving system whose likelihood of occurrence is
extremely low.
B. Failure of 1 sensor occurring concurrently with another failure affecting the safe operation of
the partially automated driving system.
11. "Serious failure" of the motor vehicle refers to an electrical or mechanical failure of the motor
vehicle, including suspension of power supply, failure of the braking system, sudden reduction in
tire air pressure, etc., that may affect the driving control of the partially automated driving system
or the driver's driving control.

Requirements of Brake Hose (Article 112-2)

1. Hydraulic brake hoseA. Performance requirements1) Constriction requirements
Every inside diameter of any section of a hydraulic brake hose(except for that part of an end
fitting which does not contain hose) assembly shall be not less than 64 percent of the nominal
inside diameter of the brake hose2) Expansion requirements
The maximum expansion of a hydraulic brake hose assembly at 6,900 kPa, 10,300 kPa and
20,000 kPa shall not exceed the values specified in Table below.
Diameter ofHydraulicBrake HoseExpansion of free length brake hose(cm3/m)6,900kPa10,300kPa
20,000 kPaexpansion hoseLow expansionexpansion hoseLow expansionexpansion hose

4.002.00> 3mm, to5mm2.821.81
3.352.365.503.00> 5mm3.41
2.694.273.84--3) Burst strength requirements
The hydraulic brake hose assembly shall then withstand water pressure of 27,600 kPa for 2
minutes or more without rupture, and then shall not rupture at less than 49,000 kPa for a 3
mm, or smaller diameter hose, or at less than 34,500 kPa for a hose with a diameter larger
than 3 mm.4) Whip resistance requirements
A hydraulic brake hose assembly shall not rupture when run continuously on a flexing
machine for 35 hours5) Tensile strength requirements
A hydraulic brake hose assembly shall withstand a pull of 1,466 N without separation of the
hose from its end fittings during a slow pull test, and shall withstand a pull of 1,646 N without
separation of the hose from its end fittings during a fast pull test.
6) Water absorption and burst strength requirements
A hydraulic brake hose assembly, after immersion in water for 70 hours, shall withstand water
pressure of 27,600 kPa for 2 minutes or more, and then shall not rupture at less than 34,500
kPa.7) Water absorption and whip resistance requirements
A hydraulic brake hose assembly, after immersion in water for 70 hours, shall meet 4) whip
resistance requirements.8) Water absorption and tensile strength requirements
A hydraulic brake hose assembly, after immersion in water for 70 hours, shall meet 5) Tensile
strength requirements.9) Low-temperature resistance requirements
A hydraulic brake hose conditioned at a temperature between minus -48oC and – 45oC for
70 hours shall not show cracks visible without magnification when bent around a cylinder.
10) Brake compatibility requirements
Hydraulic brake hose assembly (except for brake hose assemblies designed for use with

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)
mineral or petroleum-based brake fluids) shall meet the requirement as followed after having
been subjected to a temperature of 120 degrees for 70 hours while filled with brake fluid.
a) Every inside diameter of any section of a hydraulic brake hose(except for that part of an
end fitting which does not contain hose) assembly shall be not less than 64 percent of the
nominal inside diameter of the brake hose.
b) The hydraulic brake hose assembly shall then withstand water pressure of 27,600kPa for
2 minutes or more without rupture, and then shall not rupture at less than 34,500kPa.
11) Ozone resistance requirements
a) A hydraulic brake hose shall not show cracks visible under 7-power magnification after
exposure to ozone for 70 hours at 40°C.
b) At the completion of 48 hours of dynamic ozone test, the brake hose shall not show cracks
which can be examined visually without magnification.
12) High temperature impulse test requirements
A brake hose assembly shall comply to the following requirement in high temperature impulse
test.
a) shall withstand pressure cycling for 150 cycles, at 146oC without leakage
b) shall not rupture during a 2 minute, 27,600 kPa hold test
c) shall not burst at a pressure less than 34,500 kPa.
13) End fitting corrosion test requirements
After 24 hours of exposure to salt spray, a hydraulic brake hose end fitting (except where
crimping or the application of labeling information has caused displacement of the protective
coating) shall show no base metal corrosion on the end fitting surface.

Note) brake hose assemblies designed for use with mineral or petroleum-based brake fluids
means the brake hose assemblies manufactured in accordance with ISO 6120.

B. Label requirements
1) Each hydraulic brake hose shall have at least two clearly identifiable stripes (These stripes may
be interrupted by the information of 2) or additional information at the manufacturer option) of
at least 1.5 mm in width placed on opposite sides of the brake hose parallel to its longitudinal
axis. However, hydraulic brake hose manufactured for use only in an assembly whose end
fittings prevent its installation in a twisted orientation in either side of the vehicle shall be
exempted.
2) Each hydraulic brake hose (except the case of a part of brake hose assembly) shall be labeled at
intervals of not more than 153mm, in letters and numerals at least 3 mm of high with the
following information.
a) A designation that identifies the manufacturer of the hose
b) The month, day, and year, or month and year, of manufacture, expressed in numerals
c) The nominal inside diameter of the hose
d) Either "HR" to indicate that the hose is regular expansion hose or "HL" to indicate that the
hose is low expansion hose.
3) Each hydraulic brake hose assembly shall be labeled by means of a band (The band may move
freely along the length of the assembly, as long as it is retained by the end fittings.) around the
brake hose assembly in letters and numerals at least 3 mm of high with a designation that
identifies the manufacturer of the hose assembly. Or it can be labeled by means that at least one
end fitting of a hydraulic brake hose assembly shall be labeled with a designation at least 1.5
mm of high that identifies manufacturer of the hose assembly.

cent at 200 °C- Thisrequirementdoes notapply tobrake lining
assemblies.- Buses with GVWnot exceeding5tons- Trucks (includingtrailers) with

Shear strength- Disc brake: 250N/cm2 or more- Onlyapplicable toReplacementBrake lining

The hardness figure for the frictionmaterial at the rubbing surface shall bethe mean value out of five samplelinings from different productionbatches by taking five measurements atdifferent places of each brake lining.


1. "Brake lining" means the friction material component with the shape and final dimension to be
fixed on to the shoe or backplate
2. "Shoe" means a component of a shoe assembly which carries the brake lining;
3. "Brake lining assembly" means a component of a friction brake which is pressed against a drum
or disc, respectively, to produce the friction force.
4. "Drum brake lining" means a brake lining for a drum brake.
5. "Pad assembly" means a brake lining assembly of a disc brake.
6. "Shoe assembly" means a brake lining assembly of a drum brake.
7. "Shear strength" means a sliding failure on a material along a plane parallel to the direction of
the force and the strength of a material against the type of yield or structural failure of the force.
8. "Compressibility" means the characteristics of a material for which volume is reduced when the
pressure is applied the material.
9. "Hardness" means the measure of how resistant solid matter is to various kinds of permanent
shape change when a compressive force is applied.
10. "Ambient temperature" means the natural temperature at ambient condition without heating
and cooling.

Wheel for Vehicle (Article 112-11)

1. Wheel performance requirementsA. Requirements per wheel materials1) Steel wheelsDisc wheel∙ Rotating bending test∙ Rolling test

2) Aluminium or Magnesium alloy wheelsOne piece wheels or Demountable rim wheels∙ Rotating bending test∙ Rolling test∙ Impact test

B. Performance requirements1) Rotating bending testRequirementsA) Acceptance limits
(1) Shaft displacement less than 10 per cent greater than the displacement
measured after approximately 10,000 cycles.
(2) There shall not exist a material separation with a propagation of more than
1 mm occurring after a test (defects caused by the production process and
vehicles with a steel wheel are not to be taken into account).
B) Allowable loss of tightening torqueinitially applied to the wheel fixingstuds and nuts30% or less

2) Rotating testRequirementsA) Acceptance limits(1) Air leakage is not accepted.
(2) There shall not exist a material separation with a propagation of more than
1 mm occurring after a test (defects caused by the production process are
not to be taken into account).B) Allowable loss of tightening torqueinitially applied to the wheel fixingstuds and nuts30% or less

3) Impact testVehicle type
PC, Trucks with GVW not exceeding 3.5 tons, special purpose vehicles
Acceptance
1) There shall not exist not any visible fracture penetrating through the wheel surface (initial crack
which is visible and occurred in the area of wheel disc of wheel assembly). However, Fractures
and indentations caused by the direct contact with the falling weight are acceptable.
2) Wheels with demountable rims shall not be dismantled
3) All tire air pressure shall not be leaked within one minute of completing the test.
4) In the case of wheels with demountable rims or other components that can be dismantled,
threaded fastenings that are close to the spoke (part made by connecting the outer rim of wheel
with steel wires in a radial shape) or ventilation holes shall not fail the wheel

1. In addition to the display details in the table above, the details of the name for the outline of the

B. display methods
1) Display details shall be displayed permanently in a conspicuous place.

(2) In the case of symmetry: Notate with Limwell character "S"
c) Wheel inset or outset(1) Inset: Mark with a positive number(2) Outset: Mark with a negative number

the nominal rim diameter may be displayed in the reverse order.
1) Name of the rim shape2) Components3) Nominal rim diameter

Note)
"Inset/outset" refers to the distance between the attachment face of the disc and the center line of

삭제함: No. 1499 (2025.05.30)[Table 32-2]

Requirements for Retro-Reflecting Band and Identification for the Standard Exemption
(Article 49 Paragraph 8, Articles 112-12 and 114-11)

1. Retro-reflecting bandA. Type
1) "Class C" means to apply the contour of vehicles in the form of strip (50 mm ≤ width ≤ 60
mm).
2) "Class D" means to apply the distinctive marking/graphics for a limited area less than 2 m2.
3) "Class E" means to apply the distinctive marking/graphics for a limited area of at least 2 m2.
4) "Class F" means to consist of red and white diagonal stripes each 100 mm wide sloping
outwards and downwards at 45°.B. Requirements for installation
1) The retro-reflecting band marking full contour shall be installed on the rear of vehicles
exceeding 2,100 mm in width of the following categories.
a) trucks/special purpose vehicles with GVW exceeding 7.5 tons (except incomplete
vehicles/tow vehicles)
b) trailers with GVW exceeding 3.5 tons (except incomplete vehicles)
2) The retro-reflecting band marking partial contour shall be installed on the side of vehicles
exceeding 6,000 mm in length of the following categories.
a) trucks/special purpose vehicles with GVW exceeding 7.5 tons (except incomplete
vehicles/tow vehicles)
b) trailers with GVW exceeding 3.5 tons (except incomplete vehicles)
3) A line marking may be installed instead of the mandatory contour marking if the structure of
the vehicle makes it impossible to install the full/partial contour marking pursuant to Item B'
1) or 2).
4) If the exterior surfaces of the bodywork are constituted of rigid and flexible material, this line
marking shall be installed on (a) rigid part(s) of the vehicle. The retro-reflecting band may be
installed on the flexible material.
5) If the structure of the vehicle makes it impossible to install the retro-reflecting band, at least
one of the plate with the retro-reflector of IVA type pursuant to Table 6-27 or with the retro-
reflecting band of Class C shall be installed per 1,500 mm of vehicle bodywork.
6) The retro-reflecting band may be installed optionally in the following cases.
a) to the rear and to the side
On all other categories of vehicles, except PCs, trailers with GVW of 0.75 tons or less, or
vehicles specified in Subparagraph 1 Item B' 1) or 2), partial or full contour marking may
be applied instead of mandatory line markings.
b) to the front
Line marking may be applied on trailers with GVW exceeding 0.75.
7) Arrangement
a) The retro-reflecting band shall be vertically and horizontally, and shall be installed as close
as practicable the contour of the outer shape of the vehicle.
b) It shall be installed as same as possible with the width and length of the vehicle
8) Positiona) Width
(1) The retro-reflecting band shall be as close as practicable to the edge of the vehicle
(2) The retro-reflecting band shall equate to at least 70 per cent of the overall width of the

more than 2,400 mm from the front end of the vehicle.
(a) Retro-reflector size minimum 25 cm2;
(b) One retro-reflector mounted not more than 600 mm from the front end of the vehicle;
(c) Additional retro-reflectors spaced not more than 600 mm apart;
(d) The distance between the last retro-reflector and the start of the retro-reflecting band
shall not exceed 600 mm;
(2) The retro-reflecting band shall equate to at least 70 per cent of the overall length of the
vehicle as following requirements. In this case, when calculating the length, any
horizontal overlap shall not be calculated in duplicate.
(a) For motor vehicles, length of vehicle or in the case of tow vehicle-trailer, length of
tow vehicle-trailer shall be included. However, the alternative retro-reflecting band
pursuant to the proviso of Item B' 8) b) (1) shall be installed not more than 2,400 mm
from the front end of vehicle

※ Maximum value of A: 2,400 mm
(b) For trailers, the overall length of the vehicle (excluding the drawbar)

(3) If the retro-reflecting band shall equate to at least 80 per cent of the overall length of
the cargo compartment, it is deemed to meet the requirements specified in (1) and (2).
c) Height
(1) The lower end of line markings and contour markings shall be installed as low as
practicable within the following range
(a) Not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,500 mm above the ground in the unloaded

(2) The upper end of retro-reflecting band shall be installed as high as practicable not more
than 400 mm9) Visibility
The retro-reflecting band shall be considered visible, if at least 70 per cent of the illuminating
surface of the installed marking is visible when viewed by an observer positioned at any point
within the observation planes defined below
a) For front and rear retro-reflecting band, the observation plane is perpendicular to the
longitudinal axis of the vehicle situated 25 m from the extreme end of the vehicle and
bounded by:
(1) Height: horizontal planes of 1 m or more and 3.0 m or less above the ground;
(2) Width: vertical planes which form an angle within 4° outwards from both side of vehicle
body parallel to the vehicle's outmost longitudinal plane


Front (trailers only)

b) For side retro-reflecting band, the observation plane is parallel to the longitudinal median
plane of the vehicles situated 25 m from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle and bounded
by:
(1) Height: horizontal planes of 1 m or more and 1.5 m or less above the ground;
(2) Width: vertical planes which form an angle within 4° outwards from both side of
front/rear outmost longitudinal plane parallel to the vehicle's side longitudinal plane

10) Orientation
a) For the side, it shall be installed as close as practicable to being parallel to the median
longitudinal plane of the vehicle considering the structure of the vehicle. If this is not
possible, it shall follow as close as practicable the contour of the outer shape of the vehicle.
b) For the front and rear, it shall be installed as close as practicable to being parallel to the
transverse plane of the vehicle. If this is not possible, it shall follow as close as practicable
the contour of the outer shape of the vehicle.

Method of Indicating Truck Load Capacity (Article 19 Paragraph 2)

1. The gross vehicle weight and the maximum load capacity shall be clearly marked on the back of a
truck in accordance with the standards of each of the following items.
A. The mark shall include a background and a text or just text
B. Size and character arrangement shall be as specified in the following.
1) If displayed in two lines, the cover size shall be 300 mm or more in width and 100 mm or
more in length, and the font size (height) shall be 30 mm or more.
2) If displayed in one line, the cover size shall be 300 mm or more in width and 40 mm or more
in length, and the font size (height) shall be 30 mm or more.
C. The background color and text of the display details shall be clearly contrasted.
D. Format of the cover (example)1) If displayed in two lines


2) If displayed in a single line respectively


2. The markings of the GVW and the maximum load capacity shall not be easily discolored or erased.
3. If the display method of Subparagraph 1 cannot be applied to the rear of the vehicle due to the
structure of the vehicle, it may be displayed in any of the following Items.
A. Displaying the GVW and the maximum loading capacity on the rear of the right side of the
vehicle [Example of Subparagraph 1 Item D 1)]
B. Displaying the maximum load capacity on the rear of the left side of the vehicle and the GVW
of the vehicle on the rear of the right side [Example of Subparagraph 1 Item D 2)]

2. Wiping system etc. may conform to the following requirements notwithstanding the requirements
specified in Article 51 and Article 109:
A. Each vehicle shall, as a minimum requirement, be fitted with wiping and washing systems.
B. Requirements for wiping system
1) The lowest frequency shall be at least 25 cycles per minute.
2) The wiping system shall wipe at least 90% of Area A as established by Table 30 Subparagraph
1.
3) The wiping system shall return to its original position when the operation is stopped.
4) The wiping system shall operate normally in the low ambient temperature condition.
C. Washing system
1) The washing system shall be able to inject a sufficient amount of washer fluid necessary to
wash at least 60% of Area A as established by Table 30 Subparagraph 1 when the wiping
system is activated for 10 cycles at a maximum speed.
2) Each connecting parts etc. shall operate normally in the load condition that the injection
nozzle is blocked.
3) The washing system shall operate normally in the low and high temperature conditions.

3. The headlamp may conform to the following requirements notwithstanding the requirements
specified in Article 48 Paragraph 3 and Article 106 Subparagraph 1.
A. If the headlamp meets the requirements for type and power specified in any one of Table 5-5 or
Table 5-10, it shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of Article 48 Paragraph 3.
B. If the headlamp meets the requirements for luminous intensity and brightness specified in any
one of Table 19, Table 19-7 or Table 19-8, it shall be considered as conforming to the
requirements of Article 106 Subparagraph 1.

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Driving Beam (Main Beam)
Headlamp for the Micro Vehicle (Article 38 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirementsA. Installation position1) Width
A) One driving beam headlamp may be installed on the upper, lower, left and right of another
front lamp. If another front lamp is installed in vertical direction, the reference point of the
driving beam headlamp shall be located within the median longitudinal plane of the micro
vehicle, and if installed in horizontal direction, the reference points of these lamps shall be
respectively symmetrical to the median longitudinal plane of the micro vehicle
B) One driving beam headlamp reciprocally incorporated with another front lamp shall be
located within the median longitudinal plane of the micro vehicle. However, if installed
with another front lamp at horizontal positions of the driving beam headlamps, the reference
points of these lamps shall be respectively symmetrical to the median longitudinal plane of
the micro vehicle
C) If two driving beam headlamps are installed, the reference point of these headlamps shall
be symmetrical to the median longitudinal plane of the micro vehicle
2) Length
Driving beam headlamp shall be positioned in the front of the micro vehicle, and it shall be
structured to not cause any distraction to the driver directly/indirectly with the reflecting part
of the vehicle or rearview mirror when switched ON
B. The outermost distance between driving beam headlamp and passing beam headlamp installed
separately shall be not more than 200 mm.
C. Observation angle
The visibility of the apparent surface for driving beam headlamp shall be ensured in any angle
of not more than 5 degrees upwards, downwards, leftwards, and rightwards
D. Orientation
The illuminating direction of the lamp shall be towards the front of the vehicle. However, it may
move according to the angle of the steering wheel
E. Operation requirements
1) The driving beam headlamp shall be structured to switch ON and OFF simultaneously
2) For changing over from the passing beam headlamp to the driving beam headlamp, the driving
beam headlamp shall switch ON simultaneously
3) For changing over from the driving beam headlamp to passing beam headlamp, the driving
beam headlamp shall switch OFF simultaneously
4) The passing beam headlamp may maintain to be switched ON with the driving beam headlamp
simultaneouslyF. Tell-tale
A non-flashing blue tell-tale to indicate the operation status of the lamp shall be installed.
G. Other requirements
The aggregate maximum intensity of all the driving beam headlamps which can be switched ON
shall not exceed 430,000 cd.

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Passing Beam Headlamp for the
Micro Vehicle (Article 38 Paragraph 2 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirementsA. Installation position1) Width
A) One independent passing beam headlamp may be installed on the upwards, downwards,
leftwards and rightwards of another front lamp. If another front lamp is installed in vertical
direction, the reference point of the passing beam headlamp shall be located within the
median longitudinal plane of the micro vehicle, and if installed in horizontal direction, the
reference points of these lamps shall be respectively symmetrical to the median longitudinal
plane of the micro vehicle
B) One passing beam headlamp reciprocally incorporated with another front lamp shall be
located within the median longitudinal plane of the micro vehicle. However, if installed
with another front lamp at horizontal positions of the passing beam headlamps, the
reference points of these lamps shall be respectively symmetrical to the median longitudinal
plane of the micro vehicle
C) If two passing beam headlamps are installed, the reference point of these headlamps shall
be symmetrical to the median longitudinal plane of the micro vehicle
2) Height
Not less than 500 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground
3) Length
Passing beam headlamp shall be positioned in the front of the micro vehicle, and it shall be
structured to not cause any distraction to the driver directly/indirectly with the reflecting part
of the vehicle or rearview mirror when switched ON
B. The outermost distance between driving beam headlamp and passing beam headlamp installed
separately shall be not more than 200 mm.
C. Observation angle
1) The visibility of apparent surface for passing beam headlamp shall be ensured in any angle of
not more than 15 degrees upwards and 10 degrees downwards
2) For the single lamp, the visibility of apparent surface for passing beam headlamp shall be
ensured in any angle of not more than 45 degrees leftwards and rightwards. If two lamps are
installed, the visibility shall be ensured in any angle of not more than 45 degrees outwards,
10 degrees inwardsD. Orientation
The illuminating direction of the lamp shall be towards the front of the vehicle. However, it may
move according to the angle of the steering wheel
E. Operation requirements
1) The passing beam headlamp shall be structured to switch ON and OFF simultaneously
2) For changing over from driving beam headlamp to the passing beam headlamp, the passing
beam shall switch ON simultaneously
3) For changing over from the passing beam headlamp to driving beam headlamp, the passing
beam headlamp shall switch OFF simultaneously. However, the passing beam headlamp may
maintain to be switched ON with the driving beam headlamp simultaneously
F. Tell-tale
If a tell-tale to indicate the operation status of the lamp is installed, a non-flashing green tell-tale

1) If the mounting height (the lower edge of the apparent surface) of the passing beam headlamp
is ≤ 0.8 meter, the initial aiming for vertical inclination of the cut-off shall be adjusted from -
1.0% to -1.5%
2) If the mounting height (the lower edge of the apparent surface) of the passing beam headlamp
is 0.8 meter < Mounting height ≤ 1.0 meter, the initial aiming for vertical inclination of the
cut-off shall be adjusted from -1.0% to -2.0%
3) If the mounting height (the lower edge of the apparent surface) of the passing beam headlamp
is > 1.0 meter, the initial aiming for vertical inclination of the cut-off shall be adjusted from -
1.5% to -2.0%

2. The luminous intensity shall meet the requirements under Subparagraph 2 in Table 5-18 or
Subparagraph 2 in Table 6-4

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Front Fog Lamp for the Micro
Vehicle (Article 38-2 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirementsA. Installation position1) General
A) One independent front fog lamp may be installed on the upwards, downwards, leftwards
and rightwards of another front lamp. If another front lamp is installed in vertical direction,
the reference point of the front fog lamp shall be located within the median longitudinal
plane of the micro vehicle, and if installed in horizontal direction, the reference points of
these lamps shall be respectively symmetrical to the median longitudinal plane of the micro
B) One front fog lamp reciprocally incorporated with another front lamp shall be located
within the median longitudinal plane of the micro vehicle. However, if installed with
another front lamp at horizontal positions of the headlamps, the reference points of these
lamps shall be respectively symmetrical to the median longitudinal plane of the micro
C) If two front fog lamps are installed, the reference point of these headlamps shall be
symmetrical to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle
D) If two front fog lamps are installed, the extreme outer edge on the apparent surface shall
not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
2) Height
A) Not less than 250 mm and not more than 800 mm above the ground
B) Front fog lamp shall not be higher than the highest point on the apparent surface of the
passing beam headlamp.3) Length
Front fog lamp shall be positioned in the front of the vehicle, and it shall be structured to not
cause any distraction to the driver directly/indirectly with the reflecting part of the vehicle or
rearview mirror when switched ON.B. Observation angle
1) The visibility of apparent surface for front fog lamp shall be ensured in any angle of not more
than 5 degrees upwards and 5 degrees downwards
2) For the single lamp, the visibility of apparent surface for front fog lamp shall be ensured not
more than 45 degrees leftwards and rightwards. If two lamps are installed, the visibility shall
be ensured in any angle of not more than 45 degrees outwards, 10 degrees inwards
C. Orientation
The illuminating direction of the lamp shall be towards the front of the vehicle. However, it may
move according to the angle of the steering wheel
D. Operation requirements
1) The front fog lamp shall be structured to switch ON and OFF simultaneously
2) The front fog lamp shall be structured to switch ON and OFF independently with the headlamp.
E. Tell-tale
A non-flashing green tell-tale to indicate the operation status of the front fog lamp shall be
installed.

2. The luminous intensity shall meet the requirements under Subparagraph 2 in Table 6-6

Requirements for Installation and Luminous Intensity of Rear Fog Lamp for the Micro
Vehicle (Article 38-2 Paragraph 2 Subparagraph 3)

1. Installation requirementsA. Installation position1) Width
A) If one rear fog lamp is installed, it shall be installed on the leftwards of median longitudinal
plane of the micro vehicle.
B) If two rear fog lamps are installed, they shall be installed symmetrical to the median
longitudinal plane of the micro vehicle.
2) Height
Not less than 250 mm and not more than 1000 mm above the ground. However, it may be not
more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any lamp(s)
B. Distance
The distance between apparent surface of the rear fog lamp and the stop lamp shall be not less
than 100 mm.C. Observation angle
1) The visibility of the apparent surface of the rear fog lamp shall be ensured in any angle of not
more than 5 degrees upwards and downwards
2) The visibility of the apparent surface of the rear fog lamp shall be ensured in any angle of not
more than 25 degrees leftward and rightward
D. Orientation
The illuminating direction shall be towards the rear of the vehicle.
E. Operation requirements
1) The rear fog lamp shall be structured to switch ON and OFF simultaneously
2) The rear fog lamp shall be structured to switch ON only if one or more of the driving beam
headlamp, passing beam headlamp, and front fog lamp switch ON
3) The rear fog lamp may be structured to switch OFF independently from other lamps.
4) The rear fog lamp shall automatically switch OFF in the following cases
A) If the front fog lamp switches OFFB) If the vehicle is stopped by the ignition key
5) If the rear fog lamp is switched OFF, it shall be switched ON automatically or independently
only if the manual control device is operated
F. Tell-tale
A non-flashing yellow tell-tale to indicate the operation state of the rear fog lamp shall be
installed

2. The luminous intensity shall meet the requirements under Subparagraph 2 in Table 6-7
